Practice on synthetic data Step 1. Spectrogram Step 2. Harmonics ↔ eRPM Step 3. Resonance Step 4. The filter, numerically
text: summary Betaflight and ArduPilot filters are signal processing, and tuning them by intuition means tuning blind. This module gives you the minimum theory without which you can't read a spectrum: sampling and the Nyquist frequency, aliasing why 10 kHz interference shows up as 2 kHz , what a spectrum and a spectrogram are, how to find motor harmonics and tell them apart from frame resonance, and what LPF and notch filters do in both the frequency domain attenuation and the time domain delay . With Python code and the link to eRPM. theory Sampling and Nyquist The gyro is sampled at a rate fs Betaflight: 8 kHz on F4/F7/H7 with MPU6000/ICM42688; ArduPilot: 1–4 kHz with batch logging up to 8 kHz . The Kotelnikov–Nyquist theorem: frequencies up to fs/2 can be represented without distortion. Anything above “folds over” aliasing : a signal of frequency f fs/2 appears at f − k·fs . Example: fs = 8 kHz, 10 kHz interference → seen as 2 kHz. A worse example: ArduPilot logs the IMU at 1 kHz while sampling internally at 4 kHz — a motor harmonic at 600 Hz ends up at 400 Hz in the log. Hence: spectra only from data with a known fs, batch logging for frequencies above 500 Hz, and the gyro's hardware anti-aliasing filter configurable on the ICM42688 is mandatory. Spectrum: what's on the axes The horizontal axis is frequency Hz , the vertical axis is power dB or deg²/s²/Hz . “A peak at 250 Hz, 20 dB above the noise” means 100 times more power than the background. The Welch spectrum averages over time — good for a steady segment hover . A spectrogram is the spectrum over time: color is power, the vertical axis is frequency; you can see the peaks move with throttle. Resolution: frequency versus time A spectrum over N samples resolves frequencies in steps of Δf = fs/N and describes a segment of duration N/fs. 8 kHz and N = 512: Δf ≈ 15.6 Hz over 64 ms; N = 4096: Δf ≈ 2 Hz, but over half a second — a peak that “moved” with throttle smears into a band. For hover you use long windows fine frequency resolution , for a spectrogram of maneuvers — short ones. The Hann window the default in scipy.signal.welch reduces the “leakage” of a strong peak's power into neighboring frequencies; without a window, a false “skirt” that looks like noise appears around the motor harmonic. Motor harmonics The motor fundamental is f₁ = RPM/60. Betaflight with ESC telemetry computes it from eRPM: RPM = eRPM / pole pairs ; a 2207 typically has 7 pairs 14 magnets → motor_poles = 14 . On the spectrogram these are sloped lines, repeated at 2f₁, 3f₁ blades, imbalance . Four motors give four close lines that merge into a band. Check: take the eRPM from the log at the same moment, compute f₁, compare with the peak position — a match within ±5 Hz confirms it's a motor. Resonance versus motors - A peak that is horizontal on the spectrogram independent of throttle is a resonance of the frame/mount/wires. Fixed with mechanics or a static notch. - A sloped peak tracks eRPM is a motor. Fixed with the RPM filter it tracks on its own or balancing. - A broad “cushion” at the bottom, 20–80 Hz, growing with sharp moves — propwash and aerodynamics; it can't be filtered without losing response; it's addressed with D-term and mechanics. What a filter does — two points of view A 1st-order LPF PT1 with cutoff frequency fc: in the frequency domain −3 dB at fc, then −20 dB/decade ×10 in frequency = ×0.1 in amplitude . In the time domain — delay : the group delay at low frequencies ≈ 1/ 2π·fc ; a 100 Hz PT1 delays the useful signal by ~1.6 ms. PT2/PT3 cascades cut steeper −40/−60 dB/decade but delay more. Betaflight: gyro_lpf1_static_hz , dterm_lpf1_static_hz , throttle-based dynamic LPF; ArduPilot: INS_GYRO_FILTER , ATC_RAT_ _FLTD/FLTE/FLTT . A notch centered at fₙ with a width Q : a deep dip only around fₙ, little delay outside the band. Narrow high Q — precise, but misses when RPM changes; wide — more robust, but delays more. The RPM notch is narrow because it knows the frequency; the dynamic notch searches for the peak itself Betaflight dyn_notch_count/q/min_hz/max_hz ; ArduPilot's harmonic notch INS_HNTCH_ with tracking by throttle, RPM or FFT . The price of any filter is delay; the price of delay is stability margin the “Control Theory” module . The goal of filter tuning: minimum delay with motor noise below the level that heats the motors D-term noise . Ballpark numbers 5" 6S hover: f₁ ≈ 250–350 Hz, peaks 20–30 dB above the background before filtering, ≤ 5 dB after the RPM notch. The delay of the gyro LPF + D LPF chain in a good 5" tune is 1–2 ms; with “heavy” filtering it's 4–6 ms, and that's already noticeable in bounce-back. {{diagram:peak-diagnosis How to identify a peak in the gyro spectrum by how it behaves with throttle, and how to deal with it.}} {{diagram:chart-gyro-spectrum A model gyro spectrum: at the bottom, the vehicle's motion the useful signal , motor harmonic peaks moving with throttle , a narrow frame resonance peak staying put and the noise floor.}} {{diagram:chart-aliasing Aliasing at 1 kHz sampling: everything above 500 Hz “folds” into the 0–500 Hz band — a 700 Hz vibration looks like 300 Hz in the data. That's why the anti-aliasing filter must come before sampling, not after.}} practice Step 0. Practice on synthetic data Before trusting your own log analysis, check it on a signal where the answer is known: python import numpy as np from scipy import signal fs = 8000; t = np.arange 0, 10, 1 / fs rpm = np.interp t, 0, 5, 10 , 12000, 21000, 12000 throttle up and down phase = 2 np.pi np.cumsum rpm / 60 / fs motor fundamental follows rpm x = 2.0 np.sin phase + 0.8 np.sin 2 phase motor 1x and 2x + 1.0 np.sin 2 np.pi 180 t frame resonance, fixed + np.random.default_rng 0 .normal 0, 0.5, t.size noise floor f, P = signal.welch x : 2 fs , fs, nperseg=2048 first 2 s: near-steady print "peaks Hz :", sorted int v for v in f signal.find_peaks 10 np.log10 P , prominence=10 0 f2, t2, S = signal.spectrogram x, fs, nperseg=512, noverlap=384 Expected:

summary: Blackbox is the flight data recording system in Betaflight that captures the controller state on every control loop cycle (up to 8 kHz). The log contains the gyro, accelerometer, stick signals, PID controller activity, motor outputs and filter parameters. This article gives you a complete understand
headings: Purpose and architecture of Blackbox What exactly is logged Log format and storage devices How settings affect log quality Physical meaning of the noise spectrum Logging parameters The fields you need most often Reading a log in 5 minutes Worked example: “one motor runs hotter” Preparing hardware and software Recording a log and maneuvers Working with Blackbox Explorer PIDscope (formerly PIDtoolbox) Step-by-step filter tuning Automatic log check
text: summary Blackbox is the flight data recording system in Betaflight that captures the controller state on every control loop cycle up to 8 kHz . The log contains the gyro, accelerometer, stick signals, PID controller activity, motor outputs and filter parameters. This article gives you a complete understanding of how to set up logging, interpret the graphs and use the tools Blackbox Explorer, PIDscope for troubleshooting and tuning. After studying it, you'll be able to identify your drone's noise structure, estimate filter latency, and tune PIDs and filters based on objective data rather than random trial and error. theory Purpose and architecture of Blackbox Blackbox records the internal state of the flight controller at the highest possible rate, to enable offline simulation, debugging and analysis of control algorithms using real flight data. The log is built from frames of several types: - I-frames intra — full frames, independently decodable. - P-frames inter — delta frames, using prediction. - G/H frames — for GPS data. - S frames slow — rarely changing states. - E frames event — state transitions. Compression uses predictors and variable-length encoding, which lets you store a large amount of data at a moderate data rate. What exactly is logged Blackbox records: - time, - P/I/D values and the summed output, - setpoint sticks , - gyro and accelerometer data, - voltage/current, RSSI, - ESC commands, - GPS frames if present . Log format and storage devices Logging can go to: - onboard flash usually 2–16 MB , - an SD card preferred for long sessions , - an external logger over UART. For an SD card, FAT32 and a card with low write latency are recommended. How settings affect log quality - 1 kHz — basic PID analysis; - 2 kHz or 1.6 kHz for BMI270 — detailed noise/filter analysis. If the looptime is small high PID rate , you may need to raise the baud rate or lower the logging rate, otherwise you can get dropped frames. Physical meaning of the noise spectrum - <20 Hz — useful dynamics; - 20–100 Hz — vibration/propwash/PID problems; - 100–250 Hz — frame resonances/play; - 250 Hz — motor/prop noise and harmonics. The goal of filtering is to suppress high-frequency noise without adding extra latency in the useful range. Logging parameters blackbox_device SPIFLASH / SDCARD / SERIAL , blackbox_sample_rate 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, … of the PID rate: with 8 kHz PID and 1/4 — a 2 kHz log , blackbox_mode NORMAL — on arm; MOTOR_TEST; ALWAYS — on the ground too: for measuring gyro noise/bias , blackbox_high_resolution more precise gyro/setpoint , blackbox_disable_ disable field groups: acc , rc , gyrounfilt , rpm , gps … — saves bandwidth , debug_mode which 8 debug values to log: GYRO_SCALED — raw gyro before the filters 4.5 only; removed in 2025.12, use the gyroUnfilt field , RPM_FILTER , D_LPF , DSHOT_RPM_TELEMETRY , FEEDFORWARD , GPS_RESCUE_ , RTH … . Data rate: 2 kHz with the full set of fields is around 60–100 KB/s → 16 MB of flash is enough for 3–4 minutes; SD — hours. An external logger is the Blackbox function on a UART in the Ports tab serial <id 128 … with the blackbox baud ; there are no separate blackbox_uart / blackbox_baud settings in 4.5 and 2025.12. {{diagram:chart-blackbox-flash-minutes При 60–100 КБ/с 2 кГц, все поля 16 МБ flash хватает на 2.7–4.6 минуты, 8 МБ при 80 КБ/с — на 102 с, 2 МБ — на 26 с; для длинных сессий нужна SD.}} The fields you need most often gyroADC 0..2 after the filters , gyroUnfilt 0..2 before, if the field is enabled , setpoint 0..3 , rcCommand 0..3 , axisP/I/D/F 0..2 , motor 0..3 , eRPM 0..3 , vbatLatest , amperageLatest , rssi , debug 0..7 , flightModeFlags , stateFlags , failsafePhase ; events E-frames : arm/disarm, mode change, failsafe. The log header contains about 190 key parameters PIDs, rates, filters, motors , but not the whole diff : there's no aux , serial , OSD, failsafe — a full backup only via diff all . Reading a log in 5 minutes 1. Blackbox Explorer: overview — any gaps dropped frames , vbat under load, rssi/LQ . 2. Gyro spectrogram before/after — motors, resonances the “Signals and spectra” module . 3. Overlay setpoint on gyro for roll — overshoot/bounce-back by eye; axisD — noise. 4. motor 0..3 — symmetry one higher than the others = imbalance/mechanical issue , saturation at 100%. 5. Numbers — via Python data-python , into a decision table. Worked example: “one motor runs hotter” In the log, motor 2 at hover is 8% higher than the others and eRPM 2 is lower — the motor is producing less thrust: a damaged prop, a bearing or a twisted frame; the noise in gyroUnfilt at 2×RPM of that motor is higher. The fix is mechanical, not PID. Without a log this would have looked like “need to bump up D”. {{diagram:blackbox-chain Where in the flight controller loop the main Blackbox fields come from and how the log gets into the analysis tools.}} practice Preparing hardware and software Hardware: - an FC with flash or an SD slot, - ESCs with Bidirectional DShot BLHeli_32/Bluejay , - a high-quality, mechanically stiff build. Setup: - enable BLACKBOX , - set the logging rate usually 2 kHz , - for noise analysis use debug_mode = GYRO_SCALED , - enable the RPM filter. Recording a log and maneuvers Blackbox usually starts on arm and stops on disarm. For a good analysis, fly: - hover and straight-and-level flight, - throttle sweep 20% - 100% , - sharp rolls/flips, - throttle pumps, - sharp turns propwash check . Working with Blackbox Explorer 1. Download the .bbl Mass Storage Mode . 2. Open the log in Blackbox Explorer. 3. Check the header i — it has all the firmware parameters. 4. For analysis, select Gyro , Setpoint , P/I/D , Motor , Debug . 5. Use I/O to select sections of equal length. PIDscope formerly PIDtoolbox Since 2024 PIDtoolbox has been distributed as a paid subscription product; its open continuation is PIDscope GPL-3.0, runs in the free GNU Octave, supports Betaflight 4.x and 2025.12 logs . It's useful for: - estimating filter latency, - comparing spectra in

Without them the D-term turns noise into motor jitter and heat; with too much, every filter adds delay, the aircraft bec
headings: What exactly we filter and why Filter types and the price of each The gyro chain in Betaflight 4.5 (parameters; the actual order in `filterGyro()`: LPF2 → RPM → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch) The D-term chain Sliders and when they're enough “Filtered enough” criteria What filters don't cure Step 0. Preparation Step 1. Baseline Step 2. Reading the spectrum Step 3. Decisions from the table Step 4. Locking it in Lab Automatic log check
text: summary Filters sit between the gyro and the PID controller and decide what the controller “sees”: the useful movement of the frame, or motor noise, resonances and vibration on top of it. Without them the D-term turns noise into motor jitter and heat; with too much, every filter adds delay, the aircraft becomes “mushy” and the stability margin melts away. This module walks through the Betaflight 4.5 filter chain in the order the code applies it LPF2 when downsampling → RPM notch → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch for the gyro; notch → LPF1 → LPF2 for the D-term , explains each parameter with its default values, gives a method for tuning from the Blackbox spectrum with concrete “good enough” criteria, and shows where filters do not help mechanics, propwash . The interactive part: the chain's frequency response and group delay. theory What exactly we filter and why The gyro signal = frame movement 0–100 Hz, useful + noise. Noise sources and where they sit in the spectrum more in the “Frame and vibration” and “Signals and spectra” modules : {{diagram:fc-signal-path Where the filters sit in the chain: between the gyro and the PID; whatever they let through ends up in the D-term and on the motors.}} Source Frequency on a 5" 6S Look on the spectrogram Cure --- --- --- --- Motor fundamental imbalance 250–450 Hz at hover, up to 700+ at throttle a slanted line that follows throttle RPM filter 2nd, 3rd harmonics blades, aerodynamics ×2, ×3 parallel lines RPM filter harmonics Frame / FC mount resonance 100–300 Hz a horizontal line mechanics, dynamic notch, static notch Broadband noise play, bad bearings, electrical the whole range a “cushion” mechanics, LPF Propwash 20–80 Hz bursts during sharp moves not filters: D-term, mechanics, props The main victim of noise is the D-term : the derivative amplifies the signal in proportion to frequency 40 times more at 400 Hz than at 10 Hz , so the motors “hum” and heat up, while P and I barely notice the noise. Hence two chains: a gentle one for the gyro it feeds all three terms and a harsher one for D. Filter types and the price of each - PT1 — a first-order filter: −3 dB at the cutoff frequency fc, then −20 dB/decade; group delay at low frequencies ≈ 1/ 2π·fc PT1 100 Hz → 1.6 ms; 250 Hz → 0.64 ms . The “cheapest” in delay. - PT2, PT3 — cascades of PT1: −40/−60 dB/decade, delay ×1.6/×2.2 relative to a PT1 with the same fc. Used when you need to cut noise above the band sharply at moderate delay the D-term LPF defaults to PT1 in 4.5; the type is changed with _lpf1_type / _lpf2_type : PT1, BIQUAD, PT2, PT3 . - BIQUAD 2nd order, Butterworth — steeper than PT1, delay between PT1 and PT2. - Notch — a dip around the center frequency with a width set by Q the higher Q, the narrower ; outside the band the delay is almost zero. That's why narrowband motor noise is properly cut with notches rather than by lowering the LPF. The price of filtering is delay; the price of delay is phase margin the “Control theory” module : with a total gyro+D chain delay of about 1–2 ms, a good 5" tune holds P/D 30–50% higher than with 4–6 ms. {{widget:filter-response}} The gyro chain in Betaflight 4.5 parameters; the actual order in filterGyro : LPF2 → RPM → static notches → LPF1 → dynamic notch 1. RPM filter rpm_filter_harmonics = 3 , rpm_filter_q = 500 , rpm_filter_min_hz = 100 , rpm_filter_fade_range_hz = 50 , rpm_filter_lpf_hz = 150 , rpm_filter_weights = 100,100,100 — one notch per harmonic per motor 3 harmonics × 4 motors = 12 notches , with the center taken from eRPM via bidirectional DShot dshot_bidir = ON , motor_poles = 14 for a 2207/2306 with 14 magnets . Q = 500 means a width of ≈ f/5: narrow and precise. min_hz — below this frequency no notch is placed so the useful signal isn't cut at low throttle , fade_range_hz — a smooth fade-in above min_hz. There's a separate module, “RPM filter”. 2. Dynamic notch dyn_notch_count = 3 , dyn_notch_q = 300 , dyn_notch_min_hz = 100 , dyn_notch_max_hz = 600 : an FFT on the gyro finds the strongest peaks in the min..max range and puts notches on them. It catches what the RPM filter doesn't know about — frame resonances. With the RPM filter, count = 1–2 and q = 300–500 is enough; without the RPM filter — count = 4–5 , q = 250–300 wider . 3. LPF1 — dynamic by default: the cutoff slides with throttle from gyro_lpf1_dyn_min_hz = 250 to gyro_lpf1_dyn_max_hz = 500 gyro_lpf1_dyn_expo sets the curve ; with gyro_lpf1_static_hz ≠ 0 and dyn_min = 0 — static. Type gyro_lpf1_type = PT1 . 4. LPF2 — static gyro_lpf2_static_hz = 500 , PT1: a safety anti-aliasing cutoff. Static notches gyro_notch1_hz/cutoff , gyro_notch2_hz/cutoff 0 = off — for one known resonance you don't want to hand to the dynamic notch. Plus the gyro's hardware filter in the chip gyro_hardware_lpf = NORMAL — on an ICM42688 this is the DLPF, and it already sits in the signal path before all the software filters. The D-term chain dterm_lpf1_ — dynamic by default dterm_lpf1_dyn_min_hz = 75 , dterm_lpf1_dyn_max_hz = 150 , dterm_lpf1_type = PT1 , dterm_notch_hz/cutoff 0 = off , dterm_lpf2_static_hz = 150 PT1 . Two to three times lower than the gyro ones, because D amplifies high frequencies. It's the D filters that contribute most of the chain's delay and are the first to “blur” the response. Sliders and when they're enough simplified_gyro_filter = ON , simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier = 100 and simplified_dterm_filter_multiplier = 100 scale all the cutoff frequencies at once: 100 = defaults, 150 = 50% higher less filtering, less delay , 50 = half. For a clean 5" with the RPM filter, the practice is: gyro 100–150, D-term 100–130. text: summary An ESC is a separate computer with its own firmware, and that firmware decides the RPM filter, how the motors sound, how hot they run and even whether a motor will start after a crash. The “Motors and ESC” module explained what an ESC does; here you'll learn which firmware goes on which hardware, what bidirectional DShot and EDT are, which ESC settings actually change how it flies PWM frequency, timing, demagnetization, startup power , how to flash through the flight controller in Betaflight and ArduPilot, and how not to turn a 4-in-1 into a brick. theory Who's who Firmware Hardware Status What matters --- --- --- --- BLHeli_S 8-bit EFM8 BB1/BB2/BB21 factory firmware on cheap ESCs, no longer developed no bidirectional DShot in its original form Bluejay 8-bit EFM8 BB21 and BB51 BB1/BB10 only up to version 0.18.1 open source, actively developed bidirectional DShot, EDT, PWM frequency 24/48/96 kHz, startup melodies BLHeli_32 32-bit ARM closed source; development and support ended in 2024 it works, but there will be no updates or new configurator AM32 32-bit ARM STM32F051, G071, AT32F421, GD32, etc. open source, actively developed a replacement for BLHeli_32 where a target exists for the board The firmware name on the box tells you about the ESC's microcontroller: “BLHeli_S” means 8-bit, “BLHeli_32” or “AM32” means ARM. Bidirectional DShot and EDT - DShot is a digital command protocol from the flight controller to the ESC: DShot300/600 is the speed in kbit/s; no throttle range calibration, with a checksum. - Bidirectional DShot bidir : over the same wire, the ESC replies with electrical RPM eRPM . This is the input for the Betaflight RPM filter and the harmonic notch in ArduPilot. Mechanical RPM = eRPM / number of poles / 2 , so the motor's pole count usually 14 for 22xx–28xx must be set in the flight controller. - EDT Extended DShot Telemetry adds the ESC's temperature, voltage, current and status to the same replies, with no separate telemetry wire. Supported by Bluejay and AM32; you enable it in the flight controller. Settings that change how it flies - PWM frequency. Higher 48–96 kHz is quieter and smoother at low throttle, with better response; lower 24 kHz means less switching loss and heat, and more “thrust per amp” on heavy aircraft. For 5" freestyle 48 kHz is typical, for big props 24. - Timing advance . The commutation advance angle. Higher means more RPM and current, and heat; lower is more efficient, but risks losing sync on sharp throttle changes. Auto/medium is a sensible start. - Demagnetization demag compensation . Protection against losing sync on sharp throttle changes with big motors. Desyncs the motor twitches or stops in flight are treated first by raising the compensation. - Startup power startup/rampup power . Too high and the windings burn when the motor is jammed; too low and a heavy motor won't start. - Rotation direction. Changed in the ESC firmware or with a DShot command from the flight controller; no need to resolder wires. - Melodies and beacon. The “lost drone” sound after a crash is a useful feature, not a toy. How to flash - Through the flight controller passthrough . The flight controller routes the ESC signal wire through to the computer. Betaflight: connect USB, close the Configurator the port is busy , open ESC Configurator esc-configurator.com in Chrome for BLHeli_S/Bluejay and AM32; for BLHeli_32 use BLHeliSuite32 the archived version . ArduPilot: SERVO_BLH_AUTO = 1 for the motors on planes, SERVO_BLH_MASK , DShot protocol, disconnect the GCS, keep USB, and in the configurator choose the “BLHeli32/AM32 Bootloader Betaflight/Cleanflight ” interface. IOMCU outputs MAIN don't support passthrough; you need the FMU/AUX outputs. - The target rule. The firmware is chosen for the specific ESC board layout/target . A wrong target ranges from misbehavior to burned MOSFETs. The configurator usually shows the current layout; flash only a matching one. - Before flashing : remove the props, save the current settings a screenshot or a file , flash one ESC at a time if in doubt, use a protected battery smoke stopper . Flight controller: what to enable - Betaflight: set motor_pwm_protocol = DSHOT600 or 300 , set dshot_bidir = ON , set motor_poles = 14 ; to check, the Motors tab shows RPM, DShot errors ≈ 0%. - ArduPilot: MOT_PWM_TYPE set to DShot300/600, SERVO_BLH_BDMASK is the mask of outputs with bidirectional DShot, SERVO_BLH_POLES is the pole count; ESC telemetry shows up in the log ESC and is used by the harmonic notch INS_HNTCH_MODE = 3 , driven by ESC telemetry . {{diagram:esc-firmware-choice Choosing ESC firmware: an 8-bit ESC on BB21/BB51 gets Bluejay instead of BLHeli_S, a 32-bit one gets AM32 if a target exists, a working BLHeli_32 can stay, and without a target don't flash.}} practice Step 1. Inventory Read each ESC through passthrough: firmware and version, layout/target, PWM frequency, timing, direction. Write the table into the aircraft's passport. Step 2. Bidir DShot and RPM If the firmware supports it, enable bidirectional DShot and the pole count in the flight controller. Betaflight: the Motors tab, with the motors spinning no props , shows RPM and the error percentage. Write down eRPM and mechanical RPM at 10% throttle and check the conversion formula with your pole count. Step 3. Flashing if there's a benefit Only if you need bidir DShot or EDT that you don't have: BLHeli_S → Bluejay only on BB21/BB51 MCUs or BLHeli_32 → AM32 if a target exists. Save the settings first; take the target from the layout you read. After flashing, restore the direction and check the motor order and direction. Step 4. PWM frequency: comparison in flight Don't measure without props: you need a real operating mode. With props, tethered or in flight: two flights with the same pack at 24 and 48 kHz Bluejay/AM32 . text: summary A breakdown of a real case: a 10-inch quadcopter's motors “whistle” and it flies unevenly. The cause turned out to be not the PID but a single line of config: the lower bound of the RPM filter was above the motors' rotation frequency, and for most of the flight the filter simply wasn't working. This module teaches you to check whether the RPM filter covers the real RPM range using Blackbox data, not by eye. theory How the RPM filter works With bidirectional DShot, each ESC reports its motor's eRPM to the flight controller. Betaflight converts eRPM into RPM using motor_poles and places narrow notch filters exactly on each motor's rotation frequency and its harmonics. By default that's 12 notch filters per axis 4 motors × 3 harmonics on roll, pitch and yaw. The notch “tracks” the RPM in real time, so it cuts motor noise with almost no extra delay. Why big props have different math The frequency of a motor's fundamental harmonic: f = RPM / 60 . A five-inch in hover spins at tens of thousands of RPM, and the fundamental sits in the hundreds of hertz. A 10-inch has low-speed motors low KV, heavy props , and the fundamental in hover can drop to 50–100 Hz. The rpm_filter_min_hz parameter sets the lower bound: the notch doesn't go below it. If the bound is above the motor's real frequency, the filter sits “off target” from the noise. That's exactly what happened in the case below. Hardware requirements - An ESC with DShot telemetry support: BLHeli_32 from 32.7.0, AM32, Bluejay BLHeli_S or JESC. - dshot_bidir = ON and a correct motor_poles the number of magnets in the bell, not the number of stator teeth . - Telemetry errors in the Motors tab no higher than 1%. If an ESC doesn't report valid telemetry, Betaflight blocks arming with the DSHOT_TELEM flag in the OSD/ status . Case: viking10, iFlight Blitz F722, 10" The pilot's complaint: the motors whistle, the flight is uneven. A spectrum analysis of the log Python, orangebox + scipy showed: - motor fundamental: p5 = 48 Hz, median 91 Hz, p95 = 165 Hz; - the config had rpm_filter_min_hz = 100 — meaning for more than half the flight the motor spun below the bound and the RPM filter didn't see it; - in the 80–150 Hz band the filtered gyro was only ~2 dB quieter than raw, D-term +44.5 dB — that's the “whistle”; - static notches sat at 68 Hz, while the motors in hover ran at 84–96 Hz — the filters were cutting empty air. The fix: rpm_filter_min_hz = 50 , static notches removed, gyro LPF returned to default. After the next flight, in the same 80–150 Hz band: filtered gyro −9.5 dB was +24.4 , D-term −1.0 dB was +44.5 , motor command noise dropped from ~450 to ~20 arbitrary units. eRPM errors — 0%. The takeaway: before touching the PID, check that the filters sit where the noise actually lives. Parameters 4.5 and what they mean Parameter Default Meaning --- --- --- dshot_bidir OFF → ON eRPM telemetry over the same DShot line motor_poles 14 number of magnets; eRPM/ poles/2 = RPM rpm_filter_harmonics 3 harmonics 1×, 2×, 3× of the motor frequency rpm_filter_weights 100,100,100 “weight” depth of each harmonic in %; the 2nd and 3rd can often be weakened to 50–80 on clean aircraft → less delay rpm_filter_q 500 Q factor: notch width ≈ f/ Q/100 ; 500 → f/5 rpm_filter_min_hz 100 below it no notch is placed protects the useful band ; for 10" — 50 rpm_filter_fade_range_hz 50 smooth fade-in of the notch above min_hz rpm_filter_lpf_hz 150 filter on the eRPM estimate itself smoothing telemetry jumps The effect can only be measured with the spectrum: before/after attenuation of 20–30 dB in the harmonic band is normal; less than 10 dB — something is wrong polarity/poles/E% . Why the RPM filter lets you raise D D noise ∝ frequency × gyro noise amplitude. Once the narrow motor peaks are removed, you can raise the D-LPF frequencies less delay and D more damping at the same motor temperature — that's what gave the jump in flight quality in 4.1+, not “new PIDs.” Worked example: a 7" with Bluejay BLHeli_S ESC → flash Bluejay 48 kHz , dshot_bidir = ON , motor_poles = 14 2806.5 , Motors tab: RPM on all four, E = 0%; rpm_filter_min_hz = 70 hover ~110–130 Hz on a 7" , rpm_filter_harmonics = 3 , weights 100/80/60; spectrum: 125 Hz peak −27 dB; dyn_notch_count 1 for the frame; after that — simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier 120, D-term 110; bounce-back 14 → 9%, motors warm. {{diagram:rpm-filter-chain RPM filter: eRPM from the ESC is converted into the motor frequency and its harmonics, a notch is placed on each; rpm_filter_min_hz limits it from below.}} {{diagram:chart-rpm-harmonics Why the viking10 case broke: the motor fundamental was 48–165 Hz median 91 Hz, hover 84–96 Hz, i.e. ~5000–5800 RPM , and the 100 Hz lower bound kept the notch above the noise for more than half the flight. A 50 Hz bound puts the filter back on the harmonic.}} {{widget:rpm-harmonics}} practice Step 1. Enable and check telemetry Connect the battery without it the Motors tab will show E: 100% and run in the CLI: set dshot_bidir = ON set motor_poles = 14 save After the reboot, always read the values back. Betaflight can silently correct an incompatible combination for example, the DShot protocol on a particular board : get dshot_bidir get motor_pwm_protocol status The dshot_telemetry_info command should show telemetry for all motors with near-zero errors status doesn't print it . Step 2. Find the real range of motor frequencies 1. Enable Blackbox with a logging rate of at least 1 kHz and do a normal flight with hovering. 2. In Blackbox Explorer or PID Toolbox look at the eRPM field or the gyro spectrum and find the minimum frequency in hover and on throttle cuts. 3. The raw eRPM n field blackbox_decode/orangebox is stored in units of 100 eRPM: Hz = eRPM × 100 / motor_poles / 2 / 60 ; Blackbox Explorer shows rpm and Hz on its own. Step 3. Adjust the lower bound Set rpm_filter_min_hz below the motor's minimum operating frequency, with margin: get rpm_filter set rpm_filter_min_hz = 50 save For a 5" the de

text: summary PID tuning without theory is trial and error. This module explains, at a level sufficient for an engineer, what closed-loop stability is, why delay eats the phase margin and leads to oscillations at high P, how the step response relates to poles and damping and why bounce-back is an underdamped pole , and why the autopilot builds an angle → angular rate cascade with an inner loop several times faster than the outer one. The formulas are kept to a minimum, and each one is tied to what you see in the PID simulator and in the log. theory Plant, controller, loop The plant is the vehicle: the input is the motor command, the output is the angular rate. The controller is the PID: the input is the error setpoint − gyro , the output is the command. The closed loop: the output affects the input through the measurement. The whole point of the theory is to predict the behavior of the loop without closing it. A first-approximation model of one axis The motor torque creates angular acceleration: J·ω̇ = M − b·ω, where J is the moment of inertia and b is the aerodynamic damping. The transfer function from torque to ω is a first-order lag 1/ J·s + b — a “leaky integrator”: ω grows as long as torque is applied. Plus the delays : the motor current/RPM, τ ≈ 10–30 ms for a 5" , the gyro and D filters 1–5 ms , the loop period and the ESC protocol 0.1–0.5 ms . The total pure delay T_d is the main enemy. Stability and phase margin A loop with a P controller: at low P it's sluggish, at high P it oscillates, at even higher P the oscillations diverge. The boundary is where the loop gain equals 1 at the frequency where the phase shift reaches −180°. A pure delay T_d gives a phase shift of −360°·f·T_d: at 50 Hz with T_d = 5 ms that's −90°, and the plant pole adds another −90° — and there's your −180°. Therefore: - Phase margin — how many degrees remain to −180° at the frequency where the gain = 1. 45–60° is a good tune small overshoot ; 20–30° — ringing and bounce-back; 0 — sustained oscillations. - The delay T_d eats the margin linearly with frequency: the faster you want the loop higher P , the more you lose. Doubling the delay at the same P loses ~half the margin. - Hence the limit “P no higher than the delay allows.” Reducing the delay higher filter cutoffs, an RPM notch instead of a wide LPF, a fast ESC protocol, light props is the only way to raise P without oscillations. Step response, poles, damping A second-order closed loop is described by its natural frequency ωₙ and damping ζ: - ζ 1 — overdamped, slow; - ζ ≈ 0.7 — fast with ~5% overshoot; this is the goal; - ζ = 0.4 — ~25% overshoot, ringing; - ζ → 0 — oscillations. Overshoot ≈ exp −π·ζ/√ 1−ζ² : 0.7 → 4.6%, 0.5 → 16%, 0.3 → 37%. Settling time ≈ 4/ ζ·ωₙ . Bounce-back after the stick stops is the same underdamped pole, just excited by a “downward” step: large bounce-back = low ζ = either too little D, or too much P/delay. The D-term increases the damping ζ — that's why “lots of D” removes the bounce, but D amplifies noise ∝ frequency, and the D filters add delay, which again reduces the margin. That's the tuning trade-off. I-term: steady-state error and windup I removes steady-state error wind, asymmetry . It pays in phase: an integrator gives −90° at low frequencies, so too much I means slow oscillations 0.5–3 Hz, “wandering” . Windup is I accumulating while the outputs are saturated stick at the endpoint, motors at the ceiling : firmware limits it iterm_limit , iterm_relax , in ArduPilot ATC_RAT_ _IMAX . Feedforward FF applies a command proportional to the derivative of the setpoint, bypassing the error: the output starts moving before the error has built up. It doesn't affect stability it's outside the loop , but too much of it gives overshoot on sharp stick moves. Good FF means low response delay at the same P. Cascade: angle → rate The outer loop angle computes the desired angular rate from the angle error; the inner loop rate tracks it. The rule: the inner loop must be 3–10 times faster than the outer one in bandwidth , otherwise the outer loop “sees” the dynamics of the inner one and the cascade oscillates. In ArduPilot: ATC_ANG_RLL_P outer, ~4.5–12 and ATC_RAT_RLL_P/I/D inner ; on top of that, the position loop PSC_ is slower still. In Betaflight angle mode: angle_p_gain default 50 on top of the rate PID. In PX4: MC_ROLL_P → MC_ROLLRATE_P/I/D . Autotune tunes the inner loop first, then the outer one — for the same reason. What this means for tuning 1. First reduce the delay mechanics, filters , then raise P. 2. P — until ringing starts, then back off by 20–30% phase margin . 3. D — until bounce-back is < 10% and the motors don't heat up. 4. I — until the drift disappears, without “wandering.” 5. The outer loop — after the inner one. Where the total delay T_d comes from and which link weighs the most — compute it for your own setup: {{widget:link-latency}} {{diagram:angle-rate-cascade The “angle → angular rate” cascade: the outer P on angle sets the setpoint for the inner PID on the gyro.}} {{diagram:chart-step-responses Step response of a second-order system: ζ = 0.7 gives ~5 % overshoot and fast settling — the target for the rate loop; ζ = 0.3 rings, ζ = 1 is sluggish.}} practice Step 1. Simulator: the P limit at two delays In the interactive PID simulator the “PID Controller in Betaflight” module : with a 2 ms delay, raise P until sustained oscillations start, and write down P_max and the frequency; with a 5 ms delay, repeat. Expected: P_max is noticeably lower, and the oscillation frequency is lower. Step 2. ζ from overshoot From the log data-python → step_metrics : overshoot → ζ via the formula; settling time → ωₙ. Compare two axes. Step 3. Bounce-back ↔ D Take logs before/after changing D by 20%: the median bounce-back and the motor noise. Explain them through ζ and delay. Step 4. Cascade ArduPilot SITL: raise ATC_ANG_RLL_P from 4.5 to 15 with a standard rate tune — observe the angle oscillations; explain them by the ratio of the bandw

title: System identification: chirp, frequency response, a model for tuning
summary: Tuning “by eye,” and even AUTOTUNE, answers the question “which gains,” but not “why.” System identification answers it: you feed the vehicle a known signal (a chirp — a sine wave with rising frequency), record the response, compute the frequency response, and fit a model with meaningful parameters
headings: Why a model The chirp and the requirements for the experiment SYSID mode in ArduCopter Frequency response from spectra Fitting the model Model → tuning Step 1. Synthetic check Step 2. Phase margin from the model Step 3. SYSID in SITL Step 4. Change and compare
text: summary Tuning “by eye,” and even AUTOTUNE, answers the question “which gains,” but not “why.” System identification answers it: you feed the vehicle a known signal a chirp — a sine wave with rising frequency , record the response, compute the frequency response, and fit a model with meaningful parameters to it — the motor time constant, the delay, the gain. With a model, tuning becomes a calculation: phase margin, crossover frequency, what a filter will cost. This module covers the chirp and the requirements for the experiment, the SYSID mode in ArduCopter, estimating the frequency response from spectra, fitting a first-order-plus-delay model, and using the model to choose gains. The code is checked on synthetic data first, then on a SITL log. theory Why a model - A controller is tuned for a plant. The plant of a copter's rate loop is “torque command → angular rate”: the body inertia, the motor time constant prop spin-up , the delays filters, ESC, the computation loop . - A model of the form G s = K·e^ −sτ / Ts + 1 or with an integrator, to go to the angle describes this chain with three numbers. Knowing them, you can compute the phase margin for any gains, see how much phase a new filter will “eat,” and compare two vehicles objectively. - The “Control Theory” module gave you the language transfer functions, margins ; here you learn how to get a model from a flight. The chirp and the requirements for the experiment - A chirp is a sine wave whose frequency rises from f₀ to f₁ over the recording time. An exponential logarithmic chirp spends the same time on every octave — convenient for a logarithmic frequency axis. - Frequency range : from below the expected loop bandwidth 1–2 Hz to above the crossover frequency 30–60 Hz for small copters , but below the frequencies where the noise and frame resonances are. - Amplitude : large enough for the signal to be above the noise, and small enough not to drive the motors into saturation and nonlinearity. The sign of saturation is motors at their limit in the log. - Duration : tens of seconds — more periods at low frequencies, a more accurate estimate. - Closed loop. The vehicle flies with the controllers running, so input and output are coupled through the controller. It matters where the signal is injected and what is taken as the “input”: you estimate the ratio of the output to the actual signal at the plant input for example, to the controller/mixer output , not to the setpoint. SYSID mode in ArduCopter - A mode “like STABILIZE” that injects a chirp at a selected point in the loop and writes the data to the log SIDD messages — time-domain data, SIDS — settings . - SID_AXIS — where to inject angle, rate or mixer on roll/pitch/yaw, etc.; the values are per the list for your version . While SID_AXIS = 0 , you can't enter the mode; in addition, the vehicle must be airborne, and you can switch to SYSID for axes 1–13 only from a manual-throttle mode STABILIZE, ACRO , and for axes 14–19 only from LOITER. - SID_MAGNITUDE — amplitude, SID_F_START_HZ and SID_F_STOP_HZ — the range, SID_T_REC — recording duration, SID_T_FADE_IN / SID_T_FADE_OUT — smooth ramp-up and ramp-down of the amplitude. - Safety: altitude, open space, the pilot ready to take over by switching modes; start with a small amplitude, and in SITL first. - Betaflight and PX4: Betaflight since 2025.12 has a CHIRP mode build option USE_CHIRP , parameters chirp_ , the settings are written to the Blackbox header ; 4.5 has no built-in chirp analysis is done from Blackbox with manual disturbances ; in PX4 the copter autotune identifies the model online by itself, and for manual identification there are signal generators in test builds — see the documentation for your version. Frequency response from spectra For a linear system Y f = H f ·U f . The estimate is H = Y·U / U ², averaged over frequency bands: divide the cross-spectrum by the input spectrum. Averaging over a band suppresses noise; where there is little energy in the input outside the chirp , the estimate is meaningless. - Coherence the quality of the estimate — how much of the output is explained linearly by the input: close to 1 — good; dropping — noise, nonlinearity, another input wind, pilot . - The result is points on a Bode plot: gain in dB and phase in degrees. Fitting the model Model G s = K·e^ −sτ / Ts + 1 : - at low frequencies the gain ≈ K; - at the corner frequency 1/ 2πT the gain is −3 dB, the phase −45° without delay ; - the delay τ doesn't change the gain but adds −360°·f·τ of phase, growing with frequency. So T is seen from the gain, τ from the “extra” phase at high frequencies. The fit minimizes the difference between the complex H and G over the points grid search over T and τ, K analytically . On the module's example T = 20 ms, τ = 10 ms, noise on the output the fit returns T = 20 ms and τ ≈ 9 ms: the model is continuous while the data are discrete with a 2.5 ms step, so half a step of delay gets “lost.” {{diagram:chart-sysid-bode Frequency response from a chirp: points computed from spectra and a first-order-plus-delay model; the gain corner is at 8 Hz, and the phase drops off because of the delay.}} Model → tuning - Phase margin. For a proportional controller Kp the open loop is L = Kp·G. The crossover frequency is where L = 1; the phase margin is 180° + ∠L at it. The larger Kp, the higher the crossover frequency and the smaller the margin because of the delay. - The cost of a filter. A low-pass filter with frequency f_c adds approximately −arctan f/f_c of phase: at a 20 Hz loop crossover, an 80 Hz filter takes away ~14°. This is the “filters eat the margin” from the “Filters” module — now as a number. - Comparing vehicles and changes. New props, motors, frame — a new model: you can see whether the time constant or the delay changed, and how much in gains it costs. practice Step 1. text: summary “Crisper,” “softer,” “it wobbles,” “it runs hot” — pilot feelings that can be turned into numbers from the log so you can compare profiles honestly. This module gives you a working method: filters before PID, one parameter per step, four profiles in one flight, five per-maneuver metrics. The case study is an experiment on two identical 7" drones: four profiles, what matched the feelings, what didn't, and why the outcome was not a new PID but new filters. theory Order: filters first, then PID PID amplifies everything that comes from the gyro, noise included. Tuning PID on bad filters is like tuning an amplifier against a background of interference. So: the RPM filter and the dynamic notch are working, the spectrum is clean the filter and RPM filter modules , and only then — PID. Betaflight 4.3+ sliders The simplified tuning mode turns groups of parameters at once: - Damping D — resistance to fast movements, damps overshoot; higher — the motors heat up. - Tracking P and I — how precisely it follows the stick and disturbances; higher — oscillations. - Stick Response FF — response to fast stick movements; higher — overshoot at the end of a flip. - Dynamic Damping D max — how much D can grow on fast moves. - Drift – Wobble I — holding in turns and at zero throttle. - Master Multiplier — everything at once; you touch it when the others run out of travel. In the CLI these are simplified_pi_gain , simplified_d_gain , simplified_feedforward_gain , simplified_dmax_gain in 2025.12 — simplified_d_max_gain , simplified_i_gain , simplified_master_multiplier plus simplified_tuning apply . There are four PID profiles and four rate profiles — switched from a switch or in the CLI with the profile N command. {{widget:pid-sim}} Symptoms - P too high — twitchy, overcorrects, fast oscillation. Too low — sluggish, slow wobble. - I too high — “robotic,” low-frequency oscillation. Too low — drifts off, “skates like on ice.” - D too low — bounce-back after flips, propwash on descents. Too high — hot motors, mushy response. - FF too high — overshoot at the start of a flip, jitter on stick movements. Check motor temperature after every change to D or the filters: a short flight, land, finger on the motor. If you can't hold it — roll back. Five per-maneuver metrics A maneuver is a segment where setpoint is above a threshold for example, 200 °/s for longer than 50 ms. For each one: Feeling Metric How to compute --- --- --- runs hot motor noise std of motor commands above 40 Hz, averaged over motors shakes on descent propwash RMS gyro RMS in the 20–70 Hz band on descent segments wobbles after a stop bounce-back opposite-sign gyro peak within 150 ms after the stop / maneuver amplitude, % slow on the stick entry lag time from the start of setpoint movement to 50% on gyro, ms undershoots / overshoots peak tracking max gyro / max setpoint, % The median over 10–20 maneuvers is robust; one bad snap ruins the mean. The classic step response Blackbox Explorer; PID-Analyzer — not developed since 2019, PIDscope works well on long freestyle logs, but on short logs of 1–2 minutes per profile it is noisy to ±40% — direct metrics are more honest. Case study: four profiles on two 7" drones Two nearly identical 7" drones same frame, motors, props, FC , brought to a common baseline. The four profiles differed only in sliders; filters were the same: COOL SHARP WASH FLOAT --- --- --- --- --- Tracking 1.00 1.15 1.00 1.00 Damping 1.00 1.00 1.20 0.85 D max 1.00 1.00 1.20 1.00 Feedforward 1.00 1.15 1.00 0.80 Result drone A, medians : motor noise 16.1 / 23.3 / 18.0 / 14.6; bounce-back 6.0 / 8.5 / 9.4 / 14.9%; entry lag 38 / 31 / 40 / 44 ms. - SHARP “crisper” — yes: lag is 7 ms lower. The price — motor noise +45%. That's P: it raises the gain at all frequencies. - FLOAT “softer” — yes, the quietest. But bounce-back is almost 15%: after a stop the drone rolls back by 1/7 of the amplitude. Bad for filming. - WASH “didn't feel a difference” — and the numbers confirmed it: propwash 0.97 of COOL, within the noise. At 1.4 kg on 7" props, propwash is aerodynamics, not underdamping. The profile was dropped. - The two “identical” drones gave different bounce-back on SHARP 2.9% vs. 8.5% : on the second one the pilot flew harder, and D-max had time to kick in. The lesson about the method: compare profiles only within a single flight or normalize to the maneuver amplitude. Outcome: COOL is the best compromise. Crispness was brought back not through P but through the filters: simplified_gyro_filter_multiplier 1.00 → 1.10 and dyn_notch_q 400 → 450, PID as in COOL. That's how the CRISP profile came about. The first proposal was more aggressive 1.25 and a single notch ; it was rejected in favor of small steps: 1.10 → flight → if successful, 1.20. Tuning protocol by data, not by feel 1. Baseline : 4.5 defaults, filters per the “Filters” module, clean spectrum, cold motors. Log A: 30 s hover + 10 maneuvers with a sharp stop on roll/pitch + 3 descents with propwash. 2. Metrics from log A data-python : step_metrics , bounce_back , motor noise, propwash RMS — into a table. 3. One slider per flight : Damping ±0.1 → log → metrics; then Tracking ±0.1; then Stick Response. Acceptance criterion: the target metric improved, the others didn't get worse, the motors aren't hotter. 4. A profile for the job : racing higher Tracking, higher Stick Response and calm higher Damping — different profile s, switched from a switch. 5. Lock it in : diff all + a “what — why — metrics before/after” table in the repository the “CI” module . One flight — one change. Two changes in one flight make the log useless. Metric reference values for 5" 6S Metric Good Tolerable Problem --- --- --- --- overshoot 3–10% 10–20% 20% P/FF bounce-back < 8% 8–15% 15% D, delay entry lag to 50% 20–35 ms 35–50 50 FF, filters settle ±5% < 80 ms 80–150 150 motor noise std 40 Hz low, stable grows with D “grass” on the motor trace motor temperature warm too hot to touch for 5 s can't hold a finger on it

title: Рейты, RC smoothing и feedforward: от стика до setpoint
summary: Модуль разбирает путь команды от стика до setpoint — желаемой угловой скорости, с которой PID сравнивает гироскоп. Это калибровка каналов (`rxrange`), формулы пяти типов рейтов из `fc/rc.c`, кривая газа, профили рейтов, RC smoothing с автоподбором частоты среза по скорости приёмника и feedforward с

Порт формул и конвертер рейтов Шаг 2. PT3-сглаживание ступеньки стика Шаг 3. Jitter-фильтр, газ и throttle limit Переход на реальное железо
text: summary Модуль разбирает путь команды от стика до setpoint — желаемой угловой скорости, с которой PID сравнивает гироскоп. Это калибровка каналов rxrange , формулы пяти типов рейтов из fc/rc.c , кривая газа, профили рейтов, RC smoothing с автоподбором частоты среза по скорости приёмника и feedforward с его фильтрами от дрожания. Лабораторная — Python-порт формул прошивки. Он переводит рейты между Actual, Betaflight и Quick с сохранением центра и максимума и моделирует PT3-сглаживание ступеньки стика на ELRS 50…1000 Гц. Затем на железе: проверка rxrange , чтение rc_smoothing_info с реальным линком и слепое сравнение профилей рейтов с переключением в полёте. theory Цепочка от стика до PID Порядок обработки rx/rx.c , fc/rc.c , flight/mixer.c ; одинаков в 4.5 и 2025.12 : 1. Приёмник отдаёт канал в микросекундах. CRSF/ELRS: 172…1811 → 988…2012 мкс rx/crsf.c . 2. rxrange растягивает первые четыре канала после map из min…max в 1000…2000. AUX-каналы не масштабируются. 3. Проверка валидности: вне rx_min_usec … rx_max_usec 885…2115 канал считается плохим. Он 300 мс держит последнее значение, затем получает значение из rxfail , а для каналов 0–3 Betaflight объявляет потерю сигнала failsafe . 4. Roll/pitch/yaw: rcCommand = rcData − mid_rc с вычетом deadband yaw_deadband , ограничение ±500. Отклонение x = rcCommand / 500 − deadband ∈ −1; 1 . 5. applyRates x даёт °/с, затем ограничение _rate_limit по умолчанию 1998 . Результат — rawSetpoint. 6. Feedforward считается из rawSetpoint на каждом новом RC-пакете. 7. RC smoothing PT3 сглаживает setpoint и feedforward на частоте PID-цикла. Дальше их берёт PID. 8. Газ: rcData − min_check ·1000/ 2000 − min_check → кривая thr_mid / thr_hover / thr_expo → PT3 газа → throttle_limit_ в миксере. {{diagram:chart-bf-rates-curves Центр и максимум ещё не задают ощущение стика. Actual 20/67/54 и Betaflight 1.01/0.70/0.01 совпадают до 4 °/с. Дефолтный Actual 7/67/0 70 → 670 °/с с тем же центром и максимумом в Betaflight расходится до 151 °/с в середине хода.}} Пять типов рейтов rates_type , по умолчанию ACTUAL Значения хранятся целыми: rc_rate , srate , expo по осям roll_ / pitch_ / yaw_ . Ниже x — отклонение стика, e = expo/100 . Формулы взяты из функций apply Rates . Тип Формула, °/с Центр наклон при x→0 Максимум x = 1 --- --- --- --- BETAFLIGHT x' = x·\ x\ ³·e + x· 1−e ; 200·r·x' / 1 − \ x\ ·s , r = rc_rate/100 при r 2: r += 14.54· r−2 , s = srate/100 200·r· 1−e 200·r / 1−s ACTUAL C·x + M−C ·\ x\ · x⁵·e + x· 1−e , C = rc_rate·10, M = srate·10 C M QUICK R·x / 1 − c·k , R = rc_rate·2, k = M/R − 1 / M/R , c = \ x\ ³·e + \ x\ · 1−e R M = srate·10 KISS 2000· rc_rate/1000 · x³·e + x· 1−e / 1 − \ x\ ·srate/100 2·rc_rate· 1−e 2·rc_rate / 1 − srate/100 RACEFLIGHT 10·rc_rate·x· 1 + e· x²−1 · 1 + \ x\ ·srate/100 10·rc_rate· 1−e 10·rc_rate· 1 + srate/100 Выводы из формул: - В Actual три параметра независимы: centre sensitivity, max rate, expo. В Quick независим центр, а expo и rate вместе формируют кривую. В Betaflight, KISS и RaceFlight каждое число меняет и центр, и максимум. - В Betaflight expo не трогает максимум, но снижает центр в 1−e раз. Super rate поднимает край кривой гиперболой 1/ 1 − x ·s . - Дефолт — ACTUAL 7/67/0 и в 4.5, и в 2025.12 : центр 70 °/с, максимум 670 °/с. При expo = 0 кривая Actual не линейна: квадратичный член M−C ·x· x даёт 185 °/с на половине хода. - QUICK при quickrates_rc_expo = ON применяет expo к самому стику, а не только к super-фактору. - Лимиты по типу validateAndFixRatesSettings , config/config.c обрезают значения при загрузке конфига. rc_rate/srate: BETAFLIGHT 255/100, ACTUAL 200/200, QUICK 255/200, KISS 255/99, RACEFLIGHT 200/255. Expo везде до 100. При смене rates_type в CLI числа не пересчитываются: тот же 7/67/0 в Betaflight даёт 14 °/с в центре. Газ: thr_mid , thr_hover , thr_expo , throttle_limit_ Кривая газа — таблица из 12 точек. В 2025.12 initRcProcessing она строится из двух квадратичных кривых Безье, которые сходятся в точке thr_mid , thr_hover : положение стика thr_mid даёт выход thr_hover оба в процентах, дефолты 50 и 50 . При thr_expo = 0 получаются два прямых отрезка: 0, 0 → thr_mid , thr_hover → 100, 100 ; при равных thr_mid и thr_hover это одна прямая. С expo оба отрезка выгибаются так, что кривая уплощается вокруг точки висения: при thr_expo = 100 касательная в ней горизонтальна. Так получают более мягкий газ около висения, а точку ставят туда, где аппарат реально висит. В 4.5 переменной thr_hover нет, кривая считалась по другой формуле tmp = 10·i − mid , выход = 10·mid + tmp· 100 − expo + expo·tmp²/y² /10 , и при thr_expo = 0 thr_mid ни на что не влиял . throttle_limit_type OFF/SCALE/CLIP с throttle_limit_percent 25…100 работает в миксере. SCALE умножает газ на процент. CLIP обрезает газ сверху. Это ограничитель для учебного аппарата и полётов в помещении, по профилю рейтов. Профили рейтов и переключение Профилей рейтов четыре и в 4.5, и в 2025.12 CONTROL_RATE_PROFILE_COUNT 4 , индексы 0–3 . В профиль входит всё из таблицы ниже с пометкой «профиль»: тип, рейты, thr_ , throttle_limit_ , _rate_limit , имя. Способы переключения: - CLI rateprofile без аргумента печатает текущий и rateprofile 2 . Переменные из set / get относятся к текущему профилю. diff rates выводит только текущий профиль, diff all — все четыре. - Adjustments, функция 12 RATE_PROFILE: adjrange <i 0 <aux 900 2100 12 <aux 0 0 . Диапазон 900…2100 делится на три позиции по 400 мкс 0, 1, 2 , смена профиля сопровождается position+1 бипами. С rate_6pos_switch = ON позиций шесть, но позиции 5–6 указывают на несуществующие индексы 4–5, и профиль не меняется. Работает в полёте. - Команды стиками только в дизарме и в ACRO: газ вверх + тангаж вверх / тангаж вниз / крен вправо / крен влево → профили 1/2/3/4. В ANGLE/HORIZON те же сочетания подстраивают акселерометр. - OSD-элемент osd_rate_profile_name_pos , имя задаётся в rateprofile_name до 8 символов . Профиль PID таким способом не переключается: у Adjustments нет функции PID-профиля. Концы каналов: rxrange и почему 988–2

text: summary Вкладка Adjustments и CLI-команда adjrange дают менять PID, рейты и профили с пульта — без ноутбука, прямо в воздухе. Это удобно и опасно одновременно: изменение применяется сразу, в EEPROM само не пишется, а номер функции в CLI не совпадает с номером в исходнике. Модуль разбирает fc/rc_adjustments.c из Betaflight 2025.12 от 4.5 файл отличается только добавленной функцией 31 LED_DIMMER : 30 слотов, два канала на слот, три режима шаг, абсолютный, выбор , полную таблицу функций с номерами CLI, тайминг 500 мс и пороги ±200 мкс, сохранение стиками, OSD и Blackbox. Отдельно — команда vtx для мощности, бэнда и канала видеопередатчика на тумблере, vtxtable и vtx_low_power_disarm . Лабораторная: Python-модель, повторяющая логику прошивки прогон и вывод в тексте , затем стол без пропов и короткая сессия висения с подстройкой D и сохранением. theory Зачем это нужно и чего это не умеет Типичные задачи: подкрутить P/D/FF в поле, когда ноутбука нет; переключать профили рейтов для разных пилотов; профиль OSD «гонка / дальний / пусто»; цвет LED-ленты; мощность VTX «низкая на столе, рабочая в воздухе». Для последнего служит отдельная команда vtx , а не adjrange . Чего Adjustments не умеют ни в 4.5, ни в 2025.12 : переключать PID-профиль функции нет, режима в Modes тоже нет , менять D max d_max_ ; в 4.5 недоступен был d_min_ , фильтры, слайдеры simplified_ , anti-gravity, бэнд/канал/мощность VTX. PID-профиль меняется только при дизарме: стиками газ вниз + рысканье влево + крен влево / тангаж вверх / крен вправо → профиль 1/2/3, fc/rc_controls.c , из OSD-меню, командой CLI profile или через auto_profile_cell_count . В полёте — никак. Профили, которые переключаются в воздухе: рейты функция 12 , OSD 29 , LED 30 ; с 2025.12 так же меняется яркость ленты 31, LED_DIMMER . Двухканальная модель: слот, диапазон, функция Слотов 30 MAX_ADJUSTMENT_RANGE_COUNT 30 , индексы 0…29; официальная страница In-flight Adjustments пишет «12» — это устарело . Каждый слот хранит: - канал диапазона auxChannelIndex , AUX1 = 0 и диапазон start..end 900–2100, шаг 25, как у aux . Слот активен, если start ≤ канал < end конец не включается, isRangeActive в fc/rc_modes.c ; - функцию — номер из таблицы ниже; - канал подстройки auxSwitchChannelIndex , AUX1 = 0 — тумблер или крутилка, которая меняет значение. Он может совпадать с каналом диапазона; - center и scale — для абсолютного режима. Все активные слоты обрабатываются одновременно: можно крутить четыре параметра четырьмя каналами. Неактивный слот ничего не меняет, поэтому «безопасную позицию» селектора проще всего оставить без слота. Подстройки обрабатываются в задаче приёма RC fc/core.c , и в арме, и в дизарме , но не в режиме CLI и не при активном PARALYZE в дизарме. Три режима - Шаг STEP — center = 0 , функция не из группы выбора. Канал подстройки выше mid_rc + 200 1700 мкс при mid_rc 1500 → +1, ниже mid_rc − 200 1300 → −1. Шаг равен 1 для всех функций. При удержании значение повторяется каждые 500 мс RESET_FREQUENCY_2HZ ; возврат в центр сразу «взводит» слот, поэтому быстрые нажатия быстрее удержания. Бипер: 2 коротких — вверх, 1 такой же короткий — вниз beeperConfirmationBeeps 2 / 1 . - Абсолютный ABSOLUTE — center ≠ 0 , шаговая функция. Значение = center + rc − 1500 × scale / 500 целочисленное деление C, усекает к нулю , применяется при каждом изменении канала. Крутилка в 1000 даёт center − scale , в 2000 — center + scale . Пока слот неактивен, «последнее значение канала» сбрасывается в 0 — в момент включения слота значение прыгает в позицию крутилки. - Выбор SELECT — функции 12, 24, 25, 29, 30. Диапазон 900–2099 делится на N равных частей: позиция = rc − 900 / 1200 / N . RATE_PROFILE: N = 3, или 6 при rate_6pos_switch = ON но профилей рейтов 4 — позиции 5–6 некуда переключать . OSD_PROFILE: N = 3, пишется позиция + 1 osd_profile 1…3 . LED_PROFILE: N = 3 RACE / BEACON / STATUS . PID_AUDIO: N = 7. HORIZON_STRENGTH: N = 255. Пределы: P/I/D 0–200 хотя set p_roll принимает до 250 , F 0–2000 set f_roll — до 1000 , RC rate 1–255, expo 0–100, super rate 0–255, thr_expo 0–100, feedforward_transition 1–100. Таблица функций 2025.12: номер CLI ≠ номер enum CLI-номер — это позиция в массиве defaultAdjustmentConfigs плюс 1, а не значение adjustmentFunction_e . В enum на местах 25–28 стоят ROLL/PITCH RC RATE/EXPO, которых в массиве нет, поэтому с 25-го номера всё сдвинуто на 4. Таблица ниже напечатана скриптом лабораторной из исходника 4.5.6 и сверена с 2025.12.5: строки 1–30 совпадают, в 2025.12 добавлена строка 31. text: summary The Betaflight command line CLI is a text interface that gives you access to the flight controller's configuration at a level the graphical interface doesn't offer. From the CLI you can change any parameter, including ones not exposed on the configurator tabs, check the hardware state, manage resources microcontroller pins and make backups. The key practical goal of this article is to give you confident command of resource and pin remapping without reflashing, and to teach you to inspect what is in the firmware build and restore the configuration after a failure. theory CLI architecture The CLI runs over a serial port UART , using the same channel as the configurator MSP , MultiWii Serial Protocol . To enter the CLI from a terminal e.g. PuTTY/screen , send the character — it switches the controller into command mode. Key commands and what they do - Session control: save , exit , batch start , batch end - Viewing the configuration: get , diff , dump , status , version - Changing parameters: set , feature , profile , rateprofile - Resource remapping: resource , timer - Troubleshooting and debugging: tasks , flash_info , dma Diff vs Dump: what to use and when diff all prints only the changed parameters. It is the main format for backups and for safe transfer within the same firmware version. dump all prints a full snapshot of the configuration, including default values. It suits deep troubleshooting, but is dangerous to carry between different versions. It is recommended to save separately: - diff all - resource show - status version/build {{diagram:bf-diff-scopes Простой diff пишет только активные PID- и рейт-профиль; все 4 + 4 профиля, mcu_id и обёртку с save содержит только diff all.}} Resource remapping: concept and limits The resource command manages the “function - physical pin” binding: text resource <FUNCTION <INDEX <PIN resource MOTOR 1 B00 resource MOTOR 5 NONE - ADC resources ADC_BATT , ADC_CURR , ADC_RSSI can only be assigned to ADC pins. - UARTs are limited by the controller's hardware blocks — not every pin can be used as a serial port. - For DShot, timers and DMA are critical: a wrong pin/channel leaves the motors dead. Betaflight 4.5 specifics Between versions, the names and logic of some parameters change: - D-term naming: in 4.5 d_roll is the peak D and d_min_roll is the base; in 2025.12 it's the other way round: d_roll is the base and d_max_roll is the peak d_min_ were removed . - GPS rescue: some variables were reworked. - Failsafe landing: differences in naming/behavior appeared. Because of this, you can't mindlessly paste old backups into new firmware. Checking the build contents via BUILD KEY In Betaflight 4.5+ status shows a BUILD KEY . Put it into the URL below and you get JSON with the list of enabled options Options : text https://build.betaflight.com/api/builds/<BUILD_KEY /json This helps diagnose missing features e.g. GPS/LED/VTX without reflashing. The recipes you need most often commands from cli/cli.c Task Command --- --- Find the version, target / BUILD KEY version / status CPU load, arming flags, gyro rate status , tasks Move a motor to another pad resource MOTOR 3 B01 → save resource show all — what's in use Change the motor order without resoldering resource pair swap, or “Motor direction/remap” on the Motors tab Reverse one motor's direction DShot commands dshotprog 0 21 21 — reversed, 20 — normal; on some ESCs 7/8 — direction 1/2 , then dshotprog 0 12 save settings ; motors without props, index from 0 255 — all motors Check DShot telemetry dshot_telemetry_info Timers/DMA motor, LED, serial conflicts timer , dma show Reset to defaults without saving / with saving defaults nosave , defaults Enter the DFU bootloader bl or bl rom Flash as a USB drive pulling logs msc Flash/configure ESCs serialpassthrough / escprog via the ESC configurator Batch-load a diff without intermediate reboots batch start … batch end → save Channel ranges, stick map rxrange , map AETR1234 Profiles profile 1 , rateprofile 2 Betaflight has no battery_profile command Beeper/sound test, sensors beeper , play_sound , gyroregisters detected sensors are in the status output Board signature and identification board_name , manufacturer_id , mcu_id , signature Worked example: the motor 2 pad burned off An F405 board, the M2 pad came off. resource show all — free timer pads: LED_STRIP 1 A08 . Check timer A08 list — there's a timer with DMA; resource LED_STRIP 1 NONE , resource MOTOR 2 A08 , timer A08 AF1 if needed , dma pin A08 0 , save ; Motors tab — motor 2 spins in the right position, without props; diff all into the repo with a comment. If the pad's timer conflicts with the other motors' DShot one DMA group , dma show will reveal it, and bitbang DShot dshot_bitbang = ON works around some conflicts. {{diagram:bf-resource-remap Moving a motor to another pad: check the timer and DMA, free the old resource, assign the new one, save and check on the Motors tab.}} text Available: RX_PPM INFLIGHT_ACC_CAL RX_SERIAL MOTOR_STOP SERVO_TILT SOFTSERIAL GPS RANGEFINDER TELEMETRY 3D RX_PARALLEL_PWM RX_MSP RSSI_ADC LED_STRIP DISPLAY OSD CHANNEL_FORWARDING TRANSPONDER AIRMODE RX_SPI ESC_SENSOR ANTI_GRAVITY practice Getting into the CLI 1. Connect the flight controller over USB and open Betaflight Configurator. 2. Go to the CLI tab. 3. Click Connect if the connection didn't come up automatically. The terminal alternative: - connect to the port /dev/ttyACM0 on Linux or COMx on Windows ; - set the baud rate to 115200 ; - send the character. Making a full backup Before any changes, save the current state: text status version diff all resource show timer show Save the output to a file — it gives you: - the version and build; - the list of changed parameters; - resource assignments; - the timer configuration. Viewing and changing parameters Viewing: text get gyro_ get acc set dyn_notch_min_hz = 150 Changing: text set dyn_notch_min_hz = 150 set dyn_notch_q = 250 save For batch editing fewer reboots : tex

text:
summary Once you have more than one drone, configuring them by clicking around in Configurator is a road to mistakes. The Betaflight CLI is available over an ordinary serial port, which means you can script it. This module shows a working Python template pyserial and collects the pitfalls we actually stepped on while configuring several quadcopters in bulk: floating COM ports, “silent” parameter corrections, reboots and diff incompatibility between versions. theory How entering the CLI works Over USB, a flight controller is a virtual COM port USB CDC . The baud rate in the port settings doesn't matter for USB CDC; 115200 is the convention. The character puts the controller into the CLI, exit leaves it with a reboot. While the FC is in the CLI, no signal goes to the motors — the ESCs may beep, that's normal. Pitfall 1: the COM port isn't fixed If several identical boards are connected to the computer, they share one USB VID/PID, and the COM port number changes after every reboot. You can't bind to COM8 . The reliable identifier is the craft_name inside the config: open each port, enter the CLI, run get craft_name and pick the right one. Hence the rule: every drone gets a distinct craft_name before you start working. Pitfall 2: exit noreboot reboots In Betaflight 4.5.0–4.5.3 the exit command always reboots the controller the noreboot argument appeared in 4.5.4 and 2025.12.x . So after any exit the script has to find the port again by craft_name . When you “just want to peek at a value”, don't leave the CLI with a command — just close the port. Pitfall 3: silent corrections set + save doesn't guarantee that the value stayed the way you wrote it. On boot, Betaflight corrects incompatible combinations: the DShot protocol, bidirectional DShot, the timer layout on a specific board. In our practice, on an F405 board, after enabling bidir the DShot protocol turned out not to be what we had written. Rule: after every save and reboot, re-read every changed value with get and compare it with the expected one. Pitfall 4: a diff doesn't carry over between versions Parameter names and meanings change between firmware versions: debug_mode values get renamed, the serial command syntax changes, the meaning of the D-term PID parameters changes. You can't paste a diff all from 2025.12 into 4.5 or vice versa line by line. Moving settings between versions only works deliberately, section by section, with re-reading. Why diff and not dump diff all contains only the differences from defaults — you can read it by eye and keep it in git. dump is everything at once; when you update the firmware it drags the old defaults along as explicit values. Minimal script for exporting diff all pyserial python import serial, time, sys, glob def cli port, cmds, timeout=3.0 : """Open CLI, run commands, return full text. Do not send 'exit' reboots on 4.5 .""" with serial.Serial port, 115200, timeout=0.2 as s: s.write b" 
" ; time.sleep 0.5 ; s.read s.in_waiting or 1 out = "" for c in cmds: s.write c + "
" .encode ; t0 = time.time ; buf = "" while time.time - t0 < timeout: chunk = s.read 4096 .decode errors="replace" if chunk: buf += chunk; t0 = time.time if buf.rstrip .endswith " " : break prompt returned out += buf return out ports = glob.glob "/dev/ttyACM " Linux; Windows: COM for p in ports: name = cli p, "get craft_name" if "viking7" in name: text = cli p, "version", "diff all" open "viking7/betaflight/diff-all.txt", "w" .write text break else: sys.exit "craft not found" Normalize before committing: strip the date/time lines from version and the echo, sort the blocks — otherwise git diff gets noisy the “CI” module . What's worth automating and what isn't Worth it: a diff all backup before every flying day; checking invariants failsafe, poles, bidir from the export; bulk changes of craft_name /VTX table across the fleet; downloading logs via msc . Not worth it: bulk “rolling out PIDs” to different vehicles different mechanics , any change without re-reading with get after save . {{diagram:bf-cli-session A CLI session over serial: wait for the prompt, re-read values after set, find the port again after save.}} practice Step 1. A minimal CLI client in Python python import time import serial from serial.tools import list_ports def cli_cmd port: serial.Serial, cmd: str, wait: float = 0.6 - str: port.write cmd + "
" .encode time.sleep wait return port.read_all .decode errors="replace" def enter_cli port: serial.Serial - None: port.write b"
" time.sleep 0.3 port.read_all port.write b" " time.sleep 1.2 port.read_all def find_craft craft_name: str - str: """Return the COM port of the FC whose craft_name matches. Never trust COM numbers.""" for info in list_ports.comports : try: with serial.Serial info.device, 115200, timeout=1 as p: enter_cli p out = cli_cmd p, "get craft_name" do NOT send exit here: on 4.5.x it reboots the FC if f"craft_name = {craft_name}" in out: return info.device except serial.SerialException: continue raise RuntimeError f"FC '{craft_name}' not found" Step 2. Applying changes with verification python CHANGES = {"rpm_filter_min_hz": "50", "failsafe_delay": "15"} port_name = find_craft "viking2" with serial.Serial port_name, 115200, timeout=1 as p: enter_cli p backup = cli_cmd p, "diff all", wait=3.0 open "viking2_before_diff.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8" .write backup for key, val in CHANGES.items : cli_cmd p, f"set {key} = {val}" cli_cmd p, "save", wait=1.0 FC reboots, COM port may change time.sleep 6 port_name = find_craft "viking2" find it again after reboot with serial.Serial port_name, 115200, timeout=1 as p: enter_cli p for key, val in CHANGES.items : out = cli_cmd p, f"get {key}" ok = f"{key} = {val}" in out print "OK " if ok else "FAIL" , key, "expected", val Step 3. Keep configs as code 1. A folder per drone, with configs/ and logs/ inside. 2. File name: <drone _<board _<YYYY-MM-DD _diff.txt — sorting by name = sorting by date. 3. text: summary GPS на Betaflight нужен для GPS Rescue, стрелки дома и скорости в OSD. Важно не «спутники есть», а «дом записан правильно и курс известен». Модуль разбирает выбор и подключение u-blox M8 или M10, что Betaflight пишет в приёмник при gps_auto_config = ON по коду io/gps.c , который в четырёх местах расходится с документацией , переменные gps_ и mag_ , флаг арма GPS, запись дома, курс без компаса, OSD, gpspassthrough с u-center, холодный, тёплый и горячий старт, DOP и CEP. Лабораторная на Python: парсер UBX по правилам 4.5 проверяется на реальной записи M8030 DOP совпал с приёмником до 0.02 , затем шесть синтетических логов показывают влияние созвездий и шума VTX, плюс загрузка UART. На железе — спутники при выключенном и включённом VTX, хронометраж холодного старта и проверка дома. Сам GPS Rescue — в bf-failsafe и bf-setup-scratch . theory Что GPS даёт Betaflight 2025.12 Betaflight не летает по точкам это INAV и ArduPilot, inav-gps . С 2025.12 он умеет удерживать позицию режим POS HOLD, id 11, переменные pos_hold_ и ap_position_ ; опция сборки и высоту ALTHOLD ; в 4.5 этих режимов нет. Координаты идут в GPS Rescue, в дом, дистанцию и стрелку OSD, в скорость и координаты OSD и телеметрии, в высоту flight/position.c смешивает GPS с баро с весом gpsTrust = min 1/PDOP, 0.9 и в круговой таймер gps_lap_timer_ . Без компаса GPS ещё и задаёт курс; POS HOLD без компаса разрешает pos_hold_without_mag по умолчанию OFF . Модуль: M8 или M10 Параметр u-blox M8 NEO-M8N, FW 3.01 u-blox M10 MAX-M10S, ROM SPG 5.10 --- --- --- Созвездия по умолчанию GPS + GLONASS + SBAS, QZSS , Galileo выключен GPS + Galileo + BeiDou B1I + QZSS, SBAS Холодный старт 26 с GPS+GLO , 29 с только GPS 27 с по умолчанию, 23–28 с в других наборах Горячий старт 1 с 1 с Точность CEP 24 ч, статика 2.5 м 2.0 м с SBAS 1.5 м Макс. частота навигации NEO-M8N: 5 Гц при двух системах, 10 Гц при одной 3 Гц по умолчанию GPS+GAL+BDS , 10 Гц для GPS+GAL, 6 Гц для GPS+GAL+GLO; 18 Гц при одной системе Питание самого модуля 2.7–3.6 В 1.76–3.6 В, 9.5 мА при 3 В GPS+GAL+BDS UART по умолчанию 9600 8N1, NMEA 9600 8N1, NMEA Цифры — из даташитов u-blox. M10 точнее, экономнее и видит больше спутников, но заводской MAX-M10S при GPS+GAL+BDS не выдаёт 10 Гц, на которые его настраивает Betaflight: потолок 3 Гц. Умолчания M10 зависят от прошивки: у ROM 5.00 это GPS+GAL, у SAM-M10Q — GPS+GAL+GLO+BDS B1C. Версию и набор созвездий смотри в u-center MON-VER, MON-GNSS . FPV-модуль — это приёмник, LDO, патч-антенна, иногда конденсатор или батарейка на V_BCKP и компас на I²C. «5 В» на шелкографии — вход LDO, сам чип питается 3.3 или 1.8 В; без LDO нужен пад 3.3 В, решает маркировка платы. Питание V_BCKP сохраняет эфемериды и часы — повторный старт за секунды. Пусковой ток SAM-M10Q — до 100 мА. Проводка и установка - UART крест-накрест: TX модуля → RX полётника, RX → TX, общий GND. Нужны оба провода: Betaflight шлёт модулю конфигурацию. Только аппаратный UART: на SoftSerial скорость режется до 19200 serial.c , этого мало шаг 3 . Компас SDA/SCL — на I²C-пады. - Антенна смотрит в небо, над ней ничего проводящего. SAM-M10Q даёт оптимальную диаграмму на земляной плоскости 50 × 50 мм; плата FPV-модуля 20–25 мм, поэтому крупный модуль на мачте обычно лучше мелкого в раме. - Помехи: сигналы L1 у Земли — около −130 дБм на 1561–1602 МГц BeiDou B1I 1561.098, GPS и Galileo 1575.42, GLONASS ≈ 1602 . Модуль — подальше от VTX и его антенны, цифрового модуля с камерой, ESC и силовых проводов; видео 1.2–1.3 ГГц ближе всех к L-диапазону. Насколько мешает твой VTX, покажет стендовый тест в практике. - Наклон: документация советует наклонить аппарат на 45° во все стороны — спутники не должны теряться, домой аппарат летит с наклоном. Как Betaflight настраивает модуль по коду Последовательность ниже прочитана по io/gps.c 4.5.6 проверено на 4.5.6 . В 2025.12 файл переформатирован; по нему сверено только то, что названо явно: скорости автопоиска добавлена 230400 , провайдер VIRTUAL, умолчания pg/gps.c , порог GPS_MIN_SAT_COUNT = 4, переключение модели через gps_ublox_acquire_model / gps_ublox_flight_model и то, что gps_auto_baud по-прежнему читается только в status . {{diagram:bf-gps-boot-flow После включения Betaflight сам ищет скорость модуля, переводит его на скорость из serial , пишет настройки в RAM и переключает динамическую модель на первом 3D fix. Дом записывается при арме и при калибровке гиро стиками и только при числе спутников не меньше gps_rescue_min_sats .}} При gps_provider = UBLOX автомат gpsConfigureUblox делает следующее. 1. Поиск скорости. Три запроса MON-VER через 330 мс. Нет ответа — следующая скорость: от скорости из serial вверх до 115200, затем с 9600 вверх по кругу. Ответ hwVersion 00080000 = M8, 000A0000 = M10 выбирает ветку: для M9 и новее CFG-VALSET, для M8 и старше старые сообщения CFG. 2. Смена скорости. Модулю уходит $PUBX,41,… со скоростью GPS из команды serial , затем пауза 990 мс. 3. Конфигурация только при gps_auto_config = ON : пауза 1 с, затем 16 M10 или 22 M8 шагов не чаще раза в 110 мс: частота 1 Гц, отключение NMEA, модель gps_ublox_acquire_model , SBAS, питание FULL, NAV-PVT каждый цикл, NAV-SAT каждый 5-й, gps_update_rate_hz , CFG-GNSS Galileo . Всё — в RAM модуля UBX_VAL_LAYER_RAM . Оценка по константам: заводской модуль на 9600 при serial … 57600 готов через 2 + 0.3 + 1 + 1 + 1.8 ≈ 6 с. 4. Приём. На первом 3D fix не при арме! модуль получает gps_ublox_flight_model . Если NAV-данных нет 2.5 с, автомат снова уходит в поиск скорости. Где документация расходится с кодом проверено на 4.5.6 : - Страница GPS говорит: Stationary до арма, Airborne <4g после. В коде переключение происходит на первом 3D fix gpsUpdate , арм тут ни при чём. - Там же сказано, что gps_sbas_mode по умолчанию AUTO. В pg/gps.c 4.5 и 2025.12 — SBAS_NONE . - По документации GPS Rescue прерывается, когда спутников меньше половины gps_rescue_min_sats . В коде порог фиксирован: GPS_MIN_SAT_COUNT = 4. Это 10 с в полёте RESCUE_LOWSATS , а для «Rescue доступен» хватает 2 с ниже 4. Пр
