text: summary Консоль PX4 и система параметров по исходникам 1.17.0: как попасть в nsh на полётнике и в pxh в SITL и чего в каждой нет, все подкоманды param с точной семантикой, из каких слоёв складывается значение параметра и что из этого попадает в хранилище, чем отличаются четыре вида сброса и три вида бэкапа, почему параметр «пропадает» из QGC, какими командами смотреть датчики, модули, загрузку процессора и лог, и в каком порядке rcS применяет config.txt , extras.txt и rc.txt с SD-карты. После модуля ты по списку param show -c говоришь, что переживёт сброс и перезагрузку, выбираешь команду под вопрос и называешь строку вывода, которая подтверждает гипотезу. Лабораторная — без железа и симулятора: разбор учебного списка параметров, четыре диагностических ситуации, пара файлов для SD-карты и поиск опасных шагов в регламенте; ответы сверяются с эталоном на странице. theory Что в модуле и как читать Модуль закрывает три темы, и читать их лучше в этом порядке. Сначала консоль: как в неё попасть и какие команды есть на полётнике, а какие только в симуляторе. Затем параметры: слои значения, хранилище, команда param , сбросы, перезагрузка и бэкапы — здесь больше всего неочевидного. В конце — команды осмотра, загрузочные скрипты и таблица «какой инструмент под какой вопрос». Назначение портов, выходов и failsafe здесь не повторяется: это модули px4-hardware-peripherals, px4-outputs-servos и px4-safety-return. Как попасть в консоль На полётнике работает оболочка NuttX — nsh . В SITL NuttX нет, там своя оболочка PX4 — pxh shell — оболочка, console — консоль . Модули PX4 в обеих одни и те же, системные команды разные. Вход Как открыть Что видно Когда выбирать --- --- --- --- QGC MAVLink Console Analyze Tools → MAVLink Console, по USB или телеметрии только вывод команды, которую ты запустил по умолчанию: ничего паять не надо Tools/mavlink_shell.py ./Tools/mavlink_shell.py /dev/ttyACM0 , QGC закрыта то же, но в терминале скрипты, запись сеанса в файл System console отладочный UART переходник USB–UART 3.3 В на debug-порт, терминал 57600 8N1 весь вывод загрузки и всех модулей плата не грузится, MAVLink не поднялся nsh по USB SYS_USB_AUTO = 1, терминал, три раза Enter обычный nsh нет MAVLink-клиента под рукой pxh в SITL терминал, где запущен make px4_sitl … весь вывод процесса симулятор Правило выбора: начинай с MAVLink Console; отладочный UART нужен только там, где MAVLink ещё не запущен — при зависании на загрузке и ошибках в загрузочных скриптах. Как это устроено. MAVLink-оболочка идёт сообщениями SERIAL_CONTROL id 126 с устройством SERIAL_CONTROL_DEV_SHELL = 10, по 70 байт в сообщении; это не MAV_CMD . На один экземпляр MAVLink — одна оболочка. Аргументы mavlink_shell.py : порт устройство ,бод , IP:порт для UDP, tcp:IP:порт ; без аргумента ищет последовательный порт сам и --baudrate / -b , по умолчанию 57600; нужны pymavlink и pyserial . SYS_USB_AUTO : 0 — USB выключен, 1 — автоопределение три подряд символа возврата каретки запускают nshterm на /dev/ttyACM0 , начало пакета u-blox — сквозной доступ к GPS , 2 — только MAVLink умолчание . Параметр требует перезагрузки. System console у fmu-v6x — USART3, 57600 бод nuttx-config/nsh/defconfig . Сообщения других модулей в MAVLink-оболочку не попадают. Их читают командой dmesg — это кольцевой буфер консоли на 4 КБ: старые строки вытесняются, поэтому загрузку смотрят сразу после неё. dmesg -f & оставляет вывод фоном. nsh и pxh: что есть и чего нет Набор команд задаёт сборка платы — файл boards/<производитель /<плата /default.px4board . Команда, которой нет в сборке, отвечает command not found . Команда px4/fmu-v6x SITL px4/sitl --- --- --- param , listener , uorb , work_queue , perf , ver есть есть actuator_test , tune_control , led_control , bsondump есть есть top , dmesg , reboot есть нет i2cdetect , nshterm , hardfault_log , mtd есть нет ls , cat , free , ps , df , cp , rm встроенные в nsh есть нет sd_bench нет есть у fmu-v6c есть failure нет есть shutdown , list_tasks , list_files нет есть Так во всех трёх релизах 1.15–1.17. Следствия: top в SITL не работает — загрузку там смотрят через listener cpuload и work_queue status ; failure на полётнике в штатной сборке нет px4-safety-return ; тест карты sd_bench на Pixhawk 6X требует своей сборки. Откуда берётся значение параметра У параметра три слоя src/lib/parameters/parameters.cpp , модуль получает значение верхнего непустого: 1. Умолчание прошивки — число из PARAM_DEFINE_ или module.yaml , вшито при сборке. 2. Умолчание запуска — то, что записали командой param set-default скрипты платы rc.board_defaults , airframe и config.txt . Живёт в RAM и собирается заново при каждой загрузке. 3. Сохранённое значение — всё, что записано через param set , QGC, калибровку или самим драйвером. {{diagram:px4-console-param-layers Значение параметра — верхний непустой слой из трёх; в хранилище уходит только то, что отличается от умолчания запуска, поэтому совпавшее с умолчанием airframe после обновления прошивки молча меняется.}} Пример: умолчание RTL_RETURN_ALT в прошивке — 60 м, rc.mc_defaults ставит мультиротору 30 м, оператор может записать своё. Главное правило хранения: при сохранении пишутся только значения третьего слоя, не равные умолчанию запуска param_export_internal . Записал RTL_RETURN_ALT = 30 на квадрокоптере — в файле этого нет. Отсюда правило px4-intro: после обновления прошивки всё, что совпадало с умолчанием, получает новое умолчание. Хранилище и автосохранение Формат хранилища — BSON: подряд идут записи «тип, имя, значение», целые как int32, вещественные как double. Куда пишется, зависит от платы: Плата Основное хранилище Копия --- --- --- fmu-v6x, fmu-v6c FRAM /fs/mtd_params /fs/microsd/parameters_backup.bson платы с CONFIG_BOARD_PARAM_FILE="/fs/microsd/params" например, Matek H743-Slim /fs/microsd/params /fs/microsd/parameters_backup.bson платы с FLASH_BASED_PARAMS семейство Kakute H7, SP Racing H7 Extreme внутренний flash MCU тот же файл, если есть SD Команды «сохранить» в обычной работе нет: любое изм

text: summary Всё, что подключается к полётнику с PX4 кроме моторов и приёмника: GPS и компас, дальномеры, датчик воздушной скорости, телеметрия и экземпляры MAVLink, DroneCAN, OSD, светодиод состояния и пищалка. У всего одна схема: выбрать порт параметром _CONFIG / _CFG или включить драйвер параметром SENS_EN_ , перезагрузить, проверить командой status и listener . Модуль даёт таблицы параметров PX4 1.17.0 с умолчаниями и отличиями от 1.15 и 1.16, номера портов fmu-v6x, правило расчёта потока MAVLink в байтах в секунду, расшифровку цветов LED и мелодий. Лабораторная — без железа и симулятора: раскладка восьми устройств по портам Pixhawk 6X, бюджет канала SiK на 57600 бод, расшифровка индикации и поиск ошибок в параметрах; ответы сверяются с эталоном на странице. theory Общая схема: параметр → перезагрузка → проверка В PX4 драйвер периферии не работает «сам». Его запускает скрипт при загрузке, и только если параметр это разрешил. Способов три. - UART. У драйвера есть параметр порта: GPS_1_CONFIG , MAV_1_CONFIG , SENS_TFMINI_CFG , MSP_OSD_CONFIG . Значение — номер порта из таблицы ниже, 0 — драйвер выключен. Скорость берётся из SER_<порт _BAUD . Сборка генерирует из этих описаний скрипт rc.serial : для каждого драйвера он читает параметр порта и запускает команду вида tfmini start -d /dev/ttyS1 . - I²C и SPI. Порт выбирать не нужно, драйвер включается параметром SENS_EN_<датчик . Скрипт rc.sensors проверяет параметр и запускает драйвер на внешней шине I²C ключ -X . - DroneCAN. Драйвер шины включается UAVCAN_ENABLE , типы принимаемых данных — UAVCAN_SUB_ . Почти все эти параметры помечены reboot_required : без перезагрузки ничего не изменится. Проверка всегда в два шага, в MAVLink Console QGC: 1. Драйвер запущен: gps status , tfmini status , mavlink status , uavcan status , msp_osd status , airspeed_selector status , sensors status . 2. Данные идут: listener <топик — sensor_gps , sensor_mag , distance_sensor , differential_pressure , airspeed_validated , telemetry_status . Второй экземпляр топика — ключ -i 1 . Что такое топик uORB и listener — модуль px4-architecture. {{diagram:px4-periph-enable-flow Параметр только разрешает запуск: драйвер стартует скриптом при загрузке, поэтому порядок всегда один — параметр, перезагрузка, status, listener.}} Один порт — один драйвер. Если два параметра указывают на один порт, скрипт отдаёт порт первому, а для второго печатает Conflicting config for /dev/ttyS… видно в dmesg и не запускает его. Кто окажется первым, зависит от порядка драйверов в сборке — рассчитывать на него нельзя. Драйвера может не быть в прошивке. Набор драйверов задаёт файл boards/<производитель /<плата /default.px4board . Если параметра нет в списке QGC — драйвер не собран; он добавляется своей сборкой make px4_fmu-v6x_default boardconfig . В таблицах ниже колонка «v6x» показывает, есть ли драйвер в стандартной прошивке Pixhawk 6X px4/fmu-v6x версии 1.17.0. Порты fmu-v6x Номера портов одинаковы для всех плат Tools/serial/generate_config.py , отличается только набор. Значение Имя в QGC Разъём Pixhawk 6X Устройство SER_ _BAUD , умолчание Занят по умолчанию --- --- --- --- --- --- 0 Disabled — — — — 101 TELEM 1 TELEM1 /dev/ttyS6 SER_TEL1_BAUD = 57600 MAV_0_CONFIG 102 TELEM 2 TELEM2 /dev/ttyS4 SER_TEL2_BAUD = 921600 — 103 TELEM 3 TELEM3 /dev/ttyS1 SER_TEL3_BAUD = 57600 — 201 GPS 1 GPS1 /dev/ttyS0 SER_GPS1_BAUD = 0 авто GPS_1_CONFIG 202 GPS 2 GPS2 /dev/ttyS7 SER_GPS2_BAUD = 0 авто — 300 Radio Controller линия PX4IO/RC /dev/ttyS5 SER_RC_BAUD = 0 в списке с 1.17; на плате с IO-процессором линию занимает px4io 401 EXT2 UART4 & I2C /dev/ttyS3 SER_EXT2_BAUD = 57600 — 1000 Ethernet ETH сеть, UDP — MAV_2_CONFIG Значение 1000 доступно только драйверам с сетевой поддержкой — MAVLink и uXRCE-DDS. SER_ _BAUD принимает фиксированный список скоростей от 50 до 3 000 000; 0 означает «авто» и годится только для драйверов, которые сами подбирают скорость GPS . {{diagram:px4-periph-ports-v6x На fmu-v6x шесть свободно назначаемых UART: два GPS, companion, радиомодем, дальномер и OSD занимают их все, а airspeed и ESC уходят на I²C и CAN.}} GPS Параметр Умолчание Значения --- --- --- GPS_1_CONFIG / GPS_2_CONFIG 201 / 0 порт основного и второго приёмника SER_GPS1_BAUD 0 авто: драйвер перебирает скорости сам GPS_1_PROTOCOL / GPS_2_PROTOCOL 1 0 авто дольше старт , 1 u-blox, 2 MTK, 3 Ashtech / Trimble, 4 Emlid Reach, 5 Femtomes, 6 NMEA GPS_1_GNSS / GPS_2_GNSS 0 маска: бит 0 GPS + QZSS, 1 SBAS, 2 Galileo, 3 BeiDou, 4 GLONASS, 5 NavIC; 0 — как настроен приёмник. Только u-blox GPS_UBX_DYNMODEL 7 2 stationary, 4 automotive, 6 airborne < 1 g, 7 airborne < 2 g, 8 airborne < 4 g GPS_SAT_INFO 0 1 — публиковать satellite_info GPS_CFG_WIPE 0 1 — стереть настройки во flash u-blox при загрузке с 1.17 SENS_GPS_MASK 7 смешивание двух приёмников: бит 0 — по точности скорости, 1 — горизонтальной позиции, 2 — высоты; 0 — без смешивания SENS_GPS_PRIME 0 основной экземпляр без смешивания: 0, 1; −1 — равный приоритет SENS_GPS_TAU 10 с 1…100 с: постоянная времени сглаживания сдвигов между приёмниками GPS_UBX_DYNMODEL по версиям. В 1.15 и 1.16 airframe мультиротора rc.mc_defaults ставил 6 — «airborne < 1 g». В 1.17 эта строка убрана, и мультиротор получает умолчание параметра 7. Самолёт во всех трёх версиях получает 8. Если летаешь на 1.16 и раньше, поставь 7 вручную: модель говорит фильтру приёмника, какой динамики ждать, а мультиротор легко превышает 1 g. Два приёмника. Каждый публикует свой sensor_gps экземпляры 0 и 1 , модуль sensors сводит их в vehicle_gps_position — его и читает EKF2. При ненулевой SENS_GPS_MASK и двух приёмниках с fix не хуже 2D решение смешивается. Для каждой включённой метрики вес приёмника обратно пропорционален квадрату его заявленной погрешности: для двух приёмников w₁ = σ₂² / σ₁² + σ₂² , где σ — eph , epv или точность скорости. Итоговый вес — среднее весов по включённым метрикам. Если приёмники не сообщают точность или один потерял fix, смешивание отключается и работает жёсткий выбор: SENS_GPS_PRIME , пока у н

title: PX4: подвес, триггер камеры и геотеги

Импульс сервы подвеса и ручка Шаг 2. Шаг и интервал съёмки Шаг 3. Ошибка геотега от задержки Шаг 4. Три нагрузки и три ошибки Переход на реальное железо
text: summary Параметры и проводка PX4 1.17.0 для подвеса и съёмочной камеры: что выбирают MNT_MODE_IN и MNT_MODE_OUT , как угол превращается в микросекунды через MNT_RANGE_ , MNT_OFF_ и MIN / MAX выхода, какие сообщения MAVLink Gimbal v2 прошивка принимает и шлёт, как работают TRIG_MODE , TRIG_INTERFACE , TRIG_DISTANCE , TRIG_MIN_INTERVA , что даёт обратная связь затвора CAM_CAP_FBACK и какие топики ULog несут время и координаты кадра. Общая теория подвесов — в payload-gimbal , расчёт GSD и перекрытий — в per-mapping ; здесь только сторона PX4. После модуля ты выбираешь схему подключения по типу подвеса и камеры, считаешь импульс сервы подвеса, шаг и интервал съёмки и ошибку геотега от задержки затвора. Лабораторная — без железа и симулятора: четыре расчёта и разбор фрагмента параметров с тремя ошибками, ответы сверяются с эталоном на странице. theory Что в модуле и как читать Модуль закрывает три подсистемы PX4: модуль gimbal подвес , драйвер camera_trigger спуск затвора и драйвер camera_capture обратная связь с горячего башмака , плюс то, что из них попадает в лог для геопривязки. Сначала идёт подвес: откуда берётся команда, куда она уходит, как считается импульс и как прошивка играет роль gimbal manager. Потом камера: режимы и интерфейсы триггера, съёмка по дистанции, обратная связь и геотеги. В конце — две таблицы выбора и отличия 1.15 / 1.16 / 1.17. Роли manager / device и сами сообщения протокола разобраны в payload-gimbal и mav-services , GSD и перекрытия — в per-mapping : здесь на них только ссылки. Три модуля и условия запуска Все три модуля входят в сборки px4_fmu-v6x_default и px4_fmu-v6c_default CONFIG_MODULES_GIMBAL , CONFIG_DRIVERS_CAMERA_TRIGGER , CONFIG_DRIVERS_CAMERA_CAPTURE , CONFIG_MODULES_CAMERA_FEEDBACK в default.px4board , но стартовый скрипт rcS запускает их по параметрам: Модуль Условие в rcS Что делает --- --- --- gimbal MNT_MODE_IN −1 принимает команды, считает углы, выдаёт их на выход camera_trigger и camera_feedback TRIG_MODE 0 спускает затвор; публикует camera_trigger и camera_capture camera_capture CAM_CAP_FBACK 0 ловит фронт с башмака, публикует camera_trigger с feedback = true По умолчанию MNT_MODE_IN = −1 и TRIG_MODE = 0: ни подвес, ни триггер не работают, а gimbal status в консоли px4-console-params отвечает «not running». MNT_MODE_IN , MNT_MODE_OUT и все TRIG_ и CAM_CAP_ читаются при старте: меняешь — перезагружай плату. Остальные MNT_ модуль перечитывает на ходу. camera_feedback стартует только вместе с триггером: обратная связь без TRIG_MODE 0 топик camera_capture не наполнит. Источник команд: MNT_MODE_IN Значение Источник Когда выбирать --- --- --- −1 выключено по умолчанию подвеса нет 0 Auto: пульт и MAVLink Gimbal v2 вместе пульт у пилота плюс наземка или миссия 1 только пульт каналы AUX простой сервоподвес, без наземки и миссий 2 только ROI протокол v1, устаревает не выбирать в новых проектах 3 только DO_MOUNT_CONTROL v1, устаревает не выбирать в новых проектах 4 только MAVLink Gimbal v2 управление из наземки, миссии или companion, пульт подвесом не рулит Правило: нужен пульт и что-то ещё — 0; только пульт — 1; только программное управление — 4. В режиме 1 команды миссии и ROI подвес не двигают. В режиме 0 управляет тот, чьё обновление пришло последним; чтобы пульт случайно не перехватил подвес, ему нужен «большой ход»: канал должен сдвинуться больше чем на 0.25 по шкале −1…+1 одна восьмая полного хода, 12.5 % от последнего принятого значения, по любой из трёх осей. После такого хода primary control переходит к автопилоту, и поток GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_ATTITUDE от наземки игнорируется, пока она не заберёт управление командой DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE . Деталь из кода: флаг MAV_PROTOCOL_CAPABILITY_COMPONENT_IMPLEMENTS_GIMBAL_MANAGER в AUTOPILOT_VERSION выставляется только при MNT_MODE_IN = 4, при 0 его нет. Как на это реагирует конкретная наземная станция — в дереве PX4 не видно не проверено . Куда уходит команда: MNT_MODE_OUT Значение Выход Что считает PX4 --- --- --- 0 AUX: до трёх выходов PWM с функциями Gimbal Roll / Pitch / Yaw углы, стабилизацию MNT_DO_STAB , ограничения, пересчёт в −1…+1 1 MAVLink v1: COMMAND_LONG DO_MOUNT_CONTROL на MNT_MAV_SYSID / MNT_MAV_COMPID углы в градусах, к ним прибавлены MNT_OFF_ 2 MAVLink Gimbal v2: GIMBAL_DEVICE_SET_ATTITUDE ничего: кватернион, скорости и флаги lock уходят устройству как есть Функции выходов — в output_functions.yaml : Gimbal Roll 420, Gimbal Pitch 421, Gimbal Yaw 422. Они назначаются на экране Actuators, как любая серва; группы таймеров, 50 Гц и питание серв — в px4-outputs-servos . Следствия, которые легко пропустить: - MNT_RANGE_ , MNT_OFF_ , MNT_DO_STAB , MNT_LND_P_MIN/MAX для выхода v2 не применяются : функция расчёта углов для него не вызывается. Пределы и стабилизация — дело самого подвеса. - MNT_MAV_SYSID и MNT_MAV_COMPID читает только выход v1. В v2 адрес устройства берётся из принятого GIMBAL_DEVICE_INFORMATION : compid отправителя, system id — свой MAV_SYS_ID . Описание MNT_MAV_COMPID в справочнике параметров упоминает v2, но код его там не использует. - Пока GIMBAL_DEVICE_INFORMATION не получено, выход v2 раз в секунду запрашивает его через MAV_CMD_REQUEST_MESSAGE , а в остальных циклах продолжает слать GIMBAL_DEVICE_SET_ATTITUDE с id устройства 0 без адреса компонента; gimbal/output_mavlink.cpp , v1.17.0 — подвес, который ждёт сообщения на свой компонент, их не выполнит. В gimbal status это строка «gimbal device compid not found». - Порт MAVLink-подвеса: MAV_n_CONFIG = номер порта, MAV_n_MODE = 10 Gimbal . В этом наборе PX4 шлёт GIMBAL_DEVICE_SET_ATTITUDE и AUTOPILOT_STATE_FOR_GIMBAL_DEVICE по 20 Гц, а принимает только HEARTBEAT , GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_ATTITUDE , GIMBAL_MANAGER_SET_MANUAL_CONTROL , GIMBAL_DEVICE_INFORMATION и GIMBAL_DEVICE_ATTITUDE_STATUS . Номера портов — в px4-hardware-peripherals . Управление с пульта MNT_MAN_ROLL , MNT_MAN_PITCH , MNT_MAN_YAW 0 — выключено, 1…6 — AUX1…AUX6 выбирают поле aux1…aux6 топика manual_control_setpoint . Само поле наполняет RC_MAP_AUXn — номер кан

text: summary Самолёт и VTOL на PX4 1.17.0 от выбора airframe до первого перехода — в порядке тех же 17 шагов, что и мультиротор в px4-setup-scratch , но с тем, чего у мультиротора нет: огибающая скоростей FW_AIRSPD_ и её связь со сваливанием, газ и углы TECS, rate-контур крыла с масштабом по скорости, взлёт с руки и с полосы, посадочная схема миссии, автотюн самолёта, переход вперёд и назад так, как его реализует vtol_att_control условия завершения, работа без датчика скорости, таймауты , и quad-chute — с точными условиями срабатывания из исходника и тем, что после него делает аппарат. Каждое число, которое приходится выбирать, идёт с правилом выбора. Практика без железа и симулятора: огибающая из массы, площади и C_Lmax, хронология перехода по таблице скорости, знаки рулей и поиск трёх ошибок в файле параметров; ответы сверяются с эталоном на странице. theory Что в модуле и в каком порядке читать Сначала — чем путь самолёта и VTOL отличается от мультиротора на 17 шагах и какой airframe выбрать. Потом самолётная часть: модули контура, огибающая скоростей, газ и углы, rate-контур, полёт без датчика скорости, взлёт, посадка, автотюн. Потом VTOL: переход вперёд, переход назад, особенности tiltrotor и tailsitter, quad-chute, висение. В конце — таблица первых значений с правилами и соответствие понятий ArduPlane. Выходы, сервы и знаки поверхностей разобраны в px4-outputs-servos , датчик скорости — в px4-hardware-peripherals , failsafe и Return — в px4-safety-return , тумблер перехода — в px4-rc-tuning ; здесь они не повторяются, а только используются. 17 шагов: что меняется у самолёта и VTOL Порядок тот же, что в px4-setup-scratch там же прошивка, приёмник, калибровка питания . title: PX4 control loops and tuning
summary: Multirotor control in PX4 is a cascade of three loops: position → attitude → angular rate, plus the distribution of torques across the motors. This module explains which parameter belongs to which loop, how the forms of the rate controller differ (a K multiplier versus a plain P), what manual tuning

Allocation first Step 2. Filters from the log Step 3. Autotune Step 4. Verification What you should get and what to write down Lab
text: summary Multirotor control in PX4 is a cascade of three loops: position → attitude → angular rate, plus the distribution of torques across the motors. This module explains which parameter belongs to which loop, how the forms of the rate controller differ a K multiplier versus a plain P , what manual tuning from the step response looks like, and why for most frames the right answer is autotune. For those coming from Betaflight — a mapping table. theory The cascade 1. Position controller MPC_ : the position error gives the desired velocity MPC_XY_P , MPC_Z_P , the velocity error gives the desired acceleration/tilt MPC_XY_VEL_P_ACC and others . The hover throttle MPC_THR_HOVER and the speed limits MPC_XY_VEL_MAX , MPC_Z_VEL_MAX_UP/DN also live here. 2. Attitude controller MC_ROLL_P , MC_PITCH_P , MC_YAW_P : the angle error gives the desired angular rate. P only. 3. Rate controller MC_ROLLRATE_P/I/D/K , the same for PITCH and YAW, plus MC_ RATE_FF : the angular-rate error gives a torque. The fastest loop; it defines how the vehicle “feels”. 4. Control allocation : torques and thrust → motor commands according to the geometry CA_AIRFRAME , CA_ROTOR_COUNT , CA_ROTOR<n _PX/PY/KM . The form of the rate controller PX4 uses a parallel form with a common multiplier K: output = K × P·e + I·∫e + D·de/dt . MC_ROLLRATE_K scales all three at once, so the first step of coarse tuning is K, not P. Betaflight has no such multiplier; in the sliders its role is played by the Master Multiplier. Mapping from Betaflight Betaflight PX4 --- --- P/I/D roll rate MC_ROLLRATE_P/I/D × MC_ROLLRATE_K Feedforward MC_ROLLRATE_FF Angle mode strength MC_ROLL_P Gyro filters IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF , IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF , notch IMU_GYRO_NF _FRQ Throttle hover / air mode MPC_THR_HOVER , MC_AIRMODE Autotune For most frames the documentation explicitly recommends autotune: it is faster and usually gives a good result. It identifies the model from the responses in hover and applies the rate gains it found; applying is controlled by MC_AT_APPLY immediately, after landing or manually . Manual tuning is for when autotune can't cope: non-standard frames, heavy vibration, large vehicles. Manual tuning from the step response The order: filters → rate K, then D, then I → attitude P → position. A step: Acro or Stabilized, sharp short stick movements, a log, a plot of vehicle_rates_setpoint versus vehicle_angular_velocity in Flight Review. Overshoot — lower K or more D; slow response — more K; drift — more I. The same method and the same metrics as in the module on data-driven PID. Defaults and what they mean MC_ROLLRATE_P = 0.15, I = 0.2, D = 0.003, K = 1.0, FF = 0 the output is a dimensionless torque per 1 rad/s of error ; MC_ROLL_P = 4.0 angular rate per radian of angle error → 1/s; the default since PX4 1.17, 6.5 up to 1.16 , MC_YAW_P = 2.8; position: MPC_XY_P = 0.95 1/s , velocity → acceleration MPC_XY_VEL_P_ACC = 1.8, I_ACC = 0.4, D_ACC = 0.2; MPC_Z_P = 1.0. The hover throttle MPC_THR_HOVER = 0.5 normalized — refined by the hover thrust estimator HTE_ . Filters: IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF = 40 Hz, IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF = 20 Hz, the static notch IMU_GYRO_NF0_FRQ / BW 0 = off, BW 20 Hz , the dynamic one by ESC RPM IMU_GYRO_DNF_EN a bitmask: bit 0 — by ESC RPM, bit 1 — by the onboard FFT IMU_GYRO_FFT_EN , IMU_GYRO_DNF_MIN = 25 Hz. Air mode MC_AIRMODE 0 off, 1 roll/pitch, 2 + yaw . Units matter: the error is in rad/s, the output is a fraction of the maximum torque. P = 0.15 means an error of 1 rad/s 57°/s gives 15% of the torque. Comparison with Betaflight dimensionless “45” is only qualitative, via the module “Control theory” ζ, phase margin . Autotune in more detail MC_AT_EN = 1 enables the mc_autotune_attitude_control module; it is started from QGC PID Tuning → Autotune in Altitude/Position while hovering in calm air; the module injects an excitation with amplitude MC_AT_SYSID_AMP 0.7 on each axis, identifies the model of the rate loop and computes the gains; MC_AT_APPLY 0 — don't apply, 1 — after landing, 2 — immediately in flight — the default is 1. Afterwards — a check flight and Flight Review: a response with no overshoot 10%, D without noise. Autotune doesn't tune the filters and doesn't cure vibration — those are done before spectrum! . Worked example: 7" 6S, 1.4 kg Start: airframe Generic Quad, CA_ROTOR_COUNT = 4, IMU_GYRO_RATEMAX 400 → 800 Hz H7 , IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF 40 → 80, IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF 20 → 40 default 20 since 1.17, 30 up to 1.16 ; eRPM over DShot bidirectional DShot or ESC telemetry over UART — DSHOT_TEL_CFG , IMU_GYRO_DNF_EN = 1; MPC_THR_HOVER will be refined by the HTE estimator; first flight in Stabilized — MC_ROLLRATE_K 1.0 → 0.7 if it wobbles; autotune; MPC_XY_VEL_MAX to suit the task. Log → Flight Review: rate tracking, spectrum, vehicle_torque_setpoint without saturation. {{diagram:px4-cascade The PX4 cascade: position → velocity → attitude → angular rate → allocator, with the parameters of each level.}} practice Step 1. Allocation first Props off: Actuators in QGC — the geometry matches the frame, and in the test each motor spins in the right direction. Step 2. Filters from the log A flight with logging, Flight Review → gyro spectrogram. Set IMU_GYRO_CUTOFF and IMU_DGYRO_CUTOFF so that they cut motor noise without touching the control band. Step 3. Autotune QGC → PID Tuning → Autotune, or a switch assigned to the autotune function. Hover, start, don't touch the sticks until it finishes, land. Check that the new MC_ RATE_ were applied. Step 4. Verification Step response in Flight Review before and after: overshoot and settling time. If needed — manual adjustment of K/D by 10–20%. What you should get and what to write down - Step 1. In QGC → Actuators the frame diagram matches the real one, and the test for each motor spins exactly that motor and in the direction shown in the picture. summary: In PX4 you can expose uORB topics directly to ROS 2: the uXRCE-DDS client on the flight controller and the agent on the companion computer pass messages in both directions. This gives ROS nodes access to attitude, position and commands without a MAVLink wrapper. This module shows how to bring up the
headings: The uXRCE-DDS bridge Offboard: three messages Versus MAVLink/MAVSDK Setting up the bridge on a real aircraft Coordinate frames — the main source of bugs A minimal offboard node (Python, rclpy) Step 1. Environment Step 2. SITL with the client Step 3. The offboard example Step 4. Your own node Lab
text: summary In PX4 you can expose uORB topics directly to ROS 2: the uXRCE-DDS client on the flight controller and the agent on the companion computer pass messages in both directions. This gives ROS nodes access to attitude, position and commands without a MAVLink wrapper. This module shows how to bring up the bridge in SITL, what px4_msgs is, how offboard control works OffboardControlMode + TrajectorySetpoint + VehicleCommand and why PX4 kicks you out of Offboard if you go quiet. theory The uXRCE-DDS bridge - The client uxrce_dds_client in PX4 publishes/subscribes to a limited set of uORB topics the list is dds_topics.yaml . - The agent MicroXRCEAgent on the companion or a PC receives them over UDP or serial and exposes them in DDS — that is, in ROS 2. - On the ROS 2 side the messages come from the px4_msgs package; the px4_msgs branch must match the PX4 version , otherwise the definitions don't match. For mismatched versions there is a message translation node. The topics show up in ROS 2 as /fmu/out/ from PX4 and /fmu/in/ to PX4 . Offboard: three messages 1. OffboardControlMode — tells PX4 what you control position, velocity, acceleration, attitude, rates . It must be streamed before switching to Offboard and the whole time you are in it; below ~2 Hz PX4 exits Offboard. 2. TrajectorySetpoint — the target itself: position/velocity in NED Z points down! , yaw. 3. VehicleCommand — commands: change mode VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE , Offboard = base 1, custom 6 , arm VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM . The acknowledgment is VehicleCommandAck . Same philosophy as GUIDED in ArduPilot: the companion gives advice as a stream, the autopilot watches the timeout, and the pilot can always take over. Versus MAVLink/MAVSDK MAVLink via MAVSDK is simpler for simple tasks and doesn't require ROS. uXRCE-DDS is for when you need the ROS ecosystem navigation, vision, planning , low latency and access to internal topics. Setting up the bridge on a real aircraft PX4: UXRCE_DDS_CFG = TELEM2 port , SER_TEL2_BAUD = 921600; on the companion: MicroXRCEAgent serial --dev /dev/ttyTHS1 -b 921600 Jetson or udp4 -p 8888 for SITL/Wi-Fi. Check: ros2 topic list grep fmu , ros2 topic hz /fmu/out/vehicle_odometry expect tens to hundreds of Hz . If there are no topics: the port is taken by MAVLink MAV_1_CONFIG on the same TELEM2 — a conflict , the baud rate, uxrce_dds_client status in the PX4 console. Coordinate frames — the main source of bugs PX4 works in NED north-east-down and FRD forward-right-down ; ROS 2 REP-103 uses ENU and FLU. TrajectorySetpoint.position = x, y, z is NED: z = −10 means 10 m up. Conversions: ENU→NED: x, y, z → y, x, −z ; FLU→FRD: x, y, z → x, −y, −z . The px4_ros_com package has conversion utilities; MAVROS does it for you. A sign error in z is the classic “the vehicle dove into the ground on takeoff in the simulator”. A minimal offboard node Python, rclpy python import rclpy from rclpy.node import Node from px4_msgs.msg import OffboardControlMode, TrajectorySetpoint, VehicleCommand from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy, HistoryPolicy, DurabilityPolicy class Offboard Node : def __init__ self : super .__init__ "offboard_min" qos = QoSProfile reliability=ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT, durability=DurabilityPolicy.TRANSIENT_LOCAL, history=HistoryPolicy.KEEP_LAST, depth=1 PX4 publishes best-effort self.mode_pub = self.create_publisher OffboardControlMode, "/fmu/in/offboard_control_mode", qos self.sp_pub = self.create_publisher TrajectorySetpoint, "/fmu/in/trajectory_setpoint", qos self.cmd_pub = self.create_publisher VehicleCommand, "/fmu/in/vehicle_command", qos self.n = 0 self.create_timer 0.1, self.step 10 Hz 2 Hz minimum def cmd self, command, p1=0.0, p2=0.0 : m = VehicleCommand command=command, param1=p1, param2=p2, target_system=1, target_component=1, source_system=1, source_component=1, from_external=True, timestamp=int self.get_clock .now .nanoseconds / 1000 self.cmd_pub.publish m def step self : now = int self.get_clock .now .nanoseconds / 1000 self.mode_pub.publish OffboardControlMode position=True, timestamp=now self.sp_pub.publish TrajectorySetpoint position= 0.0, 0.0, -5.0 , yaw=0.0, timestamp=now 5 m up NED if self.n == 10: after 1 s of setpoints self.cmd VehicleCommand.VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE, 1.0, 6.0 Offboard self.cmd VehicleCommand.VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM, 1.0 self.n += 1 rclpy.init ; rclpy.spin Offboard The safeguards from the “Tracking” module limits, watchdog, the COM_OF_LOSS_T = 1 s timeout and the COM_OBL_RC_ACT action are mandatory here too. {{diagram:px4-offboard-seq Offboard from ROS 2: a stream of OffboardControlMode and TrajectorySetpoint before the mode switch, then the mode and arm commands; on a link loss — failsafe.}} practice Step 1. Environment ROS 2 Jazzy Ubuntu 24.04 installed and sourced; fallback option is Humble 22.04 mkdir -p ~/ws_px4/src && cd ~/ws_px4/src git clone https://github.com/PX4/px4_msgs.git branch matching your PX4 version git clone https://github.com/PX4/px4_ros_com.git cd .. && colcon build && source install/setup.bash Agent: MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 build from source or snap — see the documentation . Step 2. SITL with the client make px4_sitl gz_x500 — in SITL the uXRCE-DDS client starts on its own and looks for the agent on 8888. Check: ros2 topic list shows /fmu/out/vehicle_attitude and others; ros2 topic echo /fmu/out/vehicle_local_position since PX4 1.17 — /fmu/out/vehicle_local_position_v1 . Step 3. The offboard example Run the example from px4_ros_com offboard control : the node sends OffboardControlMode + TrajectorySetpoint for 10 cycles, then switches mode and arms via VehicleCommand , and after that holds a point at 5 m. Read the code: the order “stream first, then mode” is the key. Step 4. Your own node Write a Python node rclpy that holds a quadcopter at 3 m altitude and every 10 s moves the target around a circle of 5 m radius. Check: stop the node — after ~1 s COM_OF_LOSS_T , 1 s by default PX4 exits Offboard in SITL

This module puts the whole setup together: roles and the boundary of responsibility, power and heat, the physical connection to TELEM2, how to **find** the right UART on your JetPack version (the d
headings: Roles and the boundary Which Jetson and which OS Power and heat Physical connection Two communication channels Worked example: the latency budget Step 1. Prepare the Jetson Step 2. Find “your” UART with a loopback Step 3. The MAVLink channel Step 4. The uXRCE-DDS channel Step 5. Start the agent automatically Step 6. Heat under load
text: summary Jetson Orin Nano/NX is the standard companion computer for vision on PX4: CUDA and TensorRT in 7–25 W. This module puts the whole setup together: roles and the boundary of responsibility, power and heat, the physical connection to TELEM2, how to find the right UART on your JetPack version the device name differs between versions , the two communication channels — MAVLink and uXRCE-DDS — with the PX4 parameters and how to verify them, starting the agent automatically with systemd, and the latency budget of the “camera → command” chain. The first-generation Jetson Nano is no longer supported JetPack 4, Ubuntu 18.04 — don't pick it for new projects. theory Roles and the boundary Pixhawk PX4 — stabilization, EKF, failsafe, missions; Jetson — vision, planning, ROS 2, networking. The boundary is the same as in the module “Companion: role and boundaries”: without the Jetson the vehicle must still fly and return, and loss of the companion in offboard is handled by the PX4 failsafe COM_OF_LOSS_T , COM_OBL_RC_ACT , not by hope. Which Jetson and which OS Board What it gives you OS --- --- --- Orin Nano 4/8 GB the main choice for detection and tracking; 7–25 W modes nvpmodel JetPack 6 Ubuntu 22.04 → ROS 2 Humble or JetPack 7 Ubuntu 24.04 → ROS 2 Jazzy Orin NX 8/16 GB 2× the compute, the same module form factor the same Jetson Nano 2019 no longer supported, JetPack 4 not for new projects The JetPack version determines the Ubuntu version, and therefore the ROS 2 distribution: installing ROS 2 on the “wrong” Ubuntu is the road to building from source and endless dependency problems. Power and heat - The Jetson gets a separate BEC or DC-DC from the power bus with current headroom, not power from the flight controller; common ground with the Pixhawk. - Power mode: sudo nvpmodel -q shows the current one, nvpmodel -m <N switches it; jetson_clocks locks the clocks stable latency at the cost of energy . - Heat: in a closed enclosure without airflow the Orin throttles after a few minutes, and detection latency doubles module “ML on board” . A heatsink with a fan or prop wash airflow, and tegrastats in the flight log. Physical connection - UART recommended for flight : Pixhawk TELEM2 — TX, RX, GND; Jetson — pins 8 TX and 10 RX of the 40-pin header, ground on pin 6. TX↔RX crossed. 3.3 V logic on both sides; do not connect the 5 V from the TELEM2 connector to the Jetson . - The device name depends on the board and JetPack : on Orin this UART can be /dev/ttyTHS0 or /dev/ttyTHS1 , on the old Nano it is /dev/ttyTHS1 ; the Orin debug console is /dev/ttyTCU0 . Don't trust an article — check with a loopback practice, step 2 . - Ethernet Pixhawk 6X, 6X Pro, etc. : MAVLink and uXRCE-DDS over UDP, without the UART speed limit — the best option if you have it. - USB — for the bench; in flight a USB connection is unreliable: connector vibration and re-enumeration drop the link. Two communication channels 1. MAVLink MAVSDK, pymavlink, MAVROS : MAV_1_CONFIG = TELEM2 , MAV_1_MODE = Onboard the stream set for a companion , SER_TEL2_BAUD = 921600 . Pro: it's a standard, the same code works with ArduPilot; con: a limited set of data and rates. 2. uXRCE-DDS : UXRCE_DDS_CFG = TELEM2 , the same baud rate, MAVLink disabled on this port MAV_1_CONFIG = Disabled or moved to another port . On the Jetson — MicroXRCEAgent serial --dev <port -b 921600 ; the topics /fmu/out/ , /fmu/in/ from px4_msgs of the same version as the firmware since 1.16 messages are versioned, some topics have a _v1 suffix . Pro: PX4's internal topics with low latency; con: PX4 only, the versions must match. Only one thing lives on one port. If you need both — MAVLink on TELEM1/USB/Ethernet, DDS on TELEM2. Worked example: the latency budget CSI camera at 60 fps up to 16 ms until a frame is ready → TensorRT YOLO-nano FP16 ~12 ms → tracker 2 ms → DDS over UART at 921600 ~2 ms → PX4 velocity controller time constant ~0.5 s . The pure delay is ~35 ms: a tracking loop with Kp ≈ 1 1/s is stable with margin module “Tracking” . A USB camera with MJPEG adds 40–80 ms, a Wi-Fi bridge instead of a wire adds 20–50 ms with jitter; two such “small things” eat the whole margin. Hence the rule: CSI and a wire, not USB and radio. {{diagram:px4-jetson-link PX4 and Jetson: the camera is on the Jetson, the link to the flight controller is over TELEM2 via MAVLink or uXRCE-DDS.}} practice Step 1. Prepare the Jetson bash sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER access to serial ports log out and in systemctl status nvgetty on boards where the header UART is a console, stop it: sudo systemctl disable --now nvgetty sudo nvpmodel -q current power mode Step 2. Find “your” UART with a loopback A jumper between pins 8 and 10, the Pixhawk not connected. For each candidate: python import serial, sys for dev in "/dev/ttyTHS0", "/dev/ttyTHS1" : try: with serial.Serial dev, 921600, timeout=0.2 as s: s.reset_input_buffer ; s.write b"loopback-test\n" print dev, "OK" if s.readline == b"loopback-test\n" else "no echo" except serial.SerialException as e: print dev, "error:", e Exactly one port should answer OK — that is pins 8/10 on your system. “Permission denied” — the dialout group or a console on the port; “no echo” on both — wrong pins or the UART is disabled in the device tree Jetson-IO: sudo /opt/nvidia/jetson-io/jetson-io.py . Step 3. The MAVLink channel PX4 parameters in QGC: MAV_1_CONFIG = TELEM 2 , MAV_1_MODE = Onboard , SER_TEL2_BAUD = 921600 , reboot. Remove the jumper, connect TX/RX/GND. Check: python from pymavlink import mavutil m = mavutil.mavlink_connection "/dev/ttyTHS1", baud=921600 your port from step 2 m.wait_heartbeat ; print "sys", m.target_system, "comp", m.target_component import time, collections cnt, t0 = collections.Counter , time.time while time.time - t0 < 10: msg = m.recv_match type= "ATTITUDE", "LOCAL_POSITION_NED" , blocking=True, timeout=1 if msg: cnt msg.get_type += 1 print {k: v / 10 for k, v in cnt.items }, "Hz" Write down the rates of ATTITUDE and LOCAL_POSITION_NED.

title: Vectors, matrices and rotations: the language of attitude
summary: Everything the autopilot says about attitude — the angles on the OSD, the quaternion in `ATT`/`AHRS`, the gravity vector in body axes, “where the camera is pointing” — comes down to a handful of linear algebra operations. This module gives you exactly those: a vector as an arrow and as a column of n
headings: A vector: an arrow and numbers Dot and cross products The rotation matrix Composition: order matters Euler angles and their singularity The quaternion Small rotations and the attitude derivative Coordinate frames to know by heart Step 1. The `rot.py` library Step 2. Gravity in body axes Step 3. Non-commutativity Step 4. Gyro integration
text: summary Everything the autopilot says about attitude — the angles on the OSD, the quaternion in ATT / AHRS , the gravity vector in body axes, “where the camera is pointing” — comes down to a handful of linear algebra operations. This module gives you exactly those: a vector as an arrow and as a column of numbers, the dot and cross products, a rotation matrix as “where the axes went”, composing rotations and why order matters, Euler angles and their singularity, the quaternion as a compact, singularity-free form of the same rotation, small rotations and the attitude derivative, and finally — the four coordinate frames people mix up most often NED/FRD in ArduPilot and PX4, ENU/FLU in ROS . Lab: a rot.py library of 14 functions, checked against scipy.spatial.transform . Not sure you need this elective? Take the 10-problem entry test ../pages/prerequisites.html . theory A vector: an arrow and numbers A vector is an arrow direction and length , and a column of numbers is its coordinates in a chosen basis . The same arrow “down toward the center of the Earth” is written as 0, 0, 9.81 in the NED basis, and as 0, 4.9, 8.5 in the axes of a vehicle rolled 30°. That's why every vector in code should be labeled with the axes it's expressed in: g_ned , a_body . Most attitude bugs are a vector in one basis used as if it were in another. Length: v = √ v·v . Unit vector: v/ v . A basis is three mutually perpendicular unit vectors; it's right-handed if x × y = z thumb x, index finger y, middle finger z of your right hand . Dot and cross products The dot product a·b = a b cos θ = aₓbₓ + a_yb_y + a_zb_z. It's “how much of a lies along b”. Uses: projecting thrust onto the vertical T·ẑ , the angle between vectors, checking perpendicularity = 0 . The vehicle's tilt from vertical: cos θ = g_body· 0,0,1 / g_body . The cross product a × b is a vector perpendicular to both, with length a b sin θ and direction by the right-hand rule. Components: a_yb_z − a_zb_y, a_zbₓ − aₓb_z, aₓb_y − a_yb_x . Uses: torque M = r × F lever arm times force — this is exactly how motor torques are computed in the mixer , the velocity of a point v = ω × r, the normal to a plane. It's anticommutative: b × a = − a × b . The rotation matrix A rotation is a linear transformation that preserves lengths and angles. Its matrix R 3×3 has these properties: Rᵀ R = I the columns are orthonormal , det R = +1. The set of such matrices is the group SO 3 . The most useful reading: the columns of R are the axes of the rotated basis, written in the original one . If R_nb takes you from body to NED v_ned = R_nb · v_body , then the first column of R_nb is where the vehicle's nose points in NED coordinates. The inverse rotation is the transpose: R⁻¹ = Rᵀ. So v_body = R_nbᵀ · v_ned, and there should be no matrix inversions in attitude code at all. Elementary rotations about the axes angle φ, right-hand rule — a positive rotation is counterclockwise when viewed from the tip of the axis : Rx φ = 1, 0, 0 , 0, cos φ, −sin φ , 0, sin φ, cos φ Ry θ = cos θ, 0, sin θ , 0, 1, 0 , −sin θ, 0, cos θ Rz ψ = cos ψ, −sin ψ, 0 , sin ψ, cos ψ, 0 , 0, 0, 1 Composition: order matters Rotations don't commute: Rx 90° ·Ry 90° ≠ Ry 90° ·Rx 90° — check it with a cube or in the lab. The rule for reading a product R = A·B·v: B is applied to the vector first, then A. The aerospace Euler angle sequence “yaw → pitch → roll” ZYX gives the matrix from body to NED: R_nb = Rz ψ · Ry θ · Rx φ Read it like this: a vector in body axes is first “unwound” in roll, then in pitch, then in yaw — and you get it in NED. In ArduPilot code this is Matrix3f::from_euler roll, pitch, yaw , in PX4 — matrix::Dcmf matrix::Eulerf ... . {{diagram:frames-rotations Coordinate frames: NED and FRD ArduPilot, PX4 versus ENU and FLU ROS . The same vehicle, different axis labels — and different signs for “up”.}} Euler angles and their singularity The angles roll φ, pitch θ, yaw ψ are convenient for humans and useless as an internal representation: at θ = ±90° the roll and yaw axes coincide gimbal lock , and you can't uniquely recover φ and ψ from the matrix — only their sum or difference. Ranges: φ ∈ −180°, 180° , θ ∈ −90°, 90° , ψ ∈ −180°, 180° the OSD usually shows heading as 0–360° . Extracting them from the matrix: θ = −asin R₃₁ , φ = atan2 R₃₂, R₃₃ , ψ = atan2 R₂₁, R₁₁ — atan2 , not atan , or you'll lose the quadrant. For aerobatics, a wing in vertical hover and any state estimation, Euler angles are not used inside the filter. The quaternion A quaternion q = w, x, y, z = cos α/2 , n ·sin α/2 encodes a rotation by angle α about the unit axis n . Four numbers instead of nine, one normalization instead of six orthogonality conditions, and no singularity. Operations: - The conjugate q = w, −x, −y, −z is the inverse rotation for a unit quaternion . - The product q₁ ⊗ q₂ is the composition of rotations q₂ first, then q₁, like with matrices, under the Hamilton convention : w = w₁w₂ − x₁x₂ − y₁y₂ − z₁z₂; x = w₁x₂ + x₁w₂ + y₁z₂ − z₁y₂; y = w₁y₂ − x₁z₂ + y₁w₂ + z₁x₂; z = w₁z₂ + x₁y₂ − y₁x₂ + z₁w₂. - Rotating a vector: v' = q ⊗ 0, v ⊗ q . In practice it's faster through the matrix: R q with elements R₁₁ = 1 − 2 y² + z² , R₁₂ = 2 xy − wz , R₁₃ = 2 xz + wy and so on. - q and −q are the same rotation double cover . That's why you look at the sign of the dot product when comparing and interpolating quaternions. - Normalize after every update, otherwise rounding errors accumulate and the “rotation” starts to scale. ArduPilot stores attitude in the EKF as a quaternion Quaternion in AP_Math , in the log — XKQ ; PX4 — vehicle_attitude.q in w, x, y, z order. ROS 2 geometry_msgs/Quaternion uses x, y, z, w order. A swapped order is a classic companion integration bug. Small rotations and the attitude derivative For a small angle δ: sin δ ≈ δ, cos δ ≈ 1, and a rotation by the vector δ = δₓ, δ_y, δ_z is approximated as R ≈ I + δ ₓ, where δ ₓ is the skew-symmetric cross-product matrix. title: Differential equations and dynamics: from the motor to the loop
summary: PID tuning “by eye” ends where understanding *what exactly* you are tuning begins. This module gives you the minimal toolkit: the first-order equation and the time constant (motor, filter, delay mixed with inertia), the second-order equation and its three regimes (overdamped, critically damped, unde
headings: The first-order equation The second-order equation Poles: the address of behavior The transfer function Discretization: formulas for firmware Delay versus inertia Step 1. One axis with a PID in numpy Step 2. Motor τ from a log Step 3. Discretization
text: summary PID tuning “by eye” ends where understanding what exactly you are tuning begins. This module gives you the minimal toolkit: the first-order equation and the time constant motor, filter, delay mixed with inertia , the second-order equation and its three regimes overdamped, critically damped, underdamped , poles as the “address” of a system's behavior on the complex plane, the transfer function as a way to assemble blocks by multiplication, and — the thing without which no formula ever makes it into firmware — discretization: Euler, Tustin, what you lose at a 1/8000 s step and at 1/50 s. Lab: a numerical model of one quadcopter axis with a PID, which you will compare with the pid-sim widget and with a real motor response from a log. theory The first-order equation The most common model in a drone: τ·ẋ + x = K·u. This is how motor thrust responds to an ESC command, and how an RC filter output, temperature or a capacitor's charge behave. The solution for a step input u = 1 from zero: x t = K· 1 − e^ −t/τ . In time τ the output covers 63 % of the way, in 3τ — 95 %, in 5τ — 99 %. The time constant τ is the only dynamics parameter; it's also called “motor delay”, although it isn't a delay but inertia: the motor starts responding immediately, just smoothly. How to find τ from a log: on a command step, find the moment where the response reaches 63 % of the steady-state value. For a 5" motor with a prop τ ≈ 15–30 ms, for a 15" — 80–150 ms. It's τ that limits how “aggressive” you can make the D-term: D amplifies high frequencies, and the motor can't follow them anyway — it just heats up. The frequency side of the same equation: it's a low-pass filter with cutoff frequency f_c = 1/ 2πτ . A 100 Hz gyro filter means τ = 1.6 ms of “inertia” added to the loop. The second-order equation ẍ + 2ζω₀·ẋ + ω₀²·x = ω₀²·u. Two parameters: the natural frequency ω₀ rad/s and the damping ratio ζ. - ζ 1 — overdamped: creeps up slowly without overshoot. - ζ = 1 — critically damped: the fastest arrival without overshoot. - 0 < ζ < 1 — underdamped: overshoot and decaying oscillations at frequency ω₀√ 1 − ζ² ; overshoot in percent ≈ 100·e^ −πζ/√ 1 − ζ² ζ = 0.5 → 16 %, ζ = 0.7 → 5 % . - ζ = 0 — undamped oscillations; ζ < 0 — instability, the amplitude grows. A quadcopter axis with an angle PD controller is exactly this equation: inertia J·θ̈ = torque, torque = K_p· θ_target − θ − K_d·θ̇. Then ω₀ = √ K_p/J , ζ = K_d/ 2√ K_p·J . This gives the rule every tuner knows without knowing the formula: raise P — the oscillations get faster and the overshoot grows; raise D — the overshoot drops. The I-term, in turn, adds a third order and can turn ζ negative — low-frequency “I oscillations” with too much I. Poles: the address of behavior Any linear equation with constant coefficients has solutions of the form e^ st ; substituting gives the characteristic equation, and its roots s are the poles . A first-order system has one pole: s = −1/τ. A second-order one: s = −ζω₀ ± ω₀√ ζ² − 1 . Reading a pole map on the complex plane: - A negative real part — stable; the further left, the faster it decays settling time ≈ 4/ Re s . - The imaginary part is the oscillation frequency rad/s . - A pole in the right half-plane — instability: any error grows. - A pole on the imaginary axis — the boundary: undamped oscillations this is how a loop behaves with P raised until it self-oscillates . {{diagram:pole-response A pole map and the corresponding step responses: further left — faster, higher — more oscillatory, right of zero — growth.}} The transfer function For linear systems with zero initial conditions, differentiation in time turns into multiplication by s the Laplace transform . First order: G s = K/ τs + 1 . Second order: G s = ω₀²/ s² + 2ζω₀s + ω₀² . PID: C s = K_p + K_i/s + K_d·s. Blocks are combined by multiplication in series and by the closed-loop formula: T s = C·G/ 1 + C·G . The closed-loop poles are the roots of 1 + C s G s = 0: this is where the “right” PID values live. A pure delay packet transport, a filter is e^ −sL : it doesn't change the amplitude, but it shifts the phase by ω·L, and that's exactly what makes the loop unstable at high gains. Phase margin is how much more delay you can add before self-oscillation; on a well-tuned 5" combat quad it's 40–60°. Discretization: formulas for firmware The controller runs in ticks with period T_s Betaflight — PID loop 4–8 kHz, ArduPilot — 400 Hz, PX4 rate loop — 800 Hz by default, up to 2 kHz via IMU_GYRO_RATEMAX . Derivatives and integrals are replaced with differences: - Backward Euler : ẋ ≈ xₖ − xₖ₋₁ /T_s; ∫x ≈ Σ xₖ·T_s. Simple, but it adds a T_s/2 delay and distorts frequencies above f_s/10. - Tustin bilinear : s → 2/T_s · z − 1 / z + 1 . It preserves stability and the frequency response more accurately; all Betaflight filters biquad and PT1 are discretized exactly this way or through the exact RC filter formula. - A first-order PT1 in code: yₖ = yₖ₋₁ + k· xₖ − yₖ₋₁ , where k = T_s/ τ + T_s — this is the backward Euler transform, practically exact when f_c ≪ f_s. In Betaflight — pt1FilterGain . - What breaks with a large T_s: the Nyquist frequency f_s/2 — everything above it folds back aliases ; the derivative of noise grows as 1/T_s; with T_s comparable to τ, forward Euler can make a stable system unstable. Rule: the loop period should be no more than τ/10 of the fastest process the loop has to handle. Delay versus inertia People confuse them, but they're different: inertia τ is a smooth response that starts immediately; delay L is nothing happening, then an exact copy of the input. A loop with inertia can be “pushed” with gain almost without limit; a loop with delay can't: with gain K the phase margin gets eaten up, and at ω·L ≈ 1–1.5 rad the loop oscillates no matter what you do. For a 5": L ≈ 2–4 ms filters + RC with τ ≈ 20 ms. That's why the mantra “fewer filters — a sharper drone” holds right up to the moment the noise starts heating the motors. practice Step 1. One axis

title: Probability and estimation: noise, Gaussians, fusion
summary: The Kalman filter is not magic, it is two facts about Gaussian distributions applied a million times. This module gives you those facts and the language around them: a random variable, mean and variance, why sensor noise is treated as Gaussian, what independence and covariance are, what a covariance
headings: Random variable, mean, variance The Gaussian and why it is everywhere Two measurements of the same thing Vectors: covariance and the ellipse Noise over time: white, random walk, Allan deviation What of this is in the autopilot parameters Step 1. A gyro datasheet from a recording Step 2. Allan deviation Step 3. Fusion by hand Step 4. The ellipse
text: summary The Kalman filter is not magic, it is two facts about Gaussian distributions applied a million times. This module gives you those facts and the language around them: a random variable, mean and variance, why sensor noise is treated as Gaussian, what independence and covariance are, what a covariance matrix looks like as an ellipse and what “EKF variance” in a failsafe message means. The central result is the optimal fusion of two measurements, which is exactly one Kalman step. Then — how noise behaves over time: white noise, random walk, ARW/VRW and Allan deviation, which is how you read an IMU datasheet and pick EK3_GYRO_P_NSE . Lab: gyro noise and bias from a recording, Allan deviation, and a numeric problem on fusion. theory Random variable, mean, variance A sensor measurement is z = x + n: the true value plus noise. Noise is a random variable: we don't know the next value, but we know how the values are distributed. The mean μ = E n is the systematic part bias ; you can estimate it and subtract it. The variance σ² = E n − μ ² is the spread; σ the standard deviation is in the same units as the measurement. Sample estimates over N samples: μ̂ = 1/N Σzᵢ, σ̂² = 1/ N−1 Σ zᵢ − μ̂ ². For a gyro at rest μ̂ is the bias and σ̂ is the noise; both go into the sensor datasheet. The mean of N independent samples has variance σ²/N: averaging 100 samples reduces σ by a factor of 10. That is the limit of what “just filtering” gives you — and the reason slow sensors GPS at 5 Hz can't be made accurate by averaging over 0.2 s. The Gaussian and why it is everywhere The density of N μ, σ² : p x = 1/ σ√ 2π ·exp − x − μ ²/ 2σ² . Within ±1σ lie 68 % of the values, ±2σ — 95 %, ±3σ — 99.7 %. The innovation gates in the EKF EK3_ _I_GATE are exactly “reject everything farther than kσ”. The Gaussian arises from the central limit theorem: the sum of many small independent contributions thermal noise, vibration, quantization is distributed almost normally, whatever the individual contributions look like. The second argument is practical: a Gaussian is fully described by two numbers, and linear operations on Gaussians give Gaussians. For a filter that means the state can be stored as mean, covariance rather than as a histogram. Where the Gaussian model breaks: outliers GPS multipath, a magnetic anomaly — the tails are heavier than normal, hence the gates; quantization and saturation; noise that depends on the operating mode vibration under throttle . Two measurements of the same thing Measurements z₁ with variance σ₁² and z₂ with σ₂² of the same quantity x. The best minimum-variance, unbiased linear estimate weights them by inverse variances: x̂ = z₁/σ₁² + z₂/σ₂² / 1/σ₁² + 1/σ₂² , 1/σ̂² = 1/σ₁² + 1/σ₂². Rewritten with K = σ₁²/ σ₁² + σ₂² : x̂ = z₁ + K· z₂ − z₁ , σ̂² = 1 − K ·σ₁². Recognize it? z₁ is the prediction with uncertainty P, z₂ is the measurement with R, K is the Kalman gain, z₂ − z₁ is the innovation. One Kalman step is the fusion of two Gaussians. Everything else in the EKF is how to get the prediction and its P from the previous state model + process noise Q and how to do the same for a vector. {{diagram:gaussian-fusion Fusing two Gaussian estimates: the result is always narrower than either of them and shifted toward the more accurate one.}} Vectors: covariance and the ellipse For a state vector x for example, position N, E the covariance matrix is P = E x − μ x − μ ᵀ : the diagonal holds the variances of the components, the off-diagonal entries are covariances, that is, how strongly the errors are linked. The correlation ρ = P₁₂/ σ₁σ₂ ∈ −1, 1 . Geometrically P is an uncertainty ellipse: the axes lie along the eigenvectors of P, the semi-axes are √ eigenvalues . A GPS ellipse stretched along N says that north is known worse than east typical with poor satellite geometry . “EKF variance” in the ArduPilot failsafe is the normalized innovations the √test ratio of velocity, position, compass — the same numbers as in XKF4 exceeding FS_EKF_THRESH : the filter honestly admits it doesn't know where it is. A linear transform y = A·x carries the covariance as P_y = A·P·Aᵀ. This is the formula both for prediction A = F, the model matrix and for switching between coordinate frames A = R — the covariance rotates together with the ellipse . Independence: zero covariance, P is diagonal; that is exactly what you assume when you set EK3_ _NOISE with one number per source. Noise over time: white, random walk, Allan deviation White noise — the samples are independent; its integral is a random walk , whose σ grows as √t. For a gyro: the angular rate noise σ_g °/s per sample after integration gives an angle error σ_θ t = ARW·√t, where ARW = σ_g·√T_s angle random walk, in °/√h in datasheets . For an accelerometer it is VRW: the velocity error grows as √t, the position error as t^1.5. This explains why without GPS an IMU-only position drifts by meters in seconds, while the gyro angle holds for minutes. But the bias isn't constant either: it slowly wanders bias instability, flicker . Allan deviation σ τ — the standard deviation of the difference of averages over adjacent windows of length τ — separates these contributions on one plot: a slope of −½ white noise; ARW is read from it at τ = 1 s , a plateau bias instability — the best achievable bias stability , a slope of +½ rate random walk . This plot is what you use to pick the EKF process noise: EK3_GYRO_P_NSE is set in rad/s default 0.015 — with a large margin over the datasheet noise density, because it covers vibration and model errors , EK3_GBIAS_P_NSE — from the +½ slope. PX4: EKF2_GYR_NOISE , EKF2_GYR_B_NOISE . What of this is in the autopilot parameters What ArduPilot EKF3 PX4 EKF2 --- --- --- gyro noise σ goes into Q, the process noise of the prediction EK3_GYRO_P_NSE EKF2_GYR_NOISE gyro bias random walk EK3_GBIAS_P_NSE EKF2_GYR_B_NOISE GPS position σ EK3_POSNE_M_NSE +HDOP EKF2_GPS_P_NOISE baro σ EK3_ALT_M_NSE EKF2_BARO_NOISE gates in σ EK3_ _I_GATE % EKF2_ _GA

title: ROS 2 onboard: nodes, topics, QoS, tf2, bag
summary: ROS 2 isn't a “library for drones”, it's a way to build onboard software out of independent processes that talk over DDS. Its value for UAVs is ready-made nodes (cameras, lidars, SLAM, Nav2), common message types and debugging tools: recording and replaying all traffic, the node graph, visualization
headings: The graph: nodes, topics, services, actions QoS: why the subscription is silent Coordinate frames: REP-103 and REP-105 Time Launch and parameters ros2 bag Step 1. Environment Step 2. The graph by hand Step 3. Telemetry logger Step 4. Bag: record and replay Step 5. tf2
text: summary ROS 2 isn't a “library for drones”, it's a way to build onboard software out of independent processes that talk over DDS. Its value for UAVs is ready-made nodes cameras, lidars, SLAM, Nav2 , common message types and debugging tools: recording and replaying all traffic, the node graph, visualization. Its price is complexity: QoS, coordinate frames, time. This module gives you exactly the part of ROS 2 without which no offboard node will ever fly: the node graph, topics/services/actions, parameters and launch, QoS and why a subscription to PX4 “with defaults” stays silent, REP-103/105 and tf2 , simulation time and ros2 bag . Lab: a telemetry logger node, recording and replaying a bag, and working through a QoS incompatibility hands-on. The environment is examples/ros2-docker/ . theory The graph: nodes, topics, services, actions - A node is a process or part of a process with a name, parameters and interfaces. Design rule: one node — one responsibility bridge, perception, decision, safeguard . - A topic is a “one-to-many” stream of messages of one type; publishers and subscribers don't know about each other. Telemetry, setpoints, images. - A service is request-response ArmMotors , ModeSwitch . The semantics are synchronous, but inside a node you must call it asynchronously call_async , otherwise you can block your own executor. - An action is a long-running goal with feedback and cancellation NavigateToPose in Nav2 . It's topics + services assembled into a protocol. - Parameters are typed node settings ros2 param set /node alt 7.0 , with a validation callback on change. DDS finds participants on the network by itself discovery within a single ROS_DOMAIN_ID . On an aircraft with a companion and a laptop on the same Wi-Fi network, this means: without separate domains or filters, the laptop will “see” the vehicle's topics and be able to publish to them. For field flights — a separate domain, or better, ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE=LOCALHOST Jazzy; in Humble — ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 on board and a bridge to the outside only for the topics you need. {{diagram:ros2-graph The training system as a graph: the bridge to the autopilot, the logger, the state machine, perception and the watchdog are separate nodes.}} QoS: why the subscription is silent Every publisher and subscriber has a QoS profile: reliability RELIABLE/BEST_EFFORT , durability VOLATILE/TRANSIENT_LOCAL — whether a late subscriber gets the last message , history/depth how much to keep , deadline, lifespan, liveliness. A connection is established only with compatible profiles, and an incompatibility doesn't raise an error — the subscriber simply receives nothing an “incompatible QoS” warning may show up in the log . The main rule: BEST_EFFORT publisher + RELIABLE subscriber = no connection. PX4 publishes /fmu/out/ as BEST_EFFORT and TRANSIENT_LOCAL , while a ROS 2 subscriber is RELIABLE by default. That's why you subscribe to PX4 with the qos_profile_sensor_data profile BEST_EFFORT or an explicit QoSProfile . Why BEST_EFFORT for telemetry: when a packet is lost over Wi-Fi, resending an old position is useless, you need the next one — the same logic as UDP versus TCP in the mav-routing module. Check: ros2 topic info -v /fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1 shows the profiles of both sides. {{diagram:ros2-qos Reliability compatibility: a BEST_EFFORT publisher doesn't connect to a RELIABLE subscriber — silently.}} Coordinate frames: REP-103 and REP-105 ROS lives in ENU world and FLU body — REP-103; autopilots live in NED/FRD. This is the main source of integration bugs module math-linalg-rot : x/y swap places, z changes sign, yaw ψ_enu = 90° − ψ_ned, quaternions in ROS are stored as x, y, z, w . REP-105 defines the standard frames: map global, drift-free, can jump , odom continuous, drifts , base_link body . The bridges handle this differently: AP_DDS publishes directly in ENU/ map / base_link , PX4 uXRCE-DDS publishes in NED/FRD, as inside PX4, and the conversion is on your side. tf2 is a tree of transforms between frames over time: “where was the camera relative to map at the moment of the frame”. A node publishes TransformStamped to /tf dynamic and /tf_static sensor mounts , and a consumer asks lookup_transform target, source, time . A camera on a bracket is the static transform base_link → camera_link ; you set it once in the launch file. Time Every message with a header has a header.stamp . In simulation, time runs from /clock the parameter use_sim_time:=true , otherwise the nodes and the bag live in different times, and tf2 refuses to give transforms “from the future”. PX4 uses its own timestamps in microseconds timestamp and synchronizes them with the agent; ArduPilot publishes /ap/time and /ap/clock . Launch and parameters A launch file Python starts a set of nodes with parameters, namespaces and topic remapping remappings . This is what runs on board at startup: systemd service → ros2 launch . Parameters go in a YAML file, not in the code — so that the same package works on two different vehicles. ros2 bag ros2 bag record -o run1 /topic1 /topic2 writes the traffic to a file in Jazzy the default is MCAP, in Humble — SQLite3; the format is set with the -s flag ; ros2 bag play run1 replays it, and your nodes can't tell the replay from a flight. This is the main debugging tool: you recorded a flight with a bug — replay it and fix the node on the bench as many times as you like. Recording all topics with cameras on board quickly eats disk and CPU: record compressed images or at a reduced rate. practice Step 1. Environment bash cd examples/ros2-docker docker compose build ros docker compose run --rm ros bash ros2 doctor --report head -20 The image is built and tested in CI on ROS 2 Jazzy Ubuntu 24.04 inside the container, so the host can be on 22.04 as well . title: ROS 2 + PX4: uXRCE-DDS, an offboard node as a state machine
summary: The px4-ros2 module showed that PX4 “speaks” ROS 2 through the uXRCE-DDS bridge and that an offboard flight is three messages. Here you learn how to turn that into a node you can trust with a vehicle: `px4_msgs` message versions and the `_v<N>` suffixes, time synchronization, the Offboard rules (a “
headings: The uXRCE-DDS bridge Message versions Offboard rules Flight logic as a state machine Testing without a simulator Gazebo and SITL Step 1. Test the state machine Step 2. A square in Gazebo Step 3. Safeguards in the simulator Step 4. Replay from a bag
text: summary The px4-ros2 module showed that PX4 “speaks” ROS 2 through the uXRCE-DDS bridge and that an offboard flight is three messages. Here you learn how to turn that into a node you can trust with a vehicle: px4_msgs message versions and the _v<N suffixes, time synchronization, the Offboard rules a “proof of life” stream 2 Hz, setpoints before the mode switch , and most importantly, the flight logic as a state machine with no ROS inside, testable with plain pytest. The node becomes a thin wrapper: collect observations → step the state machine → execute the action. Lab: a square in Gazebo with safeguards position loss, stale status, pilot intervention , a test of the state machine against a toy vehicle model, and a flight replay from a bag. theory The uXRCE-DDS bridge Inside PX4 runs the client uxrce_dds_client : it publishes the selected uORB topics and subscribes to incoming ones according to the list in dds_topics.yaml in the PX4 sources . Outside runs the agent MicroXRCEAgent , which exposes these topics on the DDS network as ordinary ROS 2 topics /fmu/out/ from PX4 and /fmu/in/ to PX4 . The transport is UDP SITL: the agent on port 8888, the client starts automatically or a serial port UXRCE_DDS_CFG selects the port on a real flight controller . Unlike MAVLink, there are no “protocol messages” here — these are the PX4 uORB structures themselves, hence the requirement: px4_msgs on the ROS side must match the PX4 version . {{diagram:uxrce-scheme PX4 and ArduPilot connect to ROS 2 with the same scheme: “client in the firmware — agent on the companion.”}} Message versions Starting with PX4 v1.16, some messages have a version MESSAGE_VERSION in the definition , and their topics are published with a suffix: /fmu/out/vehicle_status_v1 . To keep old nodes compatible with new firmware and vice versa there is a translator node PX4 ROS 2 Message Translation Node . Practice for your own nodes: compute the topic name from the message class's MESSAGE_VERSION instead of typing it by hand — as done in px4_offboard_square.py : python def topic base, msg_cls : v = getattr msg_cls, "MESSAGE_VERSION", 0 return base if v == 0 else f"{base}_v{v}" Offboard rules 1. The external controller must continuously send OffboardControlMode which setpoints are active: position, velocity, acceleration, attitude, body_rate… at more than 2 Hz — this is the “proof of life.” The actual setpoints go in TrajectorySetpoint position/velocity/acceleration/yaw, unused fields = NaN . 2. The stream must be running before the switch to Offboard and before arming in Offboard , otherwise PX4 refuses. 3. If the stream stops for longer than COM_OF_LOSS_T , PX4 leaves Offboard and switches to the mode set in COM_OBL_RC_ACT Position, Altitude, Manual, Return, Land . 4. Commands are VehicleCommand on /fmu/in/vehicle_command : arm with VEHICLE_CMD_COMPONENT_ARM_DISARM param1 = 1 , mode with VEHICLE_CMD_DO_SET_MODE param1 = 1 — custom, param2 = 6 — Offboard , land with VEHICLE_CMD_NAV_LAND . The acknowledgement comes on /fmu/out/vehicle_command_ack ; the state is in VehicleStatus.arming_state , nav_state . 5. Coordinates in TrajectorySetpoint are NED, local , with the origin at the EKF initialization point; altitude is negative. Flight logic as a state machine A typical mistake is logic in callbacks: “status arrived → if armed → send mode.” Such code can't be tested, can't be reproduced, and behaves unpredictably when messages are lost. The right way: a pure class OffboardFSM examples/ros2-docker/.../offboard_fsm.py with a single method step obs → action , no ROS and no time pulled “out of thin air”: - Observations Obs : time, age of the last status, position validity, armed, mode, NED position, whether landed. - Action Action : setpoint, arm/mode/land requests, a note. - States : WAIT_READY → STREAM_SETPOINTS ≥ 1 s of setpoints before the mode request → ARMING → OFFBOARD → TAKEOFF → SQUARE → LAND → DONE. - Safeguards checked in every active state : status stale 1 s → ABORT; position invalid → ABORT; step timeout → ABORT; pilot switched the mode themselves → DONE with no commands don't “fight” the human . The ROS node does only I/O: it builds Obs from the latest messages on a 20 Hz timer, calls step , publishes setpoints and rate-limited commands. The same state machine is used for ArduPilot the ros2-ardupilot module — only the wrapper changes. {{diagram:offboard-fsm Offboard node state machine: a linear scenario plus safeguards that lead to landing or hand control back to the pilot.}} Testing without a simulator test_offboard_fsm.py runs the state machine against a toy vehicle model arms on request, enters Offboard only if setpoints have been flowing for ≥ 0.5 s, flies to the setpoint at 2 m/s, lands : it checks the full scenario, the “setpoints before mode” order, and the reaction to position loss, stale status and pilot intervention. That's five tests in 50 ms — you can run them on every commit in this course, in CI , and only then go to Gazebo. Gazebo and SITL make px4_sitl gz_x500 — the x500 quadcopter in Gazebo Harmonic; the PX4 documentation main recommends ROS 2 Jazzy on Ubuntu 24.04; on Ubuntu 22.04, Humble the same is stated in the v1.16/v1.17 release documentation . Agent: MicroXRCEAgent udp4 -p 8888 . For repeatable tests — headless HEADLESS=1 and a fixed world. QGroundControl connects over UDP 14550 in parallel — it's handy for watching modes and aborting the flight. practice Step 1. Test the state machine bash cd examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs python -m pytest -q test/test_offboard_fsm.py Add your own test: battery a new field battery_low in Obs → ABORT. Test first, then code. Step 2. A square in Gazebo bash docker compose --profile px4 up or natively: MicroXRCEAgent + make px4_sitl gz_x500 ros2 launch uav_ros2_labs px4_square.launch.py The node log shows the state transitions; QGC shows the mode changes; /tmp/px4_flight.csv holds the trajectory. Plot it: a 10 × 10 m square at 5 m. Step 3. Safeguards in the simula
