title: ROS 2 + ArduPilot: AP_DDS and MAVROS, one node, two routes
summary: ArduPilot has two routes into ROS 2. **AP_DDS** is a DDS client built into the firmware (the same principle as uXRCE-DDS in PX4): `/ap/*` topics in ENU and standard ROS types, services for arming and mode changes, velocity control via `/ap/cmd_vel`. **MAVROS** is a MAVLink ↔ ROS bridge that works wi
headings: AP_DDS: how to connect it What AP_DDS publishes and accepts The order of actions in ArduPilot MAVROS Comparing the routes One state machine, two wrappers Step 1. SITL with DDS Step 2. A square via AP_DDS Step 3. The same square via MAVROS Step 4. Comparison What you should get and what to record
text: summary ArduPilot has two routes into ROS 2. AP_DDS is a DDS client built into the firmware the same principle as uXRCE-DDS in PX4 : /ap/ topics in ENU and standard ROS types, services for arming and mode changes, velocity control via /ap/cmd_vel . MAVROS is a MAVLink ↔ ROS bridge that works with any firmware and with the full set of MAVLink features, at the cost of an extra layer. This module takes both apart from the source code and documentation, compares them with the PX4 route and shows how the same state machine from the ros2-px4 module flies a square on ArduPilot via AP_DDS. Lab: a square in SITL via AP_DDS, then via MAVROS, and a comparison table of latency and convenience. theory AP_DDS: how to connect it In the firmware there is a DDS client libraries/AP_DDS ; outside, there is a micro-ROS agent micro_ros_agent that exposes the data on the ROS 2 DDS network. - Parameters: DDS_ENABLE = 1 ; UDP transport — DDS_UDP_PORT default 2019 and the agent address DDS_IP0..3 ; serial transport — SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 45 on the port you need. DDS_DOMAIN_ID is the ROS 2 domain. - SITL: a build with DDS support ./waf configure --board sitl --enable-DDS , run sim_vehicle.py -v ArduCopter --enable-DDS , agent: ros2 run micro_ros_agent micro_ros_agent udp4 -p 2019 . - ArduPilot-specific message types come from the ardupilot_msgs package in the ArduPilot repository, Tools/ros2/ardupilot_msgs : Status , GlobalPosition , the services ArmMotors , ModeSwitch , Takeoff . {{diagram:uxrce-scheme The scheme is the same as in PX4: a client in the firmware, an agent on the companion, regular ROS 2 topics outside.}} What AP_DDS publishes and accepts Topic/service Type Purpose --- --- --- /ap/pose/filtered geometry_msgs/PoseStamped local pose from the EKF relative to home, ENU the firmware writes base_link into header.frame_id /ap/twist/filtered geometry_msgs/TwistStamped velocity /ap/geopose/filtered , /ap/navsat geographic_msgs/GeoPoseStamped , sensor_msgs/NavSatFix global pose, GNSS /ap/battery , /ap/status , /ap/rc sensor_msgs/BatteryState , ardupilot_msgs/Status , ardupilot_msgs/Rc battery; armed, mode, flying, external_control, failsafe /ap/tf_static , /ap/clock , /ap/time tf2, time mounts, clock for sim time /ap/cmd_vel input geometry_msgs/TwistStamped velocity in GUIDED; frame map ENU or base_link /ap/cmd_gps_pose input ardupilot_msgs/GlobalPosition global target in GUIDED /ap/arm_motors , /ap/mode_switch , /ap/prearm_check , /ap/experimental/takeoff services arm, mode Copter mode number: GUIDED = 4, LAND = 9 , pre-arm, takeoff Important: AP_DDS converts ENU ↔ NED itself — for cmd_vel based on header.frame_id map — world ENU, base_link — body . So unlike with PX4, your ROS node lives entirely within ROS conventions. QoS: poses and velocities are BEST_EFFORT, /ap/status and tf_static are RELIABLE + TRANSIENT_LOCAL a BEST_EFFORT subscriber is compatible with both . The order of actions in ArduPilot ArduCopter arms only in a mode that allows arming GUIDED does and only after the pre-arm checks. Takeoff in GUIDED is a separate command the takeoff service = MAV_CMD_NAV_TAKEOFF ; without it, the vehicle on the ground ignores horizontal setpoints. The sequence in the node: GUIDED → arm → takeoff alt → velocity/position setpoints → LAND. The velocity setpoint timeout in GUIDED is GUID_TIMEOUT seconds : if cmd_vel stops arriving, the vehicle stops. This is the same “proof of life” principle as Offboard in PX4. MAVROS MAVROS is a node that holds the MAVLink connection and distributes it across plugins: /mavros/state connection, armed, mode , /mavros/local_position/pose , /mavros/setpoint_position/local , /mavros/setpoint_velocity/cmd_vel , the services /mavros/cmd/arming , /mavros/set_mode , /mavros/cmd/takeoff , /mavros/mission/push , parameters, geofences, full access to any MAVLink message via mavros_msgs/Mavlink . It also converts ENU ↔ NED. Launch: ros2 launch mavros apm.launch fcu_url:=udp://:14550@ connecting to SITL or to a router on the companion . When MAVROS is better than AP_DDS: you need functionality that AP_DDS doesn't have missions, parameters, camera, arbitrary MAVLink messages ; you have a mixed fleet one codebase for ArduPilot and PX4 via MAVLink ; the firmware has no DDS. When AP_DDS is better: fewer layers and lower latency, standard ROS types, no MAVLink traffic on the companion for the ROS part. Comparing the routes PX4 uXRCE-DDS ArduPilot AP_DDS MAVROS --- --- --- --- What's on the wire uORB structs over XRCE DDS client, standard ROS types MAVLink Coordinate frame on the ROS side NED/FRD you convert yourself ENU/FLU the firmware converts ENU/FLU MAVROS converts Version compatibility px4_msgs = PX4 version, _vN suffixes ardupilot_msgs from the same branch MAVLink dialect, stable Feature coverage everything in dds_topics.yaml the /ap/ set, growing almost all of MAVLink External control Offboard, stream 2 Hz GUIDED, GUID_TIMEOUT GUIDED/Offboard via setpoint_ One state machine, two wrappers ap_dds_square.py uses the same OffboardFSM as the PX4 node. The only differences are in the wrapper: observations come from /ap/status and /ap/pose/filtered ENU → NED for the state machine , the “external control mode” = GUIDED, the arm request becomes “GUIDED first, then arm”, after reaching altitude — the takeoff service, the state machine's position setpoints are turned into velocity a P controller limited to 3 m/s on /ap/cmd_vel in the map frame. The safeguard logic and all the state machine tests remain valid. practice Step 1. SITL with DDS bash docker compose --profile ardupilot up --build or natively: waf configure --enable-DDS, sim_vehicle.py --enable-DDS docker compose run --rm ros bash ros2 topic list grep /ap/ ros2 topic echo /ap/status --once ros2 service call /ap/mode_switch ardupilot_msgs/srv/ModeSwitch "{mode: 4}" Step 2. A square via AP_DDS ros2 launch uav_ros2_labs ap_square.launch.py . Compare the state machine transitions in the log with the modes in Mission Planner/QGC. Plot the trajector

title: Architecture of an onboard ROS 2 application: nodes, lifecycle, watchdog
summary: A single node that does everything works exactly until the first error in its least reliable part — usually perception. An onboard application must survive a camera dropout, a hung neural network and a process restart without losing control of the vehicle. This module gives you an architecture that
headings: Four roles Managed nodes (lifecycle) Freshness watchdog Parameters and configuration Deployment Debugging and profiling Step 1. Watchdog tests Step 2. A four-node skeleton Step 3. Perception and position failures Step 4. Autostart
text: summary A single node that does everything works exactly until the first error in its least reliable part — usually perception. An onboard application must survive a camera dropout, a hung neural network and a process restart without losing control of the vehicle. This module gives you an architecture that makes that possible: a split into bridge, perception, decision and safeguards; managed nodes lifecycle with explicit states; a data-freshness watchdog with OK/DEGRADED/FAILSAFE levels and hysteresis; parameters and configuration; containers and autostart; debugging from bags and profiling. Lab: a four-node skeleton in which killing the perception node puts the system into DEGRADED and losing position puts it into FAILSAFE, verified by tests. theory Four roles Role What it does What it doesn't do Criticality --- --- --- --- Bridge uXRCE-DDS agent / AP_DDS / MAVROS translates the autopilot protocol into topics makes no decisions critical Perception camera/lidar → targets, obstacles, pose doesn't command the vehicle non-critical degradation Decision mission, state machine picks setpoints from targets and state doesn't read sensors directly critical Safeguards watchdog, application geofence, battery watch freshness and limits, have veto power don't plan critical {{diagram:ros2-graph Four roles in the node graph: bridge, perception, decision, safeguards.}} The direction rule: decision subscribes to perception and to the safeguards; the safeguards can stop decision; perception knows nothing about decision. No non-critical node may sit on the “autopilot status → setpoints” path. Managed nodes lifecycle A regular node starts working as soon as it is launched. A lifecycle node rclpy.lifecycle / rclcpp_lifecycle goes through explicit states: unconfigured → inactive → active → finalized , with the transitions configure , activate , deactivate , cleanup , shutdown , each with its own callback that can return an error. What this gives you on board: - configuration open the camera, load the model is separated from operation — you see the error before takeoff; - a node can be “paused” deactivate without killing the process — for example, to turn perception off during landing; - a manager nav2_lifecycle_manager or your own brings the system up in the right order and knows who failed to come up. {{diagram:ros2-lifecycle Lifecycle node states: configuration is separated from operation, pausing doesn't kill the process.}} Freshness watchdog Every input message has a maximum allowed age. The watchdog examples/ros2-docker/.../watchdog.py , no ROS inside stores the time of the last message for each input and outputs a single system level: - OK — everything is fresh; - DEGRADED — a non-critical input targets from the camera is stale: the mission continues, the function tracking is suspended; - FAILSAFE — a critical input autopilot status, pose is stale: decision stops commanding and requests a hold/landing. Hysteresis: an input counts as recovered only if it stays fresh continuously for recover_s for example, 1 s — otherwise a “flickering” camera will switch tracking on and off several times a second. The watchdog is a separate node with its own timer; it doesn't command the autopilot itself, it publishes the level that decision subscribes to. The last line of defense is the autopilot itself Offboard/GUIDED timeouts : if the whole application crashes, the vehicle still switches to a safe mode. Parameters and configuration Everything that differs between vehicles camera offsets, thresholds, rates, topic names goes into YAML parameters passed through launch. The add_on_set_parameters_callback callback validates new values range, type and can reject them — that way an operator in the field can't set a threshold of 10 m instead of 1 m. Secrets VPN keys, cloud tokens don't go into ROS parameters, but into files with access permissions or into the service's environment variables. Deployment - Container : an image with ROS 2, the dependencies and your package; image version = onboard software version. docker compose with restart: unless-stopped and network_mode: host DDS discovery inside containers on a bridge network is harder . - Autostart : a systemd service that runs ros2 launch or compose after the network is up and after the serial port appears After= , BindsTo=dev-ttyAMA0.device . - Logs : ros2 bag record of the key topics, split into files --max-bag-duration , --max-bag-size ; automatic deletion of old files with --max-bag-files exists only in newer rosbag2 versions, in Humble/Jazzy you have to clean up disk space yourself + journald; after an incident — download the bag together with the autopilot log. - Time : chrony/NTP on the companion, synchronization with the autopilot TIMESYNC/uXRCE — otherwise the bag and the autopilot log won't line up. Debugging and profiling - Replaying a bag into the decision and safeguard nodes module ros2-basics is the main tool. - ros2 topic hz/bw/delay — rate, bandwidth and latency relative to header.stamp . - Profiling: top / htop per process, py-spy record for Python nodes, ros2_tracing LTTng for callback latencies; on a Jetson — tegrastats CPU/GPU/temperature . - Executor: heavy callbacks the neural network go into a separate callback group MutuallyExclusiveCallbackGroup with a MultiThreadedExecutor , otherwise the 20 Hz setpoint timer will wait for inference to finish. practice Step 1. Watchdog tests bash cd examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs python -m pytest -q test/test_watchdog.py Work through test_hysteresis_on_flapping_input : why the level is still DEGRADED after 0.5 s of recovery. Step 2. A four-node skeleton Build a uav_app package with the nodes bridge_monitor subscribes to autopilot status/pose , perception_stub publishes targets at 10 Hz, crashes on command , watchdog_node a wrapper around watchdog.py , publishes the level and the reasons , decision_node the state machine from ros2-px4, subscribed to the level . A launch file with parameters from YAML.

title: Navigation and obstacle avoidance: maps, planners, setpoints
summary: The autopilot knows how to fly to a point. To fly to a point **without crashing into things**, you need a map, a planner and a chain from the plan to setpoints — and an honest understanding of what the autopilot can already do on its own (ArduPilot: BendyRuler and Dijkstra, PX4: collision prevention
headings: What the autopilot can do without you Map representations Global planning Local planning and reaction Nav2 and drones From plan to setpoints Step 1. A* with tests Step 2. Braking distance Step 3. Flying around an obstacle in Gazebo Step 4. Unknown space
text: summary The autopilot knows how to fly to a point. To fly to a point without crashing into things , you need a map, a planner and a chain from the plan to setpoints — and an honest understanding of what the autopilot can already do on its own ArduPilot: BendyRuler and Dijkstra, PX4: collision prevention and where you need your own logic on the companion. This module covers map representations occupancy grid, costmap, 3D voxels , global and local planning A , Dijkstra, reactive methods , obstacle inflation and path smoothing, the role of Nav2 and why it's “ground-based”, and how a plan turns into GUIDED/Offboard setpoints with velocity and altitude limits. Lab: A on a grid with tests, then flying around an obstacle in Gazebo using lidar data. theory What the autopilot can do without you - ArduPilot : proximity sensors PRX1_TYPE , including MAVLink OBSTACLE_DISTANCE → simple avoidance stop/slide in Loiter, AVOID_ENABLE , AVOID_MARGIN and object avoidance in automatic modes: OA_TYPE = 1 BendyRuler reactive, searches for a way around , 2 Dijkstra over polygon geofences, a global path around known no-go zones , 3 a combination. Parameters OA_MARGIN_MAX , OA_BR_LOOKAHEAD . - PX4 : collision prevention in Position mode CP_DIST — the minimum distance, from OBSTACLE_DISTANCE /ROS 2 ObstacleDistance , limits velocity toward the obstacle. This works and has been flight-tested — start with it. You need your own navigation on the companion when: the map has to be built and stored indoor flight, a forest , the path must be globally optimal in an unknown environment, or there is a higher-level goal survey an object, fly to a point found by the camera . Map representations - Occupancy grid , 2D: a cell holds the probability of being occupied in ROS nav_msgs/OccupancyGrid : 0–100, −1 — unknown . It's updated from rangefinder/lidar rays: along the ray — free, at the end — occupied log-odds, to accumulate evidence . - Costmap : occupancy + inflation + layers static, obstacles, geofences . Inflating by the vehicle radius plus a margin lets you plan for a point rather than for a body. - 3D : OctoMap an octree of voxels , ESDF/TSDF a field of distances to the nearest obstacle: Voxblox, nvblox . For flight at different altitudes a 2D grid isn't enough, but 2D at a fixed altitude is a good start. - Unknown = occupied by default: fly only where you've already seen that it's free. Otherwise the planner will route the path “through a wall” it hasn't seen yet. Global planning A\ on a grid: a search for the shortest path from start to goal with a heuristic an estimate of the remaining distance . If the heuristic never overestimates it's admissible , the path is optimal. For an 8-connected grid — the octile distance dx + dy + √2 − 2 ·min dx, dy . No “cutting the corner” diagonally between two occupied cells. Dijkstra is A with a zero heuristic slower, but the same solution . For large 3D spaces — sampling-based methods RRT , PRM . The raw A path is a cell-by-cell “staircase”. Smoothing shortcut : drop intermediate points as long as the straight segment is free; then apply the dynamics limits velocity, acceleration, jerk when building the trajectory. Local planning and reaction The global plan is built from a map that is already out of date by flight time. The local layer reacts to what is visible right now: vector fields VFH , dynamic window DWA , MPC, or simply “stop and replan”. Rates: global — 0.5–2 Hz, local — 10–20 Hz, setpoints — 20–50 Hz. The layers should be separate nodes module ros2-app-arch , and the last line of defense is the autopilot simple avoidance / collision prevention and the geofence. {{diagram:planning-layers Navigation layers and their rates; the last line of defense is the autopilot.}} Nav2 and drones Nav2 is the ROS 2 navigation stack: the BT navigator behavior trees , planners NavFn, Smac , controllers DWB, MPPI , costmap layers, recovery. It's designed for ground robots 2D, non-holonomic models . For a multicopter at constant altitude you can use it holonomic model, cmd_vel → GUIDED/Offboard velocities , but 3D planning, altitude and flight dynamics are beyond its scope. Many drone projects take the costmap layers and the BT ideas from Nav2, and write their own planner or take one from research stacks for example, EGO-Planner, Fast-Planner — for the experienced . From plan to setpoints 1. A path in the map frame ENU → intermediate points spaced 1–3 m apart. 2. Limits: the maximum velocity near obstacles depends on the sensor range and the braking distance: v ≤ √ 2·a·d , altitude within a corridor above the ground by rangefinder and below the geofence , yaw along the direction of travel if the camera must look forward. 3. Sending: PX4 — TrajectorySetpoint position and/or velocity, NED — convert! , ArduPilot — /ap/cmd_vel ENU, frame map or position targets via MAVROS. 4. Execution monitoring: deviation from the path threshold → stop and replan; goal unreachable → hold and notify the operator. practice Step 1. A with tests bash cd examples/ros2-docker/ws/src/uav_ros2_labs python -m pytest -q test/test_grid_planner.py Read grid_planner.py : inflation, the octile heuristic, the no-corner-cutting rule, shortcut. Add a test: the path with inflation is longer than the path without it, but not shorter than the straight line. Step 2. Braking distance For a vehicle with a maximum deceleration of 3 m/s² and a lidar with a reliable range of 8 m, calculate the maximum safe velocity with a 2 m margin and a 0.3 s reaction delay. Compare with the simple avoidance parameters of your firmware. Step 3. Flying around an obstacle in Gazebo A world with a pillar in the path of the square. Option A no code of your own : ArduPilot SITL with proximity from a simulated lidar, OA_TYPE = 1 , a mission through the pillar — record the BendyRuler trajectory. Option B your own node : an occupancy grid from /scan or OBSTACLE_DISTANCE , A + shortcut, setpoints via the state machine from ros2-px4. Compare the trajectories and

title: From ROS 1 to ROS 2: reading old projects and porting them
summary: ROS 1 Noetic reached end of support in May 2025, but half of the open drone projects, papers and tutorials are on ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin workspaces, XML launch files, `rospy`. This module teaches you to read such a project quickly (“what matters here and what depends on what”), to know how ROS 1 co
headings: How ROS 2 differs in substance How to read a ROS 1 project in 30 minutes Port or bridge Typical code replacements (Python) MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 Step 1. Reading the project Step 2. Reference data Step 3. Porting Step 4. Report
text: summary ROS 1 Noetic reached end of support in May 2025, but half of the open drone projects, papers and tutorials are on ROS 1: MAVROS 1, catkin workspaces, XML launch files, rospy . This module teaches you to read such a project quickly “what matters here and what depends on what” , to know how ROS 1 concepts map to ROS 2, to decide whether to port or run side by side through a bridge, and to port a small package. Lab: porting a ROS 1 node to ROS 2 while preserving its behavior, verified on recorded data. theory How ROS 2 differs in substance ROS 1 ROS 2 What it changes --- --- --- roscore master — a central name server no master, DDS discovery no single point of failure; you need domains/discovery limits TCPROS/UDPROS DDS with QoS you have to think about QoS module ros2-basics rospy , roscpp rclpy , rclcpp a different API, but the same ideas catkin, catkin_make / catkin build ament, colcon build a different build, package.xml format 3 XML launch .launch Python/XML/YAML launch .launch.py logic in the launch file parameters in a global server parameters per node rosparam → ros2 param against a specific node rosbag .bag ros2 bag SQLite3/MCAP converters exist rosbags tf tf2 also existed in ROS 1 almost unchanged nodelets components composable nodes several nodes in one process without copying MAVROS 1 MAVROS 2 mavros in ROS 2 the same plugins, different service names/QoS How to read a ROS 1 project in 30 minutes 1. The root : package.xml / CMakeLists.txt — dependencies which sensors, whether it's MAVROS, whether it's OpenCV . 2. Launch files launch/ .launch — what gets started, with which parameters and remaps. This is the “system diagram”. 3. Nodes scripts/ .py , src/ .cpp : find init_node , Subscriber , Publisher , Service , Timer / Rate . Draw the graph: what it listens to, what it publishes. 4. Parameters config/ .yaml , rospy.get_param — what is configurable. 5. Messages msg/ , srv/ — custom types. 6. MAVROS specifics : /mavros/setpoint_ , /mavros/set_mode , /mavros/cmd/arming — where the project controls the vehicle and in which coordinate frame. The result is a node graph as in ros2-basics and a list of external dependencies. With it, you can see what the port will cost. Port or bridge - ros1_bridge — a bidirectional bridge for topics/services between ROS 1 and ROS 2 with both running. It requires a compatible build the same message types on both sides , historically Noetic + Foxy/Humble from source. Now that Noetic support has ended, this is a temporary solution. - Porting — the right path for living code. The order: messages → library code without ROS pull it out! → nodes → launch → tests on recorded data. - Running ROS 1 in a container — to “see how it used to work” and to record reference data before porting. Typical code replacements Python ROS 1 rospy ROS 2 rclpy --- --- rospy.init_node "n" rclpy.init ; node = Node "n" rospy.Subscriber "/t", T, cb node.create_subscription T, "/t", cb, qos rospy.Publisher "/t", T, queue_size=10 node.create_publisher T, "/t", 10 rospy.Rate 20 ; while not rospy.is_shutdown : ... rate.sleep node.create_timer 0.05, tick ; rclpy.spin node rospy.get_param "~alt", 5.0 node.declare_parameter "alt", 5.0 ; node.get_parameter "alt" .value rospy.ServiceProxy "/s", S req cli = node.create_client S, "/s" ; cli.call_async req rospy.Time.now node.get_clock .now rospy.loginfo ... node.get_logger .info ... The main shift in thinking: the while loop with rate.sleep is replaced by a timer and callbacks , and a synchronous service call inside a callback by an asynchronous one, otherwise the node will block itself the same executor services the response . MAVROS 1 → MAVROS 2 The topic names are mostly the same /mavros/state , /mavros/local_position/pose , /mavros/setpoint_position/local , but: telemetry QoS is sensor data; some services and parameters have been renamed; launch is ros2 launch mavros apm.launch fcu_url:=... or px4.launch . For PX4 in ROS 2, people usually move from MAVROS to uXRCE-DDS module ros2-px4 ; for ArduPilot — to AP_DDS where its features are enough module ros2-ardupilot . {{diagram:ros1-migration What to do with an old ROS 1 project: a temporary bridge, a port, MAVROS 2, or a rewrite based on its ideas.}} practice Step 1. Reading the project Take an open ROS 1 drone project for example, the offboard example from the PX4 documentation for ROS 1 / MAVROS, or any repository with MAVROS 1 . In 30 minutes, draw the node graph, the list of dependencies and where the project controls the vehicle. Step 2. Reference data If you can, run the project in a ROS 1 Noetic container with SITL and record a rosbag of the node's inputs and outputs. If not, use a bag from open sources or synthetic inputs. Step 3. Porting Port one node up to ~200 lines : the logic without ROS goes into a separate module with pytest tests like offboard_fsm.py , the node is a thin rclpy wrapper. Convert the bag to the ROS 2 format the rosbags package: rosbags-convert and check that the outputs of the ported node match the reference ones. Step 4. Report A table: what was replaced, how many lines of logic became testable without ROS, what behavior differences were found usually QoS and time . The lab counts as done when you have the graph of the original project, the ported node with logic tests and a comparison of the outputs on the same data. diagnostics - Symptom: the ported node “hangs” on a service call - Possible cause: a synchronous call in a callback of a single-threaded executor. - What to do: call_async + handling the future, or a separate callback group. - Symptom: the node doesn't receive MAVROS 2 telemetry - Possible cause: QoS sensor data on the publisher or a different topic name. - What to do: ros2 topic info -v , the subscription profile. - Symptom: parameters “don't apply” - Possible cause: in ROS 2 a parameter must be declared declare_parameter and passed to a specific node. - What to do: declare it in the constructor, YAML with the node name in launch. - Symptom:

title: PID
summary: Proportional-integral-derivative controller: P reacts to the current error, I accumulates the steady-state error, D damps fast changes.

title: Feedforward (FF)
summary: A contribution to the motor command taken directly from stick movement, before any error appears. Speeds up the start of a move.

title: Setpoint
summary: The desired angular rate (from sticks and rates) that the PID compares the gyro readings against.

title: Gyro
summary: A three-axis angular rate sensor. The main stabilization sensor, read thousands of times per second.

title: T/W (thrust-to-weight)
summary: The ratio of the maximum thrust of all motors to the takeoff weight. 2:1 is the minimum for controlled flight.

title: Mixer
summary: A table that converts throttle, roll, pitch and yaw into a command for each motor depending on the frame type.

title: KV
summary: Motor RPM per volt with no load. Low KV for big props, high KV for small ones.

title: ESC
summary: Electronic speed controller: commutates the phases of a brushless motor based on commands from the FC.

title: DShot
summary: A digital FC → ESC protocol: a 16-bit packet with a checksum, no calibration. The number is the speed in kbit/s.

title: Bidirectional DShot
summary: DShot with a return channel: the ESC reports motor eRPM. The basis of the RPM filter.

title: RPM filter
summary: A bank of narrow notch filters at each motor's rotation frequency and its harmonics, driven by bidirectional DShot data.

title: Dynamic notch
summary: An automatic notch filter that finds peaks in the gyro spectrum and suppresses them.

title: D-term
summary: The derivative term of the PID. Sensitive to noise: with poor filtering it heats up the motors.

title: Blackbox
summary: Betaflight log: gyro, setpoint, PID, motors, RC at a high rate, for post-flight analysis.

title: Bounce-back
summary: Gyro rebound in the opposite direction after the stick stops; a metric of underdamping.

title: Entry lag
summary: Time from the start of a setpoint move until the gyro reaches 50% of it. The "sluggish on the sticks" metric.

title: Propwash
summary: Shaking when the vehicle flies into its own turbulent downwash, usually during descent.

title: diff all
summary: A Betaflight CLI command that outputs only the differences of the configuration from the defaults. The unit for storing a config.

title: Resource remap
summary: Reassigning a function (motor, UART, LED) to another board pad via the CLI.

title: craft_name
summary: The craft name in the Betaflight config. A reliable drone identifier for scripts instead of a COM port number.

title: UART
summary: Serial port: receiver, GPS, VTX, telemetry. Wires crossed over, common GND.

title: Inverted signal
summary: UART with inverted logic levels: idle is low. The SBUS standard; F4 can't invert in hardware.

title: SBUS
summary: A receiver → FC protocol from Futaba/FrSky: 100 kbaud, 8E2, inverted, one-way.

title: CRSF
summary: The TBS Crossfire and ExpressLRS protocol: a regular UART, full duplex, channels and telemetry over a single port.

title: ELRS (ExpressLRS)
summary: An open-source radio control system: choice of packet rate, telemetry ratio, 2.4 GHz and 900 MHz.

title: Packet rate
summary: The number of control packets per second. Higher means lower latency and worse sensitivity.

title: LQ (link quality)
summary: Fraction of successful packets out of the last 100. RSSI is the power margin; you need both together.

title: VTX
summary: Video transmitter. Controlled by the FC over SmartAudio/Tramp/MSP according to the VTX table.

title: vtxtable
summary: The table of VTX bands, channels and power levels in Betaflight. FACTORY sends the channel number, CUSTOM sends the frequency.

title: OSD
summary: Telemetry overlaid on the video in the goggles: voltage, time, link, warnings.

title: Arming disable flags
summary: Betaflight flags that prevent arming (RXLOSS, THROTTLE, ANGLE, MSP…). Visible via status and in the OSD.

title: Failsafe
summary: Behavior on link loss. In Betaflight: Stage 1 (guard time) and Stage 2 (DROP, AUTO-LAND, GPS_RESCUE).

title: BEC
summary: An onboard voltage regulator (5/9/12 V) for the FC, receiver, camera and VTX.

title: C rating
summary: A battery's rated discharge current as a multiple of its capacity. Usually inflated; trust the log and the internal resistance.

title: Voltage sag
summary: The voltage drop under current across the battery's internal resistance: I × R.

title: Cloud Build
summary: Building Betaflight firmware on the server for a selected set of options (defines).

title: Target
summary: A firmware variant for a specific board: MCU, gyro, pins.

title: ArduPilot
summary: An open-source autopilot: Copter, Plane, Rover, Sub. Navigation, missions, Lua, companion.

title: FRAME_CLASS / FRAME_TYPE
summary: ArduPilot parameters: frame type (Quad=1, Hexa=2, Octa=3, OctaQuad=4, Tri=7) and layout (X=1, Plus=0…).

title: Pre-arm checks
summary: ArduPilot checks before arming: calibrations, EKF, link, parameters. A PreArm message is a hint, not an obstacle.

title: GCS
summary: Ground control station: Mission Planner, QGroundControl, MAVProxy. Talks to the FC over MAVLink.

title: SITL
summary: Software In The Loop: the real firmware running on a PC with a physics simulator in place of sensors.

title: MAVProxy
summary: ArduPilot's command-line ground station in Python. Launched together with SITL.

title: pymavlink
summary: Python MAVLink library: connection, reading messages, commands. Low level, everything visible.

title: MAVSDK
summary: A high-level SDK on top of MAVLink (C++, Python): arm(), takeoff(), telemetry subscriptions.

title: MAVLink
summary: The FC ↔ GCS/companion protocol: packets with a message ID, system_id, component_id and a CRC based on the XML definition.

title: Heartbeat
summary: A MAVLink message sent once per second by every participant: type, mode, armed state. No heartbeat, no link.

title: COMMAND_ACK
summary: MAVLink command acknowledgment with a result. A command without an ACK check is hope, not control.

title: GUIDED
summary: An ArduPilot mode in which position/velocity targets are set by an external source (GCS, companion).

title: NED
summary: North-East-Down coordinate frame: Z points down, climbing is negative Z.

title: EKF
summary: Extended Kalman filter: fuses IMU, GPS, baro and compass into a single estimate of position, velocity and attitude.

title: Lane switching
summary: EKF switching between cores (per IMU) to a healthier one.

title: DCM
summary: A simple complementary attitude filter in ArduPilot. A backup to the EKF; works without GPS and compass.

title: DataFlash
summary: ArduPilot's onboard binary log (.bin): VIBE, ATT, CTUN, BAT, ERR, XKF and hundreds of other messages.

title: VIBE
summary: An ArduPilot log message with per-axis vibration and an accelerometer clipping counter. Below 30 is normal.

title: Mission
summary: A list of commands for AUTO mode: NAV (where to go), DO (what to do), CONDITION (when).

title: Home
summary: Copter's arming point. RTL returns here, not to the pilot.

title: Lua scripts (ArduPilot)
summary: Onboard scripts: switches, sensors, scenarios. Require ≥2 MB of flash, do not run on F4.

title: Fault injection
summary: Deliberate injection of failures (motor, sensor) in SITL to test the behavior of the vehicle and the pilot.

title: OctaQuad (X8)
summary: Four arms with two coaxial motors each. Fault tolerance at the cost of ~15% thrust loss.

title: QuadPlane
summary: VTOL in ArduPlane: takes off like a multirotor, flies like a plane.

title: Tilt-rotor
summary: VTOL with tilting motors. Q_TILT_* parameters, TiltMotor* output functions.

title: SERVOn_FUNCTION
summary: The function of an FC output in ArduPilot: motor, tilt servo, control surface. A mismatch with the wiring is dangerous.

title: Companion computer
summary: An onboard computer for vision, scenarios, networking. It advises via GUIDED; the FC decides.

title: mavlink-router
summary: A MAVLink router: one UART, many consumers over UDP/TCP.

title: systemd service
summary: A way to start a script on a Linux companion automatically and restart it after a crash.

title: EdgeTX
summary: Open-source radio firmware (TX16S and others) with Lua scripts and an AUX port in Lua mode.

title: ESP32
summary: A microcontroller with Wi-Fi and BLE: peripherals, MAVLink bridge, radio companion.

title: Kt (torque constant)
summary: Motor torque per amp of current, Kt = 60/(2π·KV) N·m/A; low KV = high torque per amp.

title: FSPL
summary: Free-space signal loss: 20·log(d) + 20·log(f) + 32.44 dB; +6 dB per doubling of range.

title: Link budget
summary: The sum of power, antenna gains and losses minus FSPL versus receiver sensitivity; margin ≥ 10–15 dB.

title: SWR
summary: Standing wave ratio: the fraction of power reflected by the antenna back into the transmitter; 1.0 is ideal, ≤ 2 is acceptable.

title: Circular polarization
summary: The field rotates (RHCP/LHCP); less sensitive to orientation and reflections; never mix RHCP and LHCP.

title: Low-ESR capacitor
summary: An electrolytic/polymer capacitor on the power bus that absorbs voltage spikes caused by wire inductance during ESC switching.

title: Smoke stopper
summary: A current limiter (bulb/resistor) in series with the positive lead at first power-up: a short circuit won't burn the board.

title: Hard iron / soft iron
summary: Compass errors: a constant offset from magnetized parts (hard iron) and field distortion from ferromagnetic materials (soft iron); calibrated with offsets and a matrix.

title: Bias
summary: The sensor output at zero input; for a gyro it integrates into attitude drift; estimated by the EKF.

title: Quaternion
summary: Four numbers with unit norm describing attitude without gimbal lock; the firmware standard.

title: Complementary filter
summary: Fusing the gyro (high frequencies) with the accelerometer/compass (low frequencies) using fixed coefficients; a special case of the Kalman filter.

title: Innovation
summary: The difference between a measurement and the filter's prediction; if the normalized innovation exceeds the gate, the measurement is rejected.

title: Kalman gain
summary: The weight given to a measurement versus the prediction, computed from the covariances; the adaptive counterpart of the complementary filter's K.

title: HDOP
summary: A multiplier on GNSS horizontal error due to satellite geometry; < 1 is excellent, > 2.5 is poor.

title: RTK
summary: Real-Time Kinematic: carrier-phase corrections from a base station give centimeter accuracy; requires a pair of dual-frequency receivers.

title: Optical flow
summary: The angular rate of the image moving under the camera; combined with rangefinder altitude and the gyro, it gives linear velocity.

title: EK3_SRC
summary: EKF3 source sets (position, velocity, altitude, heading): GPS, baro, rangefinder, optical flow, external navigation; switchable in flight.

title: Phase margin
summary: Degrees short of −180° at the loop's unity-gain frequency; delay eats into it linearly with frequency.

title: Damping ζ
summary: A parameter of a second-order loop: ζ ≈ 0.7 gives ~5% overshoot; low ζ means bounce-back and ringing.

title: Aliasing
summary: Frequencies above fs/2 showing up at false frequencies after sampling; fixed with an anti-aliasing filter and full-rate logging.

title: Group delay
summary: The delay a filter adds to the useful signal; PT1 ≈ 1/(2π·fc).

title: Welch's method
summary: Spectrum estimation by averaging FFTs over overlapping windows; resolution fs/nperseg.

title: Overshoot
summary: Response overshoot past the setpoint after a step, in percent; related to damping.

title: TECS
summary: Total energy control for a wing: throttle sets the total energy, the elevator sets the split between altitude and airspeed.

title: Stall speed
summary: V_s = √(2mg/(ρ·S·C_Lmax)); in a turn it grows as 1/√cos φ.

title: Stability margin
summary: The distance of the CG ahead of the neutral point as a fraction of MAC; 5–15% is normal.

title: Harmonic notch (ArduPilot)
summary: Harmonic notch filter `INS_HNTCH_*` with tracking by throttle, ESC telemetry or FFT.

title: AUTOTUNE
summary: Automatic tuning of rate/angle gains from a series of "twitches" on an axis in hover.

title: FMEA
summary: Failure Modes and Effects Analysis: failure → effect → detection → RPN → mitigation → verification.

title: Dead reckoning
summary: Dead reckoning from inertial sensors and wind without external measurements; accurate for seconds to tens of seconds.

title: DroneCAN
summary: A protocol over CAN for autopilot peripherals: nodes with IDs, standard messages, 120 Ω terminators.

title: CAN arbitration
summary: Resolving simultaneous transmission: a dominant 0 wins, the lower ID wins without losing time.

title: DMA
summary: Direct memory access: peripherals exchange data with memory without the CPU (DShot, SPI gyro, UART).

title: Jitter
summary: Variation in a task's actual period; grows with locking and long interrupts.

title: Work queue (PX4)
summary: Prioritized work queues in which most PX4 modules run on NuttX.

title: Traceability matrix
summary: A requirement ↔ test ↔ result table; empty cells are open requirements.

title: ADR
summary: Architecture Decision Record: context, options, decision, consequences.

title: VIO
summary: Visual-inertial odometry: position and attitude from features in frames and the IMU; drift of 0.5–2% of distance traveled.

title: ExternalNav
summary: External navigation source for EKF3 (VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE/ODOMETRY), `EK3_SRC* = 6`.

title: Precision / Recall
summary: Fraction of correct detections among those found / fraction found among the true ones; the confidence threshold trades one for the other.

title: Glass-to-glass latency
summary: Time from an event in front of the camera to its appearance on the screen; measured with a timer in the frame.

title: Offboard (PX4)
summary: Control mode from a companion with a setpoint stream ≥ 2 Hz; timeout COM_OF_LOSS_T.

title: Spot welding
summary: Spot welding nickel strip to 18650/21700 cells; soldering to cells is not allowed.

title: BMS
summary: Battery management system: voltage/current/temperature protection and balancing; cutting off discharge in flight is dangerous.

title: Thrust stand
summary: Measuring a motor's thrust/current/power with a prop; checking the build sheet's calculations against reality.

title: Engineering folder
summary: Requirements with IDs, tests and a project changelog are a mandatory part of every capstone project.

title: Troubleshooting tree
summary: A "symptom → branch → measurement → cause" sequence of checks for finding a fault.

title: Near miss
summary: A near miss with no damage; the main source of improvements to the field protocol.

title: L1 navigation
summary: ArduPlane's guidance algorithm: the vehicle aims at a point on the route line a distance L1 ahead and commands lateral acceleration based on the angle to it. The NAVL1_PERIOD sets how aggressive it is.

title: Pure pursuit
summary: "Pursuit" guidance: a point at lookahead distance L is chosen on the path, and the vehicle turns toward it with curvature 2·sin(η)/L. A larger L is smoother but cuts corners.

title: S-curve (jerk-limited)
summary: A jerk-limited velocity profile: acceleration ramps up smoothly instead of stepping. This is how ArduPilot (WP_JERK) and PX4 build trajectories.

title: Chirp
summary: A test signal whose frequency rises smoothly from f₀ to f₁. The response to it is used to build the loop's frequency response.

title: Coherence
summary: A measure from 0 to 1 of how much of the output is linearly explained by the input at a given frequency. Below ~0.6, a point on the frequency response is not worth using.

title: AP_Periph
summary: ArduPilot firmware for DroneCAN peripheral nodes: GPS, compass, airspeed sensor, ESC adapter on a separate STM32.

title: Node ID
summary: A node's number on the DroneCAN bus (1–127). Set statically or assigned by the dynamic node allocation (DNA) server on the autopilot.

title: Conducted interference
summary: Noise conducted along power and ground wires (ripple from ESCs and converters), not through the air. Fixed with an LC filter and a low-ESR capacitor at the source.

title: DRC
summary: Design Rule Check: automatic check of a board for clearances, trace widths and vias against the fab's rules. Zero DRC errors is the condition for sending it to production.

title: Gerber
summary: The set of board layer files (copper, solder mask, silkscreen, outline) plus a drill file: what the fab receives.

title: Clamp meter
summary: An instrument that measures current from the magnetic field around a wire without breaking the circuit. DC requires a Hall-effect clamp.

title: Fault tolerance
summary: The vehicle's ability to survive the failure of a single component (motor, BEC, receiver) and land under control. A quadcopter does not have it for motors; a hexa and an X8 can, given spare thrust, well-designed power and a firmware response verified in SITL or on a bench.

title: Cold solder joint
summary: A cold solder joint: dull, lumpy, with poor wetting. Holds on the bench and fails under vibration.

title: Strain relief
summary: Securing a wire near a solder joint or connector so bending and vibration don't break the strands at the joint.

title: Config diff
summary: A line-by-line comparison of two parameter dumps. A config in git plus a diff before flight shows what changed since last time.

title: Weight budget
summary: A table of the weights of all components versus the target takeoff weight. Determines the thrust-to-weight ratio and flight time before you buy anything.

title: Ohm's law
summary: U = I·R: the voltage across an element equals the current times the resistance. Power P = U·I.

title: Bluejay
summary: Open-source firmware for ESCs on 8-bit EFM8 BB21 and BB51 (BB1 only up to version 0.18.1), the successor to BLHeli_S, with bidirectional DShot for the RPM filter.

title: AM32
summary: Open-source firmware for 32-bit ARM ESCs (STM32, AT32, GD32, etc.), a replacement for BLHeli_32.

title: Frame resonance
summary: The frequency at which a frame or arm oscillates on its own. If it matches the motor speed frequency, vibration grows and the gyros get noisy.

title: Moment of inertia
summary: A measure of resistance to rotation: J = Σ m·r². Mass far from the center makes the vehicle sluggish in roll and pitch.

title: Remote ID
summary: Broadcasting the ID, coordinates and altitude of the vehicle and the pilot during flight (Bluetooth / Wi-Fi). A regulatory requirement in many countries.

title: MAVLink signing
summary: A MAVLink 2 mechanism: every packet is signed with a shared secret key and a timestamp. Rejects foreign commands and replays of intercepted ones.

title: Scheduler
summary: The part of the firmware that runs tasks at a given rate and priority: gyro loop, PID, RX, OSD. The first thing you look for when reading the source.

title: Position hold
summary: GPS position hold mode: the vehicle counters wind drift by itself. In INAV it is NAV POSHOLD.

title: INAV
summary: A Cleanflight fork with navigation: position hold, RTH, missions, wings and rovers.

title: Logic condition (INAV)
summary: A line of the INAV Programming Framework: a condition on flags and values whose result triggers an action or feeds other conditions.

title: Waypoint
summary: A mission waypoint: coordinates, altitude and an action (fly-through, loiter, RTH, landing).

title: Elevons
summary: The two control surfaces of a flying wing that combine elevator and ailerons: deflected together for pitch, in opposite directions for roll.

title: OpenIPC
summary: Open-source firmware for IP cameras that turns them into a digital FPV transmitter over Wi-Fi adapters in packet injection mode.

title: SiK
summary: Open-source firmware for 433/868/915 MHz telemetry modems with frequency hopping; used by 3DR Radio and RFD900.

title: Rotation matrix
summary: An orthogonal 3×3 matrix with determinant 1 that transforms a vector from one coordinate frame to another. Its inverse equals its transpose.

title: Gimbal lock
summary: Loss of one degree of freedom in Euler angles at ±90° pitch: roll and yaw become the same axis. That is why quaternions are used internally.

title: Natural frequency ωn
summary: The frequency at which an undamped second-order system oscillates. Together with ζ it sets the settling time and overshoot.

title: Euler method
summary: The simplest numerical integration: x(t+dt) = x(t) + f(x)·dt. Unstable with a large step, hence the loop-rate requirements.

title: Covariance
summary: A measure of how two quantities vary together. The EKF covariance matrix describes how confident the filter is in each component of the state.

title: Component ID
summary: A component's number within a vehicle in MAVLink (autopilot 1, camera 100, gimbal 154, etc.). Together with the system ID it forms the address.

title: System ID
summary: The vehicle's number on a MAVLink network (1–255). Two vehicles on the same network must have different ones: in ArduPilot 4.7 the parameter is MAV_SYSID.

title: CRC_EXTRA
summary: A byte computed from the message definition and mixed into the MAVLink CRC. Catches dialect version mismatches between sender and receiver.

title: MAVLink dialect
summary: XML description of a message set (common, ardupilotmega, development). Both sides must be built from the same dialect.

title: UDP broadcast / unicast
summary: Ways of delivering MAVLink over a network: broadcast goes to everyone on the subnet, unicast goes to a single address. Over 4G/NAT and L3 VPNs (WireGuard, Tailscale, OpenVPN tun) only unicast works; broadcast only passes through L2 tunnels (ZeroTier, OpenVPN tap).

title: MAVROS
summary: A ROS package that bridges MAVLink to ROS topics and services. Superseded by uXRCE-DDS for PX4; for ArduPilot it remains alongside AP_DDS.

title: MAVLink microservice
summary: A protocol on top of messages for one task: parameters, missions, commands, FTP. Defines the exchange order and retries on packet loss.

title: Root cause
summary: The cause lies in the process, not in a person or a part: why the failure was possible at all. You eliminate it, or the crash repeats with a different part.

title: Vehicle log
summary: A record of flight time, battery cycles, replacements and incidents for each vehicle. The basis for life-based scheduled maintenance.

title: Density altitude
summary: The altitude in the standard atmosphere with the same air density as right now. Heat and high elevation raise it, and props produce less thrust.

title: Gimbal Manager
summary: A role in the MAVLink Gimbal v2 protocol: the component that parses requests from the GCS and companion and commands the gimbal (Gimbal Device).

title: OBSTACLE_DISTANCE
summary: A MAVLink message with 72 sectors of distances to obstacles around the vehicle. ArduPilot and PX4 use it to brake and avoid.

title: INT8 quantization
summary: Converting network weights and activations from float to 8-bit integers. Speeds up inference 2–4× on NPU/TensorRT at the cost of a small accuracy loss; verified on a validation set.

title: Camera matrix K
summary: Camera intrinsics: focal lengths f_x, f_y in pixels and the principal point c_x, c_y. Maps a ray to a pixel and back; found by checkerboard calibration.

title: LANDING_TARGET
summary: A MAVLink message the companion uses to send the autopilot the angular offset or position of a marker for precision landing.

title: GSD
summary: Ground Sample Distance: how many centimeters of ground one image pixel covers. GSD = altitude · pixel size / focal length.

title: Image overlap
summary: The fraction of shared area between adjacent frames along and across the route. For photogrammetry it is usually 70–80 % along and 60–70 % across.

title: Image-plane error
summary: The target's offset from the image center (or a set point) in pixels or normalized coordinates. The outer tracking loop turns it into a velocity command.

title: Jetson Orin
summary: A family of NVIDIA modules with an Ampere GPU (Orin NX/AGX also have DLA accelerators) for onboard inference. A typical companion for PX4 and ArduPilot.

title: uORB
summary: PX4's internal publish-subscribe message bus between modules. uXRCE-DDS exposes selected uORB topics to ROS 2.

title: Cascaded controller
summary: Nested loops: position commands velocity, velocity commands angle, angle commands angular rate. The inner loop is tuned first and made several times faster than the outer one.

title: Lifecycle node
summary: A ROS 2 node with explicit unconfigured → inactive → active states and transitions between them. Gives controlled startup and shutdown of an onboard application.

title: AP_DDS
summary: The eProsima Micro XRCE-DDS client built into ArduPilot: publishes state to ROS 2 and accepts commands without MAVLink; on the ROS 2 side it is served by an agent (`micro_ros_agent` or Micro XRCE-DDS Agent).

title: QoS
summary: Quality of Service in ROS 2: reliability, queue depth, durability. A publisher and a subscriber with incompatible QoS don't connect, and there is no error: the subscriber simply receives nothing (the log only shows an "incompatible QoS" warning).

title: tf2
summary: The ROS library for the tree of coordinate frames over time: map → odom → base_link → camera. Answers where the sensor was at the moment a frame was captured.

title: ros1_bridge
summary: A bridge that forwards topics between ROS 1 and ROS 2 during a migration. Requires both distributions to be installed side by side.

title: Costmap
summary: A costmap in Nav2: cells weighted by traversability, built from obstacles with an inflation margin. Paths are planned on it.

title: uXRCE-DDS
summary: The PX4 bridge to ROS 2: a client in the firmware and the Micro XRCE-DDS Agent on the companion pass uORB topics as ROS 2 topics.

title: SDF
summary: Simulation Description Format: XML description of a Gazebo world and models: links, joints, sensors, plugins.

title: Flight Review
summary: PX4's web service for analyzing ULog logs: setpoint tracking, vibration, spectrograms and step-response estimation with no software to install.

title: UART port (TX/RX)
summary: Serial port: TX of one device goes to RX of the other. In Betaflight each UART is assigned a function on the Ports tab.

title: Ground loop
summary: A closed loop through the common wire via two ground paths, where noise current is induced. Fixed by joining grounds at a single point.

title: VLOS / BVLOS
summary: Visual Line of Sight: flying within the pilot's direct sight, the baseline requirement of most regulations. BVLOS (beyond visual line of sight) requires a separate authorization or category.

title: Figure of merit (FM)
summary: Коэффициент качества винта на висении: отношение идеальной мощности по теории импульсов T^1.5/√(2ρA) к реально затраченной. Системный FM считают от электрической мощности из таблицы мотора — у малых пропов с мотором и ESC это 0.5–0.6.

title: Нагрузка на диск (disc loading)
summary: Тяга, делённая на суммарную площадь дисков пропов, Н/м². Удельная мощность висения растёт как корень из неё: чем больше диск при той же массе, тем больше граммов на ватт.

title: Массовая доля
summary: Часть взлётной массы, приходящаяся на группу (рама, АКБ, груз, силовая установка). Позволяет замкнуть бюджет: m = масса без рамы / (1 − доля рамы).

title: Тензодатчик (load cell)
summary: Упругий элемент с мостом Уитстона из тензорезисторов: выход пропорционален силе и напряжению возбуждения (чувствительность в мВ/В, типично 1.0 мВ/В на полную шкалу). Основа тягового стенда и весов.

title: HX711
summary: 24-битный АЦП для тензомоста: канал A с усилением 128 или 64, канал B — 32, 10 или 80 отсчётов/с, последовательный вывод по линиям DOUT/PD_SCK. PD_SCK в высоком уровне дольше 60 мкс переводит чип в power-down.

title: Нейтральная точка
summary: Положение центра тяжести, при котором момент тангажа самолёта не зависит от угла атаки (dCm/dα = 0). ЦТ ставят впереди неё на величину статического запаса: 5–15 % САХ, у летающего крыла 5–10 %.

title: Коэффициент объёма ГО (V_h)
summary: V_h = S_h·l_h/(S·САХ): площадь горизонтального оперения на плечо, отнесённые к площади и САХ крыла. Чем он больше, тем дальше назад нейтральная точка; у тренеров и FPV-самолётов обычно 0.4–0.7.

title: Поляра сопротивления
summary: Зависимость C_D от C_L, обычно C_D = C_D0 + k·C_L², k = 1/(π·e·AR). Из неё получают максимальное качество, скорость максимальной дальности V_md и скорость минимальной мощности V_mp.

title: Матрица эффективности (effectiveness matrix)
summary: Матрица B размером 6×N: столбец i — моменты и силы, которые даёт мотор i при единичной команде. В PX4 считается из CA_ROTORn_* по формуле M = CT·(p × a) − CT·KM·a, F = CT·a; миксер — её (псевдо)обратная.

title: Псевдообратная матрица
summary: Обобщение обратной матрицы для неквадратных и вырожденных B: даёт решение B·u = цель с минимальной нормой u (или ближайшее в смысле наименьших квадратов). PX4 строит так миксер для любой геометрии и пересчитывает его при отказе мотора.

title: Десатурация миксера
summary: Сдвиг команд моторов вдоль вектора одной оси, чтобы вернуть их в диапазон 0…1. Порядок задаёт приоритет: в PX4 тяга, затем крен/тангаж, рыскание режется первым; airmode разрешает поднимать тягу ради управления.

title: vbat_scale / ibata_scale
summary: Коэффициенты датчиков напряжения и тока Betaflight. Напряжение прямо пропорционально vbat_scale (new = old × V_мультиметр / V_FC), ток обратно пропорционален ibata_scale в мВ на 10 А (new = old × мА·ч_FC / мА·ч_зарядки).

title: motor_output_reordering
summary: Массив Betaflight 4.5: мотор миксера i выводится на пад MOTOR с индексом reordering[i]. Исправляет порядок моторов без перепайки и без ремаппинга таймеров; его пишет диалог Reorder motors.

title: Первое висение (maiden hover)
summary: Первый подъём собранного аппарата на 1–1.5 м на 60 с в ANGLE с записью Blackbox и заранее заданными критериями прерывания: переворот при отрыве, осцилляции, газ висения вне 12–60 %, горячие моторы.

title: vbat_scale (INAV)
summary: Коэффициент делителя напряжения в INAV (1100 = делитель 11:1 × 100). Показания прямо пропорциональны ему: new = old × V_мультиметр / V_INAV.

title: current_meter_offset
summary: Смещение нуля датчика тока в INAV; по исходнику в единицах 0.1 мВ, убирает из показаний offset/scale ампер. Калибруется по току покоя: new = old + (I_INAV − I_амперметр) × scale.

title: MSP RX
summary: Приём RC-каналов по протоколу MSP (MSP_SET_RAW_RC) вместо радиоприёмника; в INAV SITL — способ подать стики скриптом или с наземной станции (receiver_type = MSP).

title: Servo autotrim
summary: Автоматическая подстройка центров серв (servo mid) в ровном полёте: INAV усредняет отклонение рулей и сохраняет новые центры при дизарме. Режим SERVO AUTOTRIM или feature FW_AUTOTRIM.

title: Расход руля
summary: Угол отклонения поверхности управления от нейтрали при полном стике. На крыле измеряется линейкой по задней кромке: h = c·sin δ.

title: Loiter (кружение)
summary: Полёт крыла по кругу заданного радиуса вокруг точки вместо висения. Нужный крен: tan φ = V²/(g·R), он ограничен nav_fw_bank_angle.

title: Загрузчик ArduPilot (.apj / _with_bl.hex)
summary: Маленькая программа в начале флеша, которая принимает новую прошивку по USB. Первый раз её пишут вместе с прошивкой файлом _with_bl.hex через DFU; дальше обновляют файлом .apj из Mission Planner или QGroundControl.

title: MOT_SPIN_ARM / MOT_SPIN_MIN
summary: Доли выхода на моторы в ArduCopter: SPIN_ARM — обороты сразу после арма, SPIN_MIN — нижняя граница управляемой тяги (не меньше SPIN_ARM + 0.03). Подбираются по порогу трогания в Motor Test.

title: MOT_THST_HOVER
summary: Тяга висения ArduCopter в долях от максимальной (≈ 1/(T/W)); обучается в полёте при MOT_HOVER_LEARN = 2. Рабочий диапазон 0.2–0.5.

title: ULog
summary: Формат бортового лога PX4 (.ulg): записывает выбранные топики uORB с временными метками, параметры и сообщения; разбирается Flight Review или pyulog.

title: SIH (Simulation-In-Hardware)
summary: Встроенный в PX4 упрощённый симулятор физики: модель считается внутри прошивки (на ПК как SITL или на самом полётнике), без Gazebo и без внешнего визуализатора.

title: Control allocation (CA_*)
summary: Блок PX4, который раскладывает требуемые моменты и тягу по исполнителям по заданной геометрии: CA_ROTOR_COUNT, позиции CA_ROTORn_PX/PY и направление вращения CA_ROTORn_KM.

title: adjrange
summary: CLI-команда Betaflight для подстроек в полёте: adjrange <слот 0–29> 0 <канал диапазона> <start> <end> <функция> <канал подстройки> [<center> <scale>]. Номер функции — позиция в defaultAdjustmentConfigs[] + 1, в 4.5 с 25-го не совпадает с enum. Изменения живут в RAM до сохранения.

title: Шаговая и абсолютная подстройка
summary: Два режима adjrange. Шаговый (center = 0): канал выше mid_rc + 200 даёт +1, ниже mid_rc − 200 даёт −1, повтор каждые 500 мс. Абсолютный (center ≠ 0): значение = center + (rc − 1500)·scale/500 при каждом изменении канала, с прыжком при включении слота.

title: vtx (VTX на тумблере)
summary: CLI-команда Betaflight vtx <слот 0–9> <aux> <band> <channel> <power> <start> <end>: задаёт бэнд, канал и индекс мощности VTX по положению AUX-канала. Слоты проверяются на каждом RC-кадре, слот, сработавший в прошлый раз, пропускается — перекрывающиеся слоты по очереди перебивают друг друга; бэнд и канал меняются только до первого арма, мощность — всегда.

title: Actual rates
summary: Модель рейтов Betaflight (дефолт с 4.3): rc_rate×10 — чувствительность в центре, srate×10 — максимум в °/с, expo меняет только форму кривой между ними.

title: Super rate
summary: Параметр модели Betaflight: делит угловую скорость на (1 − |x|·s), поднимая край кривой стика; вместе с RC rate задаёт максимум 200·r/(1 − s).

title: RC smoothing
summary: PT3-фильтр setpoint, газа и feedforward на частоте PID-цикла; в авто-режиме срез = max(15, ⌊f_rx·1.5/(1 + factor/10)⌋) Гц по измеренной частоте пакетов.

title: Runaway takeoff prevention
summary: Защита Betaflight от «taz» на первом взлёте: дизарм и флаг RUNAWAY, если |pidSum| ≥ 600 при вращении быстрее 15 °/с (рыскание 50 °/с) дольше 75 мс. Отключается до перезагрузки после 500 мс уверенного полёта (газ ≥ 20 % со стиком или ≥ 40 %).

title: Yaw spin recovery
summary: Режим Betaflight при раскрутке по рысканию выше порога (AUTO: max_yaw + max(25 %, 200 °/с), 500–1950 °/с): обнуляет крен/тангаж и I, отдаёт всю тягу на остановку вращения, выходит на 100 °/с ниже порога через 20 мс.

title: PREARM
summary: Режим Betaflight — второй ключ арма: при заданном диапазоне арм возможен только при включённом PREARM, и после каждого арма его нужно переключить (флаг NOPREARM). В 2025.12 переключение можно отменить параметром prearm_allow_rearm.

title: MSP DisplayPort
summary: Протокол, по которому полётник через UART сообщает цифровым очкам (DJI, Walksnail, HDZero), какой символ нарисовать в какой клетке сетки OSD. В Betaflight 4.4+ — функция порта VTX (MSP + DisplayPort): маска 131073 = MSP + VTX_MSP; в ArduPilot SERIALn_PROTOCOL = 42 и OSD_TYPE = 5.

title: Канва HD OSD (osd_canvas)
summary: Размер сетки символов HD OSD в столбцах и строках. В Betaflight 4.5 по умолчанию 53×20, но очки сообщают свою (HDZero — 50×18) командой MSP_SET_OSD_CANVAS. Элементы за пределами канвы прошивка прижимает к краю, а не масштабирует.

title: VTX_MSP (функция порта 131072)
summary: Бит 1 << 17 маски serial в Betaflight: управление VTX и DisplayPort по MSP. Один, без MSP или Serial RX, он недопустим — isSerialConfigValid() сбрасывает весь конфиг портов к умолчаниям.

title: NTRIP
summary: Networked Transport of RTCM via Internet Protocol: HTTP-подобный протокол, по которому кастер (обычно порт 2101) раздаёт потоки RTCM-поправок по точкам монтирования (mount points); клиент — GCS или модем ровера.

title: Moving baseline (GPS yaw)
summary: Режим RTK, где база стоит на той же раме: ровер решает вектор между антеннами с сантиметровой точностью, его направление — курс аппарата. В ArduPilot GPS1_TYPE 17 / GPS2_TYPE 18 и EK3_SRC1_YAW 2; курс есть ещё на земле, без движения.

title: Survey-in
summary: Режим базовой станции u-blox (CFG-TMODE-MODE), в котором приёмник усредняет свою позицию до заданной длительности и предела точности; даёт относительную точность RTK в сантиметры, но абсолютную — в метры.

title: AGL (высота над рельефом)
summary: Above Ground Level: высота над землёй под аппаратом, h_AGL = h_AMSL − h_terrain. В миссии — frame MAV_FRAME_GLOBAL_TERRAIN_ALT (10); высоту рельефа ArduPilot берёт из бортовой базы (TERRAIN_ENABLE) или с дальномера. Не путать с высотой над точкой взлёта.

title: База рельефа (terrain database, SRTM)
summary: Сетка высот земли с шагом TERRAIN_SPACING (100 м), которую полётник ArduPilot запрашивает у GCS (TERRAIN_REQUEST / TERRAIN_DATA) и хранит на SD в APM/TERRAIN. Это модель поверхности с типичной ошибкой ±10 м: деревьев и зданий она толком не видит.

title: Surface tracking
summary: Удержание высоты над поверхностью по дальномеру в Loiter, AltHold и PosHold ArduCopter (SURFTRAK_MODE: 0 — выкл., 1 — земля, 2 — потолок). Когда дальномер выходит из диапазона, цель без предупреждения возвращается к баровысоте.

title: UWB (сверхширокополосные маяки)
summary: Ultra-Wideband: тег на аппарате измеряет дальности до неподвижных якорей по времени пролёта импульса, позиция получается трилатерацией с точностью 10–30 см в прямой видимости. В ArduPilot — BCN_TYPE (1 Pozyx, 3 Nooploop), не больше 4 якорей, EK3_SRC1_POSXY = 4; курс маяки не дают, нужен компас.

title: Motion capture (mocap)
summary: Система инфракрасных камер (OptiTrack, Vicon, Nokov), которая по отражающим маркерам выдаёт позу твёрдого тела с точностью до миллиметра на 100+ Гц. В автопилот попадает как VISION_POSITION_ESTIMATE / ODOMETRY (EK3_SRC1_* = 6) или как псевдо-GPS через GPS_INPUT; главные ловушки — оси, задержка и скачки.

title: EKF origin (начало координат EKF)
summary: Точка lat/lon/alt, от которой EKF считает локальную позицию NED. С GPS ставится сама при первом фиксе; без GPS её задаёт GCS или мост сообщением SET_GPS_GLOBAL_ORIGIN один раз до перезагрузки, иначе pre-arm «AHRS: waiting for home».

title: Привязка к карте (map matching)
summary: Абсолютная локализация по камере: кадр, выпрямленный по высоте и курсу, сопоставляется по признакам с геопривязанным ортофото; гомография с RANSAC переводит центр кадра в пиксель карты, а тот — в широту и долготу. Ошибка не растёт с пройденным путём, в отличие от визуальной одометрии.

title: VPR (visual place recognition)
summary: Грубая локализация по изображению: каждый тайл карты сжат в один глобальный дескриптор (NetVLAD, AnyLoc), кадр ищет k ближайших. Отвечает «на какой тайл похоже», координату и достоверность даёт только последующая геометрическая проверка локальными признаками.

title: GPS_INPUT
summary: Сообщение MAVLink #232: внешний источник выдаёт себя за GNSS-приёмник (lat/lon, скорость, fix_type, horiz_accuracy, ignore_flags). В ArduPilot принимается при GPSn_TYPE = 14; приёмник считается исправным при средней частоте около 5 Гц, а horiz_accuracy становится шумом измерения EKF3.

title: Glass-to-command (задержка контура зрения)
summary: Время от попадания света на сенсор до момента, когда команда по этой картинке принята автопилотом: экспозиция + readout + захват + undistort + детектор + трекер + геопривязка + транспорт. Измеряется по меткам времени каждой стадии; именно она, а не FPS, ограничивает усиление контура слежения.

title: Захват цели (target lock) и переприхват
summary: Правило выбора одного трека среди нескольких подтверждённых: держать ID, пока трек жив, а после потери брать новый только в радиусе от последней позиции. Без него трекер переключается на похожий неподвижный объект (камень, тень), который набирает больше попаданий, чем движущаяся цель.

title: TIMESYNC
summary: Сообщение MAVLink #111: companion шлёт ts1 (свои наносекунды, tc1 = 0), автопилот отвечает тем же ts1 и своим tc1. Смещение часов = tc1 − (ts1 + RTT/2); так метки времени кадров переводятся в time_boot_ms автопилота для сопоставления с ATTITUDE и логом.

title: nvpmodel (режим мощности Jetson)
summary: Утилита Jetson, задающая потолок потребления: сколько ядер CPU включено и максимальные частоты CPU, GPU и памяти. У Jetson Nano — MAXN (10 Вт, 4 ядра, GPU 921.6 МГц) и 5 Вт (2 ядра, GPU 640 МГц); у Orin Nano Super — 15 Вт, 25 Вт и MAXN_SUPER. Бюджет относится к шинам CPU и GPU, а не ко всей плате с периферией.

title: tegrastats
summary: Штатная утилита Jetson: раз в заданный интервал печатает строку с памятью, загрузкой и частотой каждого ядра CPU, загрузкой и частотой GPU (GR3D_FREQ), температурами зон и мощностью по шинам в мВт (POM_5V_IN у Nano, VDD_IN у Orin). Падение частоты GPU при полной загрузке — признак троттлинга.

title: TensorRT engine
summary: Скомпилированный под конкретный GPU и версию TensorRT план исполнения нейросети (файл .engine), получаемый из ONNX с выбранной точностью FP32, FP16 или INT8. Между платами не переносится: переносят ONNX, а engine собирают на целевом Jetson.

title: WS2812 (адресный светодиод)
summary: Светодиод со встроенным драйвером: 5 В, GND и одна линия данных 800 кГц, 24 бита на светодиод (GRB), цепочка DIN → DOUT. До ~60 мА при полном белом; вход считает «1» от 0.7·VDD, поэтому 3.3 В с FC на грани. В Betaflight — `resource LED_STRIP`, таймер и DMA пина, до 32 светодиодов (64 с LED_STRIP_64).

title: DShot beacon
summary: Писк моторами: Betaflight шлёт ESC DShot-команду BEACON1…5 (`beeper_dshot_beacon_tone`) по условиям RX_LOST и RX_SET команды `beacon` (в 4.5 по умолчанию оба выключены). Не в арме и не при работающих моторах, не раньше 1.2 с после дизарма, не чаще ~0.5 с (RX_SET) или ~1 с (RX_LOST).

title: Профиль ленты (RACE / BEACON / STATUS)
summary: `ledstrip_profile` Betaflight: STATUS — каждый светодиод по строке `led` (функции и оверлеи), RACE — вся лента одним цветом (`ledstrip_race_color`, BLACK = по частоте VTX), BEACON — мигание 2 раза в секунду по умолчанию. В RACE/BEACON активный failsafe и режим BEEPER включают мигание 4 раза в секунду. С пульта — функция 30 в `adjrange`.

title: Таймер MCU (группа выходов)
summary: Аппаратный счётчик STM32/AT32 (TIMx) с общими предделителем и периодом и до 4 каналов на ножках. Все выходы одного таймера работают на одной частоте и в одном протоколе: серва 50 Гц и DShot на одном таймере несовместимы. Карта — timer show, timer <pin> list.

title: SERVO_TILT
summary: Фича Betaflight: две сервы подвеса (тангаж, крен) и режим CAMSTAB. В CAMSTAB импульс = middle + rate·угол_в_десятых_градуса/50, то есть rate/5 мкс на градус наклона рамы.

title: Channel forwarding
summary: Фича Betaflight CHANNEL_FORWARDING: AUX-каналы приёмника, начиная с channel_forwarding_start, выводятся на оставшиеся выходы серв как есть, без ограничения min/max команды servo.

title: TTFF (холодный, тёплый, горячий старт)
summary: Время до первого фикса GNSS. Холодный — без эфемерид и времени (u-blox M8/M10: 26–29 с), тёплый — эфемериды устарели (> 4 ч), горячий — свежие эфемериды в BBR при живом V_BCKP (1 с).

title: PDOP
summary: Множитель ошибки 3D-позиции GNSS от геометрии спутников. Betaflight 4.5 показывает и использует именно PDOP (не HDOP): около 1.0 — хорошо.

title: gpspassthrough
summary: Команда CLI Betaflight: прямой мост USB ↔ UART GPS до перезагрузки, чтобы u-center читал и настраивал модуль через полётник.

title: Turtle mode (crash flip)
summary: Режим Betaflight FLIP OVER AFTER CRASH (aux id 35): при арме с включённым режимом FC шлёт ESC DShot-команду 21 (реверс), и стик крутит назад моторы одной стороны, чтобы перевернуть аппарат со спины. Только DShot; выход — дизарм, тумблер выкл., новый арм.

title: Dynamic idle
summary: Регулятор Betaflight, который по eRPM двунаправленного DShot держит самый медленный мотор не ниже dyn_idle_min_rpm × 100 об/мин, поднимая нижнюю границу всех моторов (до 15 %, на земле до 5 %). При нём dshot_idle_value игнорируется; без телеметрии молча выключен.

title: Launch control
summary: Режим Betaflight для гоночного старта (aux id 49): после арма в ACRO аппарат держит наклон, заданный стиком, I-членом с коэффициентом launch_control_gain, пока газ не превысит launch_trigger_throttle_percent (20 %).

title: Acro (Rate mode)
summary: Режим Betaflight без самовыравнивания (ANGLE и HORIZON выключены): стик задаёт угловую скорость, при отпущенном стике аппарат сохраняет текущий наклон.

title: USB Joystick (EdgeTX)
summary: Режим, в котором пульт на EdgeTX подключается к компьютеру по USB как HID-джойстик для симулятора: в Classic каналы 1–8 идут в оси, 9–32 — в кнопки.

title: Mode 2
summary: Раскладка стиков пульта: левый — газ и рыскание, правый — тангаж и крен; стик газа не подпружинен.

title: BNF / PNP / RTF
summary: Способы продажи аппарата. BNF (bind-and-fly) — собран и настроен, с приёмником: привязываешь свой пульт. PNP — без приёмника. RTF — набор с пультом, очками и зарядкой; пульт и очки такого набора обычно не годятся для следующего аппарата.

title: Гимбал на датчике Холла
summary: Узел стика пульта, где положение измеряет бесконтактный магнитный датчик вместо потенциометра со щёткой: не изнашивается, меньше дрожание сигнала в центре.

title: Мультипротокольный модуль (4-in-1, MPM)
summary: Радиомодуль пульта с четырьмя чипами (CC2500, NRF24L01, A7105, CYRF6936) под прошивкой MULTI-Module: FrSky, FlySky, Spektrum DSM и другие старые протоколы. ExpressLRS не поддерживает.

title: Вуп (whoop)
summary: Микрокоптер 65–85 мм с кольцевой защитой винтов, обычно на одной банке (1S): 15–25 г без батареи, моторы 0702–0802 на 22 000–30 000 KV, 3–7 минут полёта. Основная платформа для полётов в помещении и тренировки.

title: AIO 5-в-1
summary: Плата микроаппарата, объединяющая полётник, четыре ESC, приёмник и аналоговый VTX. Весит 3–5 г; расплата — мало свободных UART, часто нет флеш-памяти под Blackbox, отказ одного узла означает замену всей платы.

title: SPI-приёмник ELRS
summary: Радиочип ELRS, распаянный на плате полётника и подключённый по SPI, без своего MCU и своей прошивки: протокол исполняет Betaflight. В 2025.12 это ELRS 3 (OTA-версия 3), с передатчиком на 4.x не связывается; в 2026.6 есть опция сборки ELRSV4.

title: Logical switch (EdgeTX)
summary: Виртуальный тумблер пульта L01…L64: условие над источниками (a<x, AND, Sticky, Edge) с задержкой и AND-тумблером; на сенсоре телеметрии ложен, пока телеметрии нет.

title: Special function (EdgeTX)
summary: Действие пульта по тумблеру или логическому переключателю: Play Value, Play Track, SD Logs, Override, Vario, Screenshot и др.; до 64 на модель плюс глобальные.

title: Receiver No. (EdgeTX)
summary: Номер модели 0–63, который пульт сообщает RF-модулю; у ExpressLRS используется функцией Model Match, копия модели наследует номер оригинала.

title: osd_video_system (INAV)
summary: Настройка INAV, которая задаёт сетку символов OSD и способ вывода: AUTO/PAL/NTSC — аналог (30×16 или 30×13), HDZERO — 50×18, AVATAR, BFHDCOMPAT и DJI_NATIVE — 53×20, DJIWTF — 60×22, BF43COMPAT — 30×16. В отличие от Betaflight, очки сетку не сообщают: неверное значение — элементы у края не видны.

title: Раскладка OSD (osd_layout)
summary: Один из четырёх наборов позиций элементов OSD в INAV (0 — основной, 1–3 — альтернативные, включаются режимами OSD ALT 1–3 или операцией 32 программного фреймворка). Строка CLI: osd_layout <раскладка> <элемент> <столбец> <строка> <V|H>; внутри хранится слово x | y << 6 | 0x2000.

title: Свой элемент OSD (osd_custom_elements)
summary: Элемент OSD INAV, собранный пользователем из трёх частей (текст до 15 символов, значок, число из GVAR или логического условия) с условием видимости. В INAV 8–9 их восемь, номера в раскладке 147–149 и 154–158.

title: Профиль миксера (mixer profile)
summary: Набор INAV из типа платформы, таблиц mmix и smix и настроек перехода. Профилей два (на F411 один); режим MIXER PROFILE 2 переключает их в полёте, mixer_control_profile_linking привязывает к ним control-профили. Основа VTOL в INAV.

title: Переходное смешивание (MIXER TRANSITION)
summary: Режим INAV для разгона VTOL перед сменой профиля: вход 38 правил smix становится 500, а моторы со значением throttle от −1.05 до −2.0 в mmix выдают −throttle × 1000 мкс независимо от стика. Не работает в режимах навигации, кроме ALTHOLD.

title: Флапероны
summary: Элероны, которые одновременно работают как закрылки: оба отклоняются вниз на общий угол поверх команды крена. В INAV — has_flaps = ON, режим FLAPERON и вход 14 в smix со значением flaperon_throw_offset.

title: Бэкенд OSD (OSD_TYPE)
summary: Способ, которым ArduPilot выводит OSD: 1 — чип MAX7456 рисует в аналоговом видео, 5 — MSP DisplayPort (клетки рисуют очки), 3 — MSP-телеметрия для старых DJI, 2 — окно SITL, 4 — без вывода. Второй одновременный бэкенд задаёт OSD_TYPE2.

title: OSDn_TXT_RES
summary: Сетка символов экрана n в ArduPilot при MSP DisplayPort: 0 — 30×16, 1 — 50×18, 2 — 60×22. Задаётся на каждый экран; координаты элементов при смене сетки не пересчитываются.

title: Пит-режим (pit mode)
summary: Режим минимальной мощности видеопередатчика для настройки на земле рядом с другими пилотами. В ArduPilot — бит 0 VTX_OPTIONS; биты 1 и 2 снимают его при арме и возвращают при дизарме.

title: Flight termination (PX4)
summary: Необратимое действие failsafe в PX4: выходы переводятся в failsafe-значения (PWM_MAIN_FAILn), парашюту отправляется команда раскрытия; снимается только перезагрузкой. От failure detector разрешается записью CBRK_FLIGHTTERM = 0.

title: Circuit breaker (CBRK_*)
summary: Параметр PX4, отключающий проверку или защиту только при записи точного числа-ключа (например CBRK_IO_SAFETY = 22027); защита от случайного отключения.

title: Rally point (safe point)
summary: Запасная точка посадки, заданная в плане полёта; режим Return в PX4 выбирает ближайшую из разрешённых RTL_TYPE точек — дом, rally point или начало посадочной схемы миссии.

title: IOMCU
summary: Второй микроконтроллер на платах семейства Pixhawk и Cube: обслуживает выходы MAIN 1–8, вход приёмника и кнопку безопасности. В ArduPilot его группы выходов фиксированы (1–2, 3–4, 5–8), DShot на них включается параметром BRD_IO_DSHOT, а BLHeli passthrough не работает.

title: EDT (Extended DShot Telemetry)
summary: Расширение двунаправленного DShot: кроме оборотов ESC передаёт по сигнальному проводу температуру, напряжение, ток и показатель нагрузки. В ArduPilot включается значениями 3 и 4 параметра SERVO_DSHOT_ESC и пишется в лог сообщением EDT2; требует прошивки ESC с поддержкой EDT.

title: RELAYn_PIN
summary: Номер ножки GPIO, которой управляет реле n в ArduPilot (до 4.5 — RELAY_PIN, RELAY_PIN2…). Номер берётся из GPIO(g) в hwdef платы; если ножка принадлежит PWM-выходу, этому выходу нужно задать SERVOn_FUNCTION = -1.

title: Aux function (RCx_OPTION)
summary: Действие, привязанное к каналу пульта в ArduPilot параметром RCx_OPTION: режим, арм, реле, остановка моторов и так далее. Канал читается как трёхпозиционный тумблер (LOW ниже 1200 мкс, HIGH выше 1800 мкс), функция вызывается по изменению положения после задержки 200 мс и пишется в лог сообщением AUXF.

title: Debounce (подавление дребезга)
summary: Задержка, в течение которой новое положение переключателя должно оставаться неизменным, прежде чем система на него отреагирует. В ArduPilot для aux-каналов и канала режимов — 200 мс (SWITCH_DEBOUNCE_TIME_MS); более короткий импульс не исполняется.

title: Transmitter tuning (TUNE)
summary: Подстройка одного параметра ArduCopter крутилкой пульта в полёте: канал с RCx_OPTION = 219, номер параметра в TUNE, значения на краях хода в TUNE_MIN и TUNE_MAX. Значение линейно зависит от положения крутилки, пишется только в оперативную память и в лог PTUN; в Plane ту же задачу решают параметры TUNE_CHAN и TUNE_PARAM.

title: Функция выхода (PX4, `PWM_*_FUNCn`)
summary: Номер, который связывает физический выход с источником значения: 101–112 Motor, 201–208 Servo, 301–306 Peripheral via Actuator Set, 400 Landing Gear, 401 Parachute, 407–412 RC AUX, 430 Gripper, 2000 Camera Trigger. Список — output_functions.yaml; значение в микросекунды переводит mixer_module по MIN/MAX/CENT/REV.

title: `PWM_AUX_REV` (маска реверса)
summary: Битовая маска PX4: бит n−1 меняет знак нормированного значения выхода n до пересчёта в микросекунды, диапазон зеркалится вокруг (MIN + MAX)/2 или CENT. Так механику сервы подгоняют под правило «положительная команда — задняя кромка вверх», не трогая знаки CA_SV_CSn_TRQ_*.

title: `PWM_AUX_CENTn` (центр сервы, PX4 1.17)
summary: Нейтраль PWM-сервы в микросекундах на выходе FMU; −1 — прямая от MIN до MAX. Если задан, значение −1…0 отображается на MIN…CENT, 0…+1 — на CENT…MAX, а прошивка обнуляет CA_SV_CSn_TRIM. Перенос: CENT = MIN + (MAX − MIN)/2 · (1 + TRIM).

id: g:Пакетный режим CLI (batch start / batch end)
title: Пакетный режим CLI (batch start / batch end)
summary: Режим CLI INAV, в котором считаются ошибки вставляемых строк: `diff` и `dump` начинают вывод с `batch start`, и при хотя бы одной строке `### ERROR` первая `save` не записывает конфигурацию, а печатает число ошибок. Защищает от сохранения наполовину применённого файла.

title: Control-профиль (control_profile)
summary: Один из трёх наборов PID, навигационных коэффициентов, рейтов, TPA и EZ Tune в INAV (126 настроек в 9.1.0).
